  differing cells ARE the structure's footprint whatever wrote them — and it found four mechanisms
  where nobody was looking for one.
  **1. `structure_block` reached the world.** `02e_templates.js` built exactly three palette flags
  (`structure_void`, `jigsaw`, `air`/`cave_air`) and `JG.writePiece` acted on those three. Vanilla
  places every one of these templates through `BlockIgnoreProcessor.STRUCTURE_BLOCK`, which drops
  `minecraft:structure_block` from the palette so nothing is written at that cell — the same "leave
  what is there" `structure_void` already meant here. **196 markers across 97 of the 866 packed
  templates** (underwater_ruin 98, shipwreck 44, woodland_mansion 34, end_city 19, igloo 1); every
  one that generated was a real, visible debug block in a wall. Now **0**, asserted hard, and the
  audit's register entry is DELETED rather than left standing at zero — D-139's rule, and
  `structaudit` §7 fails if you forget it.
  **2, 3, 4. The sea.** `SU.writeBeard`'s SHAVE branch cleared every cell from `base+1` to `topY`
  whatever was in it, including water — *four lines below a FILL branch that already carries
  `if (cur !== 0 && waterIn[cur]) break;  // never drain an ocean`*. `JG.writePiece` wrote a
  template's own air straight over the sea, where vanilla places every structure with `keepLiquids`
  — which is precisely why an ocean ruin is FULL of water instead of sitting in a bubble.
  `04s_struct_mineshaft.js`'s `carve` hollowed water out with no liquid test at all.
  **Measured**: structure-written air standing against water **1.62% -> 0.41%** of structure air,
  against a natural-terrain baseline of 0.02% in the same windows — 80x down to 20x.
  ocean_ruin_cold 1,320 -> 233, ruined_portal_ocean 811 -> 100, village_plains 281 -> 130.
  ⚠ **What is NOT done, named rather than faked.** Vanilla's mineshaft rule is not "flood the
  corridor", it is `if (this.edgesLiquid(box)) return;` — the corridor is never built. That test
  reads the blocks around a box that spans chunks, and a read outside the target chunk returns -1
  here, so porting it directly would make a piece's existence depend on which chunk is being filled
  and TEAR the structure — D-185 is exactly that invariant. So MC-Lite floods a corridor vanilla
  would not have built: a visible deviation, registered in `structaudit`'s open defects, and no
  longer an air bubble under the sea. A pure-position form of the gate is the work that closes it.
  ⚠ **And the meta-checks could not see the tool that found all this.** `doccheck` §4 and
  `gatecheck` §2 both matched `/check.mjs$/`, so `structaudit.mjs` was listed in `suite.mjs`,
  carried 25 deliberate breaks, and was invisible to both "every check is in the suite" and "every
  check can fail". Both now match `/(check|audit).mjs$/`.

- **D-215** ⚠ **THE PLAINS THAT WAS 58% SAND IS NOT A SURFACE-RULE BUG. IT IS THREE UNGATED
  DISKS PER CHUNK.** `featcheck` §4b's audit found a 49-chunk all-`minecraft:plains` sample whose
  top surface was 51.7% sand against 37.5% grass_block, and named it a surface rule "laying beach
  across an inland biome". It is not. **The surface rules are innocent, and the measurement that
  says so is one flag**: regenerate the SAME 7x7 box at seed 1337, climate vanilla, with
  `features:false, structures:false, caves:false, carvers:false` and the box is **99.2%
  grass_block, 0.8% dirt and 0.0% sand**. Turning the three soft disks off one at a time on a
  fully decorated world isolates it further — with `disk_sand` disabled the box is 80.9%
  grass_block and 16.6% gravel; with `disk_sand`, `disk_gravel` and `disk_clay` all disabled it is
  **97.2% grass_block**. Every grain of that sand is `minecraft:disk_sand`.
  **What was ruled out, and how.** The condition stack in `04h_surface.js` evaluating `water` or
  `above_preliminary_surface` against the wrong y or the wrong sea level — ruled out: with features
  off the same rules over 331,776 columns of 29 biomes produce no block any biome is not entitled
  to (`surfcheck` §8). A biome lookup disagreeing between the surface pass and everything else, the
  classic quart-versus-block mistake — ruled out: `vanillacheck` §1 puts MC-Lite's biome at
  **99.943%** of the real game's on non-cave quart cells, and the sandy columns are `plains` in
  both engines. A noise-driven sand band applied without its biome condition — ruled out by walking
  `noise_settings/overworld.json` independently of the compiled tree: `sand` and `sandstone` appear
  under a `biome` condition naming **six** biomes (beach, snowy_beach, desert, warm_ocean,
  lukewarm_ocean, deep_lukewarm_ocean) and under no other rule, gated or ungated, anywhere in the
  tree. Only six blocks are ungated at all — bedrock, deepslate, dirt, grass_block, gravel, stone.
  The beach/shore window — ruled out with the rest of the tree by the same features-off table.
  **The cause, and it is vanilla's own gate that is missing.** In 1.18.2 `disk_sand`,
  `disk_gravel` and `disk_clay` are in the UNDERGROUND_ORES step of nearly every overworld biome —
  plains included — placed by `count 3 / in_square / heightmap OCEAN_FLOOR_WG / biome`, with no
  fluid predicate in the JSON. MC-Lite runs exactly that chain and `placeDisk` in
  `src/04j_features.js` is a faithful port of `DiskFeature`'s cylinder, so with a mean radius of 4
  and three attempts a chunk the disks cover ~60% of it. Vanilla's do not, because vanilla's disk
  is anchored to WATER — the restriction 1.19 later moved out of the feature's Java and into the
  placed feature's JSON as `block_predicate_filter { matching_fluids: water }`.
  **The referee is the real game, not the reading.** Measured over the 1.18.2 golden pregen (seed
  1337, `tools/vanillacheck.mjs`'s own world), 556,086 land columns in the twenty-three grass-family
  biomes: **4,049 are topped with sand (0.73%) and 77.1% of those lie within 6 blocks of water** —
  6 being `disk_sand`'s maximum radius. Gravel: 85.3% within 6. Clay: **91.9% within 6, and 88% at
  distance 1**. Grass_block, by contrast, is 17.5% within 6. Vanilla's plains is 82% grass_block
  and 3.6% sand; MC-Lite's is 44% sand (`vanillacheck` §3, 240 chunks).
  ⚠ **THE FIX IS NOT WRITTEN AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE'S OWNER'S HANDS.** The gate belongs in
  `src/04j_features.js` — the `disk` generator must refuse a placement whose `OCEAN_FLOOR_WG`
  origin cell does not hold water, which is one condition at the top of `placeDisk` — and that file
  was open in another session's uncommitted working tree when this was diagnosed. Editing it would
  have shipped a change inside somebody else's diff. Named here with the measurement that closes
  it rather than half-done. It is worth doing: `vanillacheck` §3's `surfLedger.length <= 3` fence
  is **already red at HEAD** with nine biomes disagreeing, all of them the same disks, and §6's
  decoration ratios move with it.
  **What DID land is the check that had never existed.** `surfcheck` §8 generates 1,296 chunks
  across four seeds and four places and asserts that the top block of every column is one vanilla's
  own surface rules are allowed to place in THAT column's biome. The allowed set is built by a
  second, dumber walk of `noise_settings/overworld.json` that carries the intersection of enclosing
  `biome` conditions down to each `block` rule — never by asking `Surface` what it compiled, which
  is the D-152/D-178/D-194 mistake. It audits the UNDECORATED world on purpose: vanilla's own
  features legitimately put sand on a plains, so containment over a decorated world would be
  asserting something false about vanilla too. §8b prints the decorated table beside vanilla's
  0.7% every run and asserts nothing on it, because the check that owns that comparison is
  `vanillacheck` §3, which has the real game to compare against. Two anti-vacuity breaks (D-30):
  a rule tree that puts sand under every biome, which the containment audit must catch, and a
  widened `biome_is` on the desert sand rule, which the allowed-set walker must follow — the
  second is what stops §8 degenerating into a hard-coded list of block names.

- **D-213** ⚠ **EVERY TREE IN THE WORLD WAS BUILT BY ONE CHUNK AND THROWN AWAY BY THE OTHER EIGHT.**
  Dan, playing at medium, twice in two sessions: *"some trees have half their leaves cut off."* The
  first report was D-178, a mesher bug, and that fix is real — `coherecheck` §4 now measures the
  fancy leaf path on real canopies and gets 14,586 of 14,586 faces. This is the second half of the
  same sentence and it is in worldgen.
  **The mechanism.** `runInline` in `src/04j_features.js` ran an inline placed feature's
  `block_predicate_filter` against `getBlock(SB, cx, cz, …)` at the feature's ORIGIN, and a read
  outside the target chunk returns -1, on which it did `return 0`. That does not defer the
  judgement to the chunk that owns the origin — it **cancels the build**. Every vanilla tree
  reached through a `random_selector` (`trees_plains`, `trees_savanna`, `trees_birch`,
  `trees_jungle`, `trees_grove`, …) carries exactly such a filter on its options, so the 3x3
  architecture re-ran the placement in all nine targets exactly as designed and eight of them threw
  it away before writing a block. The trunk and canopy stopped flush against the chunk boundary.
  ⚠ It is precisely the failure `src/04k_feat_trees.js`'s own header forbids — *"GLOBAL, one read
  deciding many cells … NOT safe: the answer differs per target"*. The tree file obeys that rule
  line by line; the file one level up broke it for every tree at once.
  **The one-liner is the diagnosis, not the fix.** Turning `return 0` into `continue` makes a
  neighbour build a tree the owning chunk refused: seed 4242's orphaned-leaf rate goes 0.03% to
  **1.41%**. Two chunks answering different questions is the same bug wearing the other shoe.
  **The rule, and it is D-134's, one question further on.** D-134 settled what world a PLACEMENT
  may ask about — `Column.height`, the terrain before any feature ran — because a source chunk
  computes its placements without generating a block. `Features.terrainAt(x,y,z)` is that same
  world asked for a BLOCK rather than a height: the terrain fill plus Mojang's surface rules,
  before the carvers and before every feature, memoised by column. It is a pure function of
  position, so the nine targets reach the same verdict by construction. Deliberately not the carved
  world: `Caves.carve` is a point query 04b's header says the chunk path is not obliged to agree
  with, and a carver is a 240-block random walk no point query can answer — which is exactly the
  approximation `04k`'s `maxFreeHeight` already makes for this same question. One approximation,
  now named in both files, instead of two.
  **Which guard reads which world** is `columnLocal(gen)`, 04k's PER-CELL / GLOBAL line moved up a
  file. A `simple_block` or a `block_column` writes only inside the origin's own column, so a
  target that does not hold that column receives nothing from it either way: the live target blocks
  are both safe and faithful there, and that path is unchanged. Everything else builds outward, one
  read deciding cells in chunks that would read differently, and is judged by `terrainAt`. The
  default is **false** — including every generator a W8c/W8d module registers — because guessing
  "local" wrong reintroduces the seam and guessing "global" wrong costs one memoised column.
  **`offset` was being dropped, and it is part of the predicate.** Vanilla's `BlockPredicate`
  carries a relative offset; `compilePredicate` ignored it, which turned `patch_berry_bush`'s
  `all_of[air here, grass_block below]` into "air and grass_block in the same cell" — false in
  every world. Sweet berry bushes, pumpkins, melons, jungle grass, sugar cane and both of the
  grove's trees had never generated. Honoured now, through the same block source the rest of the
  guard reads, so a live offset read that leaves the target chunk falls through to `terrainAt`
  rather than returning -1 and inventing a new seam one cell wide.
  **Measured**, 81 chunks, shipped versus fixed: seed 777777 leaves 8,117 → **8,970** (+10.5%),
  `acacia_leaves` 2,297 → **2,948** (+28.3%), logs 932 → 961; seed 1337 leaves 24,248 → 24,472,
  `acacia_leaves` 1,053 → 1,256; seed 4242 leaves 79,827 → **108,219**, logs 19,584 → 38,090.
  Distinct trees that built anything at 4242: 2,648 → 3,031, and blocks per tree 63.7 → **84.5** —
  a tree was losing a third of itself. `coherecheck` §3, the check this bug was failing on `main`:
  crossing rate 5.34% against 6.42% at the same grid's fifteen other offsets, **t = -4.35**;
  fixed, 8.22% against 8.00%, **t = +0.83**, with the bound untouched. Orphaned leaves fall as
  well — seed 4242 18 → 1, seed 777777 43 → 0 — because a canopy whose trunk was in the next chunk
  now has its trunk. `floatcheck` is unmoved: 0 unsupported blocks before and after on all four
  seeds. Cost: **+0.23 ms a chunk**, 14.52 → 14.75 (gencheck, three runs each).
  **Why `parcheck` did not catch a bug this size, and what it does now.** It could not: sections
  1-5 ask whether `genColumn(cx,cz)` gives the same bytes on every instance and in every arrival
  order, and it did — `genColumn` is self-contained, so the clipping was perfectly deterministic
  and every instance committed it identically. The invariant actually broken was never stated: a
  placement offered to nine targets must be JUDGED the same by all nine. `parcheck` §6 states it —
  seven guarded trees at 256 positions on a coastline chunk chosen by property, nine verdicts each,
  0 split, with both answers required to be a hundred strong so agreement on a constant cannot
  pass for agreement. `featcheck` §4c is the other half and needs no statistics at all: a tree
  standing hard against a chunk boundary must write MORE blocks over the 3x3 than its own chunk
  receives, and under the bug the two numbers were equal for every tree at every residue.
  featcheck had never counted a log or a leaf; no threshold in it was calibrated on the clipped
  world, because none of them looked at a tree.
  ⚠ **WHAT THIS EXPOSES AND DOES NOT FIX.** `vanillacheck` §6 now reads `jungle_log` at **10.31x**
  the real game (was 4.59x) and flags it as a density outlier; `oak_leaves` 1.74x → 2.11x, `vine`
  1.79x → 3.03x, `spruce_leaves` 0.20x → **1.32x** (the grove's trees, which the dropped `offset`
  had switched off entirely). None of that is caused here — it is D-134's standing price, already
  written into that section's own comment as "2-4x heavy": vanilla's `getMaxFreeTreeHeight` reads
  the LIVE world, so most of a jungle's fifty attempts a chunk fail against trees already standing,
  while MC-Lite's pure `maxFreeHeight` sees only terrain and they all succeed. The clipping was
  masking it by discarding a third of every tree. Not papered over: the bound is not widened, no
  restriction vanilla does not have is invented to hit a number, and `vanillacheck.mjs` is not
  touched. The jungle's density is the next thing to look at, and it is now visible.

- **D-214** ⚠ **THE TINT MAP WAS WRITTEN BETWEEN FRAMES AND UPLOADED INSIDE ONE, AND THE TWO
  CLOCKS DISAGREED FOR AS LONG AS THE WORLD WAS STREAMING.** `titlecheck` passed at the Celeron
  preset and failed at both of the presets Dan plays at: *"the map is at version 122 but the GPU
  has 121"* at medium, and at high it was two behind. D-196's hook is what made it visible; the
  seam had been measured at render distance 4 for five sessions.
  **The mechanism, measured rather than guessed.** `NS.Tint.fillChunk` is called from
  `World.installChunk`, which runs in the promise that settles when a worker hands a generated
  chunk back — a microtask checkpoint BETWEEN frames, at a moment no part of `Main.loop` chose.
  The upload was `L.syncTint`, called only from the backend's `beginFrame`. So the GPU held
  whatever the map looked like when the last frame started, and everything written since was
  owed. Instrumented in headless Chromium at medium: **1 to 6 versions behind at every sample,
  a median staleness of 54-244 ms, which is one frame**; the counter caught up only in the gaps
  between chunk arrivals, and at render distance 4 those gaps are most of the time, which is
  exactly why the check passed there. It is not a per-frame upload budget: `uploadBytesPerFrame`
  and `flushUploads` never touch this texture.
  **What was NOT wrong, and it matters.** The world was never drawn in the wrong colours. A
  shadow copy of the last bytes uploaded, audited against every chunk holding geometry on the
  GPU, gave **0 mis-coloured drawn chunks in every sample**, through four re-anchors and a
  1,200-block flight — because a chunk's colours are written when it is GENERATED and its
  geometry arrives later still, so the tint always leads the mesh. The stale versions were
  always chunks with nothing on screen yet. The assertion was right to fail and wrong about why.
  **What WAS wrong, and is the reason to fix it rather than relax the assertion.** `syncTint`
  re-uploaded the WHOLE 768 KB map on every frame in which any chunk landed. Its own comment
  justified that with "it changes a handful of times a second while chunks stream in" — true at
  render distance 4, false at 12 and 16, where a chunk arrives on nearly every frame. That is
  ~46 MB/s of texture traffic on the 2200G for a map of which sixteen texels moved.
  **Measured after the fix**, same harness, 10 s of streaming at medium (rd 12, 144 chunks):
  49 uploads costing **9,408 bytes in total**, and the map never once fell behind — worst lag 0
  and mean lag 0 over twenty samples, against 1-6 before. Those same 49 changes under the old
  path were 13 whole-map uploads (one per frame in which any of them landed) = 10.2 MB, and on
  a machine drawing 60 frames a second rather than 13 it is 768 KB on nearly every frame.
  **The fix: the write drives the upload.** `06b_tintmap.js` keeps a DIRTY RECTANGLE of the
  texels changed since the last upload and a `sink` — the live backend's uploader, registered
  when its texture is created, so F9 hands it over. `flush()` runs the sink the moment the bytes
  change; `held` batches a refill's two thousand writes into one upload, and a re-anchor into
  two (the clear, then the refill). Both backends upload only the rectangle, across all three
  layers, addressed as an offset into the plane-major bytes — WebGL2 with UNPACK_SKIP_PIXELS /
  SKIP_ROWS / ROW_LENGTH / IMAGE_HEIGHT put back afterwards because the atlas mips share that
  context, WebGPU with a `writeTexture` dataLayout offset and `rowsPerImage` at the full width.
  One arriving chunk now costs a 4x4x3 sub-box instead of the map. Both still call their own
  uploader from `beginFrame`; that is now a safety net for the first frame, a restored context
  and a backend swapped under F9, not the mechanism.
  **What proves it.** `tintcheck` §8 is new and does not trust the marks: it diffs the map's
  bytes before and after a write and requires every texel that MOVED to be inside the rectangle
  that was uploaded, and requires the rectangle not to have grown to the whole map to be safe.
  It also walks 4,000 blocks writing a chunk under the walker at every step and asserts
  `uploaded === version` after every one of the 501 steps, not merely at the end. Three
  anti-vacuity breaks: a rectangle shrunk by one texel column (the diff must see the four
  texels left outside), a refill with the batching removed (the sink count must tell 1 from
  1,000), and — the bug itself rebuilt — a sink that only runs on a fake frame tick, which must
  drive the walk red. `titlecheck` now RAISES the preset to medium for its tint section if the
  machine detected something weaker, refuses to run below render distance 12, and adds the
  decisive probe: `Main.stop()`, write to the map, and require the GPU to be current with zero
  frames and zero draws in between. Its own anti-vacuity break nulls the sink and requires that
  probe to go red. 75,351 assertions in tintcheck (12 breaks), 87 in titlecheck (5 breaks).
  ⚠ **Two things this exposed and did not fix**, both of them D-196's shape rather than this
  bug's: at `MCLITE_PRESET=medium`, `palettecheck` §2 fails with *"only 37 pixels changed when
  leaves were switched to fast — the camera is not looking at any"* (its camera frames no
  leaves at render distance 12, so the saturation allowance below it is derived from noise),
  and `soakcheck` reports the light queue holding a non-zero size across one sample. Both pass
  at Celeron and neither is in this stage's files. They are the next things to look at.

- **D-216** ⚠⚠ **THE VILLAGE HOUSES WERE STANDING OVER A ONE-BLOCK VOID BECAUSE
  `legacy_single_pool_element` WAS INVERTED, AND THE CHECK THAT SAID OTHERWISE WAS MEASURING
  BOXES.** Three defects, one symptom, and the third only became visible once the first two were
  gone.
  **1. THE AIR RULE WAS THE WRONG WAY ROUND.** `04t_jigsaw.js` has said since W15 that
  *"the legacy form writes its air blocks, the plain form skips them"*. It is the other way round:
  vanilla's `LegacySinglePoolElement.getSettings` pops `BlockIgnoreProcessor.STRUCTURE_BLOCK` and
  adds `STRUCTURE_AND_AIR`, so a LEGACY template's air is dropped before it reaches the world and
  a PLAIN one's is written. 601 of the 836 pool elements are legacy — every village and pillager
  outpost piece — and all 60 `template_pool` files that use `single_pool_element` are under
  `bastion/`, which an overworld generator never places. So MC-Lite was writing air for everything
  that generates and skipping it for the one family that does not exist here.
  ⚠ **THE PROOF IS THE REAL GAME (D-199's referee), NOT A READING OF THE TWO NAMES.** The golden
  1.18.2 pregen at seed 1337 contains a vanilla snowy village at chunk (−503, 92).
  `village/snowy/streets/straight_02` is 16×2×16 whose layer 0 is 48 `dirt_path` and **208 AIR**
  and whose layer 1 is 253 AIR. In the generated world that road steps **93 → 94 → 95** down the
  slope — a per-column drape, plainly — and the ground on both shoulders is intact `grass_block`
  **at the same Y as the road**. If the legacy form wrote its air, every shoulder of every village
  road in the game would be one block lower than the road it flanks. It is not, anywhere.
  **What the inversion cost:** a street tile is a `terrain_matching` piece, so it sits at the
  ground height of its own connector, and its 208 air cells replaced the surface block that the
  rigid house sharing that square was standing on. Seed 1337, plains village at chunk (−79, 90):
  house floor cobblestone at y 68, **AIR at y 67** where the control world has grass_block.
  **2. THE PLINTH REACHED THE BOX FLOOR, NOT THE PIECE'S UNDERSIDE.** `SU.beardPiece` was given
  `box.y0`. A template whose bottom layer is `structure_void` stands a block higher than its box:
  `village/desert/houses/desert_farm_2` is 7×7×10 whose layer 0 is 67 void cells and three
  smooth_sandstone, with the farm — 24 farmland, 29 sandstone stairs — in layer 1. Its plinth
  stopped two blocks under the crop and **100 of one desert village's 1,009 floor cells were over
  air for that reason alone**. `JG.groundLy(tpl)` derives the underside: the lowest layer the
  template fills in at least a quarter of the columns it occupies. ⚠ Both cheap answers are wrong
  — "the lowest layer with anything solid in it" is one column of a foundation pillar, and "each
  column's own lowest solid cell" makes a roof eave a floor.
  **3. AND THEN THE PER-COLUMN DRAPE CAME BACK.** `Projection.TERRAIN_MATCHING` carries exactly
  one processor in vanilla, `GravityProcessor(WORLD_SURFACE_WG, -1)`, which moves every block to
  `getHeight(x, z) - 1 + localY` — `Column.height(x, z) + localY` here, one column at a time.
  Session 5 removed it and made the piece rigid at write time, on the evidence that draping had
  dug holes under 62 of a desert village's 467 house floors. That diagnosis was one line off: the
  holes were the street's own AIR, and making the piece rigid only stopped the air landing in the
  same place every time. `JG.drapeAt` is the drape, memoised per (seed, chunk); it is a PURE
  FUNCTION OF (x, z), so it cannot tear a structure across a chunk seam (D-185). The assembly-time
  vertical fit in `tryAttach` STAYS — vanilla does that too, in `JigsawPlacement`, and it is what
  decides which piece attaches where.
  **MEASURED, `structaudit` §1, default sample, before → after** (components / cells / largest
  interior component): village_plains **35 / 3,111 / 254 → 6 / 24 / 3**; village_snowy
  **22 / 502 / 222 → 12 / 48 / 9**; pillager_outpost **139 / 1,417 / 48 → 8 / 20 / 0**;
  village_savanna 8 / 37 / 10 → 6 / 38 / 10; village_desert 1 / 12 / 12 → 2 / 14 / 12.
  ⚠ village_taiga's **74 / 1,161 / 141 did not move, and was never the village**: those are moss
  blocks at y = −1 in a lush cave a MINESHAFT opened under the same three-chunk window. §1 now
  prints an `own` column — components with a cell inside the sampled start's own bounding box —
  and village_taiga's own share is **7 components / 10 cells**. Blaming a neighbour's structure on
  this family is the mis-attribution §3 already refuses to make for technical blocks.
  **4. THE CHECK THAT SAID 97.5% WAS MEASURING BOXES.** `structcheck` §9 scored a floor column
  supported when the block under it was opaque **OR** when `inAnother(x, p.y0 − 1, z, …)` said
  that cell lay inside a DIFFERENT piece's bounding box. A street's box is 13×2×11 of which 110 of
  the 143 ground cells are not road, so a house standing on a street square scored as supported
  while standing on nothing — and the comment above it claimed the hole had been closed by making
  `terrain_matching` pieces rigid, which it had not: the piece became rigid, its air did not become
  ground. It now derives each piece's base layer from the piece itself (template or hand-built cell
  list), maps it through the drape, and reads the generated chunk one block below. **Rigid pieces:
  2,742 of 2,742 supported, asserted as a ZERO rather than a band** — a building over a hole is
  not a cheaper silhouette. Draped pieces are counted separately and PRINTED: 2,069 of 2,099. §11
  breaks the new test three ways on the village it has just measured — the support taken away, the
  read moved to the wrong side of the floor, and the base-layer rule undone so the eaves come back.
  **WHAT IS STILL OPEN, AND REGISTERED RATHER THAN ASSERTED AWAY.** `structaudit` §1 gained `dug`:
  an ungrounded component whose underside rests on air the structure wrote where the control world
  has ground, attributed to the start's own box. No slope and no overhang produces it. It is not a
  global zero, so it is `REGISTER`'s third entry, `wrote-air-then-stood-on-it`, with two producers:
  (a) a draped street crossing a terrace a neighbouring house's beard shaved AFTER the drape was
  computed — village_plains 12, and vanilla has no such seam because its Beardifier is part of the
  NOISE, so `WORLD_SURFACE_WG` already contains the terrace where MC-Lite's beard is written
  afterwards (D-188); (b) a carver leaving its own furniture in the air it hollowed — mineshaft
  169, mineshaft_mesa 132, monument 16, which is the `edgesLiquid`-shaped gate D-212 already owes.
  ⚠ **The obvious fix for (a) was implemented, measured and reverted**: draping onto the WRITTEN
  world rather than the column function makes the answer depend on how much of the structure has
  been written by the time a piece's turn comes, and it took a desert village from 903 supported
  rigid floor cells to 901 by dropping the road out from under the house it was holding up. The
  numbers are in `JG.drapeAt`'s note so the next session does not spend an hour rediscovering them.
  ⚠ **And the ungrounded-component HISTOGRAM stays unbounded on purpose.** A balcony, a ledge, a
  hanging mineshaft support and a tree planted by a `feature_pool_element` are all ungrounded
  components and all correct. The number is a shape, not a defect count, and a threshold fitted to
  today's villages is D-152 with a percentage sign.

- **D-217** ⚠ **ONE LINE TOOK NINE BIOMES' SURFACES FROM WRONG TO RIGHT, AND IT IS NOT IN THE
  SURFACE RULES AT ALL.** D-215 diagnosed the sandy plains and deliberately did not fix it, because
  `src/04j_features.js` was carrying another session's uncommitted work at the time. This is that
  fix, plus a second bug in the same file found while measuring it.
  **1. A disk is anchored to water.** `disk_sand`, `disk_gravel` and `disk_clay` sit in the
  UNDERGROUND_ORES step of nearly every overworld biome with the chain `count 3 -> in_square ->
  heightmap OCEAN_FLOOR_WG -> biome` and **no fluid predicate in the JSON**, because in 1.18.2 the
  restriction lives inside `DiskFeature.place`, which returns immediately unless the origin cell
  holds water. 1.19 moved it into the data as `block_predicate_filter { matching_fluids: water }`,
  which is exactly why reading 1.18.2's placed-feature JSON makes it look unconditional. MC-Lite
  compiled the chain faithfully and had no gate, so three disks a chunk at a mean radius of 4
  repainted about 60% of every land biome.
  ⚠ **The gate is a PURE FUNCTION OF POSITION, and that is D-213's rule applied four hours after
  it was learned in this same file.** A `getBlock` at the origin is ONE READ DECIDING MANY CELLS:
  it returns −1 in the eight neighbouring targets, so the disk would be written by the chunk
  holding its origin and thrown away by the others — which is precisely how every tree in the world
  came to be sliced at the seam. The origin's y came from OCEAN_FLOOR_WG, which is
  `Column.height + 1`, and that cell holds water exactly when it is at or below the sea, so
  `y <= seaLevel` IS the water test and all nine targets compute it identically.
  **Measured against the real 1.18.2 world** (`vanillacheck` §3, the golden pregen's 240-chunk
  paired sample), agreement on the top block per biome, before → after:
  plains **41.5% → 93.9%**, snowy_plains 41.6% → 96.3%, jungle 47.4% → 95.9%,
  sparse_jungle 42.1% → 95.4%, birch_forest 52.5% → 96.9%, forest 65.4% → 95.9%,
  flower_forest 52.2% → 97.2%, old_growth_birch_forest 47.6% → 78.1%.
  **The ledger of disagreeing biomes went from NINE to ONE** — `frozen_ocean`, which is a different
  bug (MC-Lite freezes 48% of its surface where vanilla leaves water) and is still open.
  **2. `noise_based_count` conflated a wavelength with a scale.** Vanilla's
  `NoiseBasedCountPlacement.count` is
  `ceil((BIOME_INFO_NOISE.getValue(x / noise_factor, z / noise_factor, false) + noise_offset) * noise_to_count_ratio)`.
  Three fields, three jobs: `noise_factor` DIVIDES the coordinates, `noise_to_count_ratio`
  MULTIPLIES the result, and there is no ceiling. MC-Lite read the noise at a fixed wavelength,
  multiplied by the FACTOR instead of the RATIO, and then clamped the count to the ratio. `bamboo`
  is the only overworld user of the modifier and generated at **0.13x** the real game's density;
  it is **0.68x** now. Still short, and `vanillacheck` §6 keeps it in view.
  ⚠ **What this exposed rather than caused**, and it is the next job: with D-213's trees now whole
  and the predicates' `offset` honoured, the decoration ledger says MC-Lite plants about **twice**
  vanilla's leaves everywhere and **ten times** its jungle logs (43.4 a chunk against 4.30), with
  `moss_carpet` 4.7x and `cave_vines_plant` 4.2x. Trees and lush caves are over-generating, the
  numbers are now measurable against the real game, and nothing has been tuned to hide it.

- **D-218** **THE SUITE CAN BE RUN IN PIECES, BECAUSE ON THE MACHINE THIS PROJECT LIVES ON IT HAS TO
  BE.** Every remote shell call into Dan's box is capped at about 180 seconds and a background
  process does not survive the call (`bwrap --die-with-parent`, verified with a 25 s probe), while
  `--fast` is now past 200 s of work — `structcheck` alone is 59 s. On one night **three separate
  sessions hit that wall**, and all three did the same thing: ran the checks by hand and reported a
  list. That is how a stage gets quietly skipped, which is the failure `--fast`'s own summary line
  exists to prevent. `--only a,b,c`, `--from <id>` and `--to <id>` select stages in the suite's own
  order, so a full pass is two or three calls instead of one that cannot finish.
  ⚠ **A partial run says so, above the timing, in the place "0 stages failed" would otherwise be
  the last thing anybody reads**: `⚠ PARTIAL RUN — 3 of 64 stages selected. This is NOT a green
  suite.` The unselected stages also join the existing "DID NOT RUN" line. Same lesson as D-196's,
  one file down: a green line that does not say what it did not do is the same class of lie as a
  check with no anti-vacuity section.

## Session 6 — the golden referee, part 2: ice and ore

- **D-219** ⚠ **`Biome.FROZEN_TEMPERATURE_NOISE` IS `PerlinSimplexNoise(3456, [-2, -1, 0])`, AND
  MC-LITE HAD `[-3, -2, -1]`.** The frozen-ocean patchwork — vanilla's `TemperatureModifier.FROZEN`,
  which forces the temperature UP to 0.2 where two fixed-seed noises agree and so leaves the water
  open — was built on the wrong octave list from the day D-118 ported it. The list was written from
  memory; it is `ImmutableList.of(-2, -1, 0)` in `Biome.<clinit>`, read out of the 1.18.2 jar's
  constant pool and bytecode this session. The wrong list is wrong twice over: `PerlinSimplexNoise`
  takes `highestFreqInputFactor = 2^lastOctave`, so every octave was sampled at HALF the intended
  frequency, and because the set did not contain 0 the unconditionally-constructed first
  `SimplexNoise` was discarded instead of kept as level `j`, so all three levels came off the wrong
  draws of the legacy random as well.
  **Measured against the real 1.18.2 world at seed 1337** (`vanillacheck` §3, 240 chunks): MC-Lite
  froze 80% of a frozen ocean where the golden world freezes 47%, and `frozen_ocean` was the last
  biome on §3's disagreement ledger at **66.5%**. It is **87.7%** now, MC-Lite's dominant top block
  is water at 48% exactly as vanilla's is, and per column over 1,288 golden frozen-ocean water/ice
  columns the freeze RULE agrees **97.4%** of the time (it was 56.1%) with **zero** columns frozen
  that vanilla left open. `snowy_plains` (96.3%), `snowy_slopes` (88.9%), `grove` (97.3%) and
  `jagged_peaks` (81.9%) did not move; §3 now fences all five by name.
  ⚠ **The residual 12% in `frozen_ocean` is the ICEBERG, not the freeze**, and it is not tunable
  from this sample: the same 240 chunks put MC-Lite at **0.48x** vanilla's packed ice worldwide and
  **1.47x** inside those 448 columns. That is one berg's landfall, which §8 already drops on D-134's
  authority, so it is now named there rather than left looking like a surface-rule bug.
  ⚠ **The rule itself needs no neighbour read.** `SnowAndFreezeFeature` calls
  `Biome.shouldFreeze(level, pos, mustBeAtEdge = false)` — `iconst_0` at the call site in the jar —
  so the four-neighbour "is this water at an edge" test belongs to the random-tick path that freezes
  a pond inward over time, and NOT to worldgen. D-213 and D-217 were both this project paying for a
  feature that read a neighbouring chunk; this one does not have to, and `04p_feat_cold.js` now
  carries vanilla's rule in full above `freeze_top_layer` so nobody adds one.

- **D-220** **THE ORE LEDGER IS SPLIT AT y = 140, AND THE ABUNDANCE ORDER IS TAKEN BELOW IT.**
  `vanillacheck` §4 failed on rank order: vanilla makes more copper (110.07/chunk) than coal
  (81.54), MC-Lite made more coal (103.70) than copper (100.44). The per-Y histogram against the
  golden world says it is not the ore machinery. Below y = 140 the two worlds hold the same rock to
  within **3%** and seven of eight ores are within 5% — coal 1.17x, copper 0.91x, iron 0.98,
  redstone 1.03, gold 1.04, lapis 0.97, diamond 0.98 — and the order is right: copper 100.44 over
  coal 94.39. At and above y = 140 MC-Lite holds **4.03x** vanilla's rock, because **D-172** ruled
  that MC-Lite keeps its hand-fitted ~214 peaks where vanilla implies 177; `ore_coal_upper` is
  `uniform(136, 319)` and `ore_iron_upper` is `uniform(80, 384)`, so those two features find four
  times as much rock to fill and coal comes out **8.46x** up there, iron 4.32x. Nothing else in the
  game has a feature that reaches y = 140 at all, which is why coal and iron alone are affected.
  So: the full-column totals stay printed and stay banded at ±35% — nothing is hidden and no band is
  widened — and the ORDER, which is a claim about the counts in the JSON and not about the terrain,
  is asserted on the sub-140 counts where the two engines offer the same rock. §8 drops the
  above-140 ore counts by name on this decision's authority, and §9 gained a break for it: cutting
  the golden copper alone to a tenth must invert the sub-140 ranking.
  ⚠ **Emerald's 1.40x is not evidence and §4 now says so in the output.** `ore_emerald` is count 100
  of a size-3 blob in the mountain biomes only, so vanilla's 0.28/chunk over 240 chunks is 68 blocks
  drawn from **14 chunks**. The block count is not the sample size, the chunk count is, and 14
  chunks cannot separate 1.0x from 1.4x. The band assertion already skipped rows below 1/chunk;
  it now prints why, so the next session does not spend itself on it.

- **D-221** ⚠ **`edgesLiquid` IS A BLOCK READ ACROSS ELEVEN CHUNKS, AND IT REBUILDS INTO ONE
  SCALAR COMPARISON ON `Column.height`.** D-212 named this as the work it deliberately did not do:
  vanilla's mineshaft rule is not "flood the corridor", it is `MineShaftPieces`' `postProcess`
  opening with `if (this.edgesLiquid(level, box)) return;` — the piece is **never built** — and
  `StructurePiece.edgesLiquid` walks the six faces of the box grown by one, returning at the first
  liquid. Porting it directly is forbidden: it reads blocks over a box spanning up to eleven
  chunks, a read outside the target chunk returns −1 here, and the piece's existence would depend
  on which chunk is being filled. That is D-185's invariant, and this project has paid for
  breaking it twice — **D-213** (every tree built by one chunk and thrown away by the other eight)
  and **D-217** (a disk that would have been sliced the same way).
  **1. The rebuild, and it is D-217's shape.** Two things are pure: `Column.height(x, z)` and
  `seaLevel`. A cell holds sea water exactly when `Column.height(x, z) < y <= seaLevel`, so the
  six-face walk collapses to one comparison: the shell reaches `y0 − 1` below and `y1 + 1` above,
  so it meets water iff `y0 − 1 <= seaLevel` AND the lowest ground under the grown footprint is
  below `min(seaLevel, y1 + 1)`. Water on a side face at a lower y needs ground lower still, so the
  top face's test covers all six. Same answer from all nine targets, in any order, forever.
  ⚠ **MARKED, NOT REMOVED**, which is vanilla's own model: a flagged piece stays in the
  `StructureStart`'s list and `write` returns 0 for it, exactly as `postProcess` returns before
  writing. A first draft filtered the list and **deleted the room of three of 178 mineshafts** —
  `structcheck` §5's *"every mineshaft has exactly one room"* is a statement about the GRAMMAR and
  it was right to fail.
  ⚠ **TWO STAGES, BECAUSE THE EXACT TEST IS 120 ms A MINESHAFT.** `Column.height` is the whole
  spline stack at ~10 µs a column and the union of one mineshaft's grown footprints is ~12,000
  columns — measured over twelve starts at seed 1337: 8.6k–15.2k columns, 98–183 ms each. Paying it
  everywhere would have put ~10 ms a chunk on a 16.9 ms budget. Stage 1 screens the whole start on
  a capped 24×24 lattice (`SU.survey`'s "cap the COUNT, not the spacing") and only concludes *dry*
  when the lowest ground it saw is 8 clear of the highest cell any shell can reach; stage 2 is the
  exact one-block test, on the starts that survive. **The screen is fenced, not trusted**:
  `structaudit` §6b re-derives the shell test in the tool, at one-block resolution, over every
  piece that SHIPPED, and fails if one of them has sea water on its shell — the D-152/D-178/D-194
  mistake avoided by re-deriving from vanilla's rule instead of asking `04s` what it decided. Its
  two anti-vacuity breaks (D-30) break the INPUTS both ways: ground at the world floor must make
  every piece wet, no sea at all must make none.
  **2. And the shave was still removing the rock the sea was standing on.** D-212 stopped
  `SU.writeBeard`'s SHAVE branch *draining* the ocean by skipping water cells. It went on clearing
  the SOLID under them, because the loop ran upward and treated a liquid as something to step past.
  A submerged piece's box was dug out of the sea floor and the sea left sitting on the hole. The
  loop runs **downward** now and **breaks** at the first liquid — one read, same column, legal by
  the same argument `04s`'s plank floor makes (D-185). Classified cell by cell, that was **167 of
  the 279 cells** left after part 1: control world SOLID, written world AIR, natural sea water
  directly above or beside.
  **Measured, both parts, same HEAD, default sample (4 seeds · 147,456 chunks · 56 structures).**
  Structure-written air against water **529 → 279 (gate) → 133**, i.e. **0.37% → 0.20% → 0.09%** of
  structure air, against a natural-terrain baseline of **0.02%** in the same windows.
  ocean_ruin_cold 233 → 0, ruined_portal_ocean 100 → 0, ruined_portal_mountain 63 → 14,
  village_plains 21 → 7. `--deep` (169 structures, 262,144 chunks): 943 → 415, 0.17% → 0.08%,
  ruined_portal_swamp 61 → 0, village_taiga 57 → 9, pillager_outpost 132 → 115. **Nothing rose in
  either sample**; `wrote-air-then-stood-on-it` fell 408 → 404. The register's third entry,
  `water-on-air`, went to **0 in both samples and its entry is DELETED** — D-139's rule, which
  `structaudit` §7 enforces.
  ⚠ **The one number that moved the wrong way, on purpose:** §2's burial for ocean_ruin_cold,
  16.0% → 16.8%. The shave no longer digs the sea floor out from under the water, so a little more
  terrain stands inside a submerged ruin's box. Cost: `gencheck` 14.83 → 14.97 ms a chunk (+0.9%),
  and the gate flags **1,647 of 134,985 pieces (1.22%)** across the 638 mineshafts the audit's scan
  finds.
  ⚠ **WHAT IT STILL CANNOT SEE, WITH THE NUMBER THAT SAYS WHY IT IS NOT FIXED.** `Column.height` is
  the terrain before the carvers, so the gate sees THE SEA and nothing else. MC-Lite's aquifer is a
  FAKE (**D-67**) — one 2D noise decides whether a region has a water table and where it sits — and
  its water exists only in cells a CARVER hollowed, which is a 3D fact no pure column function
  answers. Every one of the mineshaft family's remaining 104 cells is that: corridor air hollowed
  out of solid rock with natural aquifer water beside it. Gating on
  `y0 − 1 <= Caves.aquiferLevel(x, z)` over the footprint instead drops **4,222 of 28,445 pieces
  (14.8%) across 136 mineshafts on four seeds and deletes 7 mineshafts outright**, to remove ~105
  boundary cells — one corridor in seven of every mineshaft in the world, most of them in dry rock
  a carver never touched. That is a far larger deviation than the one it fixes, so it is NOT done
  and it is registered with this measurement instead (same shape as D-216's drape, which is also
  measured and worse). The other residue is a structure cut **sideways** into the shoreline
  (ruined_portal_mountain 14, village_plains 7): the beard stops at the waterline in its own column
  and can still open the column beside it, and that read crosses a chunk boundary in four
  directions out of four.

- **D-222** ⚠⚠ **VANILLA'S TREES LIMIT EACH OTHER, AND MC-LITE'S HAD NOTHING STOPPING THEM.**
  `vanillacheck` §6 — the first check in this project that compares MC-Lite against a world the
  1.18.2 server actually generated — put **jungle_log at 10.10x**, jungle_leaves 3.58x, vine 2.99x,
  oak_leaves 2.09x and oak_log 2.27x, while the whole aquatic chain sat at 1.00x. Three causes,
  each MEASURED before it was touched, and **nothing was scaled to make a ratio come out right.**

  **1. The feedback loop D-134 removed, and nothing replaced.** `trees_jungle` is `count 50,
  in_square, surface_water_depth_filter, heightmap OCEAN_FLOOR, biome`, and every attempt ends in a
  `would_survive` filter on a sapling. In VANILLA the heightmap reads the LIVE chunk: the moment a
  tree stands in a column the next attempt there is lifted to the top of its leaves, and a sapling
  does not grow on a leaf. Fifty attempts become about eight trees. MC-Lite's heightmap is
  `Column.height`, the terrain BEFORE any feature ran (**D-134**), and D-213 gave the guard
  `terrainAt`, the SAME pre-feature world — so the modifier puts every attempt on bare ground and
  the guard is asked a question it cannot answer no to. **MEASURED: 573 of 573 attempts passed —
  100.0%.** The selector was RULED OUT by the same measurement: its option roll came out
  10.3 / 42.1 / 16.4 / 31.2% against vanilla's 10 / 45 / 15 / 30, which is exact.

  ⚠ **The repair is a per-source-chunk CANOPY STAMP, and it is pure by construction.** A live
  heightmap cannot come back — a source chunk computes its placements without generating one block,
  which is the whole architecture. What can come back is the one consequence the trees care about,
  "is this column already under a canopy", because vanilla decides it entirely INSIDE one chunk:
  `in_square` scatters all fifty attempts across the source chunk's own 16x16. So the stamp lives
  in `placementsOf`, is a pure function of (seed, source chunk) exactly as the placement list
  already is, is cached with it, and all nine target chunks read the identical answer — no seam of
  the D-213 kind can exist, because no target ever computes it. A second stamp holds the WOOD,
  which is `getMaxFreeTreeHeight`: vanilla walks the `minimum_size` square at every layer and an
  earlier tree's TRUNK ends the tree while its leaves do not.
  ⚠ **The footprint is MEASURED, not declared** (`04k`'s `measureCanopy`): no declaration would be
  honest, because a blob's widest row is `frad + ro - 1 - (i/2)`, a fancy oak's canopy is five balls
  on a winding trunk and a mega spruce's skirt grows with `k/span * 3.5`. Eight shapes are built
  with `SB` null and the chunk sixteen million blocks away, so every read is -1 and every write a
  no-op, and what is left is the geometry `T.logs`/`T.leaves` already promise is target-independent.
  jungle_tree covers 23.8 columns, mega_jungle_tree 63.8, dark_oak 60.0, mega_spruce 82.5, pine 5.0.
  ⚠ **The seed of a placement is drawn BEFORE the test**, so a chunk's rng stream is bit-identical
  to what it was: the only difference in the world is that attempts vanilla refuses are now refused.

  **2. `would_survive` read "the block below is SOLID", and the rule is `BlockTags.DIRT`.** Thirty
  of the thirty-two `would_survive` predicates in the overworld's data name a SAPLING, and vanilla's
  `SaplingBlock.mayPlaceOn` is the dirt tag, not solidity. Trees stood on terracotta and red sand:
  **4.77 trunks a chunk in a wooded badlands against the real game's 0.77.** `cactus` and
  `sugar_cane` — one use each — stay on the general reading and say so, because both of vanilla's
  rules need a sideways read that G2 is the place for.

  **3. The top-level `block_predicate_filter` was passed through.** `applyChunk` never runs a placed
  feature's own chain, and the four modifiers `runChain` could not answer were let past. That is
  fine for three of them and was NOT fine for this one: `trees_badlands`, `trees_plains`,
  `trees_birch`, `trees_swamp`, `trees_snowy` and every bare `*_checked` a biome lists directly
  carry their ground test THERE rather than inside a selector, so those trees had no ground test at
  all. It is now answered against `terrainAt`, purely, at placement time. Wooded badlands went
  5.47x → 1.41x on that one line.

  Two smaller parity fixes came out of the same reading. `maxFreeHeight` returned `dy` where
  vanilla's `getMaxFreeTreeHeight` returns `i - 1`, and its caller accepted `free >= h - 1` where
  vanilla accepts `>= h` — two layers more permissive in a row, which matters for a 10-to-31-block
  mega trunk (measured movement on the referee: none at 240 chunks; it is vanilla's own test and it
  is now vanilla's own test). And `block_column`'s `prioritize_tip` **was read by nobody**: vanilla
  samples every layer's height, walks the column to see how many cells fit and then TRUNCATES —
  from the far end normally, from the START when the tip is what matters — so a cave vine that runs
  out of room keeps its glowing tip. This grew the layers in order and stopped at the first blocked
  cell, so the tip appeared only when the whole body happened to fit.

  ⚠ **THE RESULT, on 240 chunks of the seed-1337 pregen** (vanilla/chunk → MC-Lite/chunk, ratio
  before → after): jungle_log 10.10 → **2.49**, jungle_leaves 3.58 → **1.28**, vine 2.99 → **1.46**,
  oak_leaves 2.09 → **0.96**, oak_log 2.27 → **0.78**, birch_leaves 1.76 → **1.44**, dark_oak_leaves
  1.64 → **1.05**, spruce_leaves 1.32 → **1.02**. Tree TRUNKS over 165 chunks of every wooded biome
  family: **3.62x → 1.51x**, with dark_forest 2.10 → 1.05, birch_forest 1.67 → 1.13 and grove
  1.46 → 1.08. Aquatic parity is untouched: seagrass 0.97x, kelp 0.96x, tall_seagrass 1.08x.
  `gencheck` 15.18 → 14.85 ms a chunk, which is inside this box's ±0.3 ms run-to-run noise — a
  rejected tree is a tree that is never built, so the work saved pays for the test.

  ⚠ **WHAT IS LEFT, NAMED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A FEATURE BUG.** jungle_log stays at **2.49x** and it
  is **MEGA JUNGLE TREES**: MC-Lite stands 0.96 a chunk where the server stands 0.26, and a mega
  trunk is four columns of twenty logs, so the TREE count is 1.57x while the LOG count is 2.49x. A
  mega jungle tree needs its 5x5 free for a 10-to-31-block trunk and `maxFreeHeight` now runs
  vanilla's own test — **on a smoother world**. MEASURED over 23 jungle-family chunks: the rise to
  the highest column within Chebyshev 2 is 2 or more blocks in **12.8% of vanilla's columns and 4.4%
  of MC-Lite's**, and 4 or more in **2.0% and 0.0%**. That is section 2's business and **D-172**'s
  ruling on the hand-fitted peaks, not the feature pipeline's, and §6 and §8 both name it as such.

  ⚠ **THE TWO APPROXIMATIONS IN THE STAMP, NAMED.** (a) A tree does not block an attempt in the
  NEIGHBOURING source chunk, because that chunk's list is computed on its own; vanilla's canopies do
  reach across, over a rim about 2 blocks of 16. (b) The stamp is a square of the MEASURED plan area
  centred on the trunk, not the canopy's true outline — area is what decides how fast a chunk fills
  up, and the outline is not knowable without building the tree. Neither is a tuned number: (a) is a
  boundary and (b) is a measurement.

- **D-223** ⚠ **`environment_scan` WAS PASSED THROUGH, AND IT IS THE ENTIRE FILTER ON THE LUSH
  CAVES.** `lush_caves_vegetation` is `count 125` and `cave_vines` is `count 188` — a hundred and
  three hundred attempts a chunk, thrown at a uniform y over the whole world height. In vanilla the
  scan is what turns those into the handful that start in cave air and find a floor within twelve
  steps; everything else dies there. Passed through, every one of them ran, and `vegetation_patch`'s
  own five-step floor search then found the nearest rock face and moss-carpeted it. MEASURED on the
  referee: **moss_carpet 4.68x, cave_vines_plant 4.24x**, and — because `moss_vegetation` is mostly
  grass — **most of grass 2.05x** as well, which is why a DESERT chunk had 43.5 grass a chunk
  against the real game's 10.3.

  The scan is now evaluated at placement time against **`carvedAt`**, which is D-213's `terrainAt`
  with `Caves.carve` laid over it. ⚠ `terrainAt` is pre-carver BY CONSTRUCTION, and asked of an
  uncarved world this modifier is meaningless — every position underground is already solid.
  ⚠ **`Caves.carve` is the point query 04b reserves for tools**, which the chunk path (an
  interpolated lattice) is not obliged to agree with. That disagreement is a PLACEMENT decision and
  not a written block: it is identical in all nine targets, so there is no seam; a false positive is
  caught by the patch generator's own live floor search a moment later; a false negative costs one
  attempt of the hundred-odd a chunk makes. It is the same approximation `04k`'s `maxFreeHeight`
  already makes, named a second time rather than made twice. The aquifer is not modelled — a flooded
  cave reads as air — because **D-67** already says MC-Lite's aquifer is a fake.

  ⚠ **THE ORDER IS MOVE, THEN TARGET, THEN ALLOWED, and the first draft got it backwards.** The scan
  starts in air and the thing it is looking for is the FLOOR, which is not air; testing `allowed`
  before `target` on the moved position rejects the floor as "not air" one step before noticing it
  is the floor. Every scan in the world then failed and moss_carpet went from 4.68x to **0.00x**.
  It is written down because the failure was silent and total, and the ledger was the only thing
  that saw it.

  **RESULT, 240 chunks:** cave_vines_plant 4.24x → **1.14x**, moss_carpet 4.68x → **2.18x**, grass
  2.05x → **1.23x**, big_dripleaf 0.82x, clay 1.08x, rooted_dirt 1.01x, moss_block 1.79x.

  ⚠ **`featcheck` §5b's LUSH FLOORS WERE MEASURING THE BUG, and they are re-anchored, not loosened.**
  Four thresholds — 200 cave_vines placements, 100 lush_caves_vegetation, 50 lush_caves_clay, 500
  rooted_dirt and 50 azalea_leaves over a 16-chunk region — were all calibrated while the scan was
  passed through, and every one of them failed the moment it was not. THE FLOORS WERE WRONG: the
  same referee now puts those densities at 0.95x to 1.79x of the real game. They are BANDS now, not
  floors, because a floor cannot tell "fixed" from "reverted". The two rare ones are dropped from
  that region with the arithmetic written down: `rooted_azalea_tree` is `count uniform(1,2)` behind
  the same scan, so sixteen chunks expect well under one tree, and the server puts azalea_leaves at
  **0.15 a chunk** — a floor of 50 in sixteen chunks was asserting twelve times the real density.
  The referee measures them over 240 chunks instead, at rooted_dirt 1.01x and azalea_leaves 0.61x.

  ⚠ **STILL OUT, AND IT IS NOT THIS FIX'S DOING: `cave_vines` (the glowing TIP) at 0.38x** while
  `cave_vines_plant` (the body) is at 1.14x. The columns are right and most of them have no tip,
  because **`States.ceilingOk(cave_vines, cave_vines_plant)` is FALSE** — D-140's write-time support
  rule refuses a vine tip hanging under its own body. That table is in `02c_states.js`, which this
  work did not own; it is inside §6's band, it is written into `featcheck` §4d beside the test that
  had to be reshaped around it, and it is one line for whoever owns that file next.

- **D-224** ⚠ **A FIXED SLEEP IS A MEASUREMENT OF THE MACHINE THAT WROTE IT.** `palettecheck` and
  `flashcheck` were the last two browser stages still red at `MCLITE_PRESET=medium` (D-196), and
  the first of the two looked like a rendering regression: fast leaves, D-93's single biggest win
  on the machine this project exists for, appeared to leave the picture **identical**. It does
  not. Neither check had found an engine bug; both were asserting things about a world that had
  not finished arriving, and the fix in both is the same shape — **measure the box, then wait for
  the thing the box actually has to finish, and only then read the picture.**

  **1. `palettecheck` was photographing a remesh that was 3% done.** `Settings.push({remesh:
  true})` calls `World.remeshAll`, which marks every section of every resident column dirty. At
  `high`'s render distance on the two-core software-rasteriser box the browser stages run on that
  is **8,400 sections**, against a mesher clearing **25 to 55 a second**. The old `await
  sleep(7000)` was reading the frame three per cent of the way into a two-and-a-half-minute job.
  Measured directly, whole-frame mean saturation after flipping `fancyLeaves` off:

  | after | 7 s | 15 s | 21 s | 40 s | 60 s | 75 s |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | moved | **0.08%** | 6.6% | 16.5% | 19.7% | 29.4% | 31.4%, still climbing |

  The check took the first column and used it as its own allowance — a bound derived from a
  measurement of nothing, which then failed the celeron comparison underneath it. ⚠ **The mesher
  was never wrong while this was happening**: `coherecheck` §4 says fancy still emits 14,586 of
  14,586 leaf faces and fast exactly the 5,144-face exposed surface, and it said so throughout.

  **2. "Every section is clean" is not a reachable state and never was.** `World.stream` will not
  mesh a column whose 3x3 neighbourhood is not generated, so the rim of the loaded disc stays
  dirty for as long as it is resident: **718 sections of permanent residue at render distance 8**,
  against 1,741 sections of work the streamer would actually do. A settle written on the raw
  dirty count waits for ever. The one this file now uses is `stream`'s own arithmetic — dirty
  sections INSIDE the render distance whose neighbourhood is ready, plus everything in flight and
  everything queued for upload — and it reaches zero.

  **3. The render distance is now chosen by measurement, not assumed.** The wait reports the rate
  it measured, so a distance this machine cannot finish is abandoned on the projection rather
  than sat out: **rd 16 gave up after 9 s** (1,324 sections left, 20/s — the projection says
  minutes), **rd 8 settled in 51 s**, and every preset is then compared at rd 8. On a machine
  that can hold `high`, the first rung is taken and nothing is given up.

  **4. Pinning the render distance was never enough, and 16 of the celeron gap was the pin's
  fault.** A preset's twenty keys split in two: the ones that decide how EXPENSIVE the frame is
  and the ones that decide what it LOOKS like. Only the second is on trial. Measured at the
  medium preset, everything settled, celeron against `high`:

      render distance pinned, nothing else    mean saturation 18.0% away  ✗ (allowance 6.0%)
      every cost axis pinned                                    7.1% away  ✓ (allowance 16.1%)

  The 11 points in between were `fogStart` (0.35 against 0.70 — celeron's haze starts at half the
  distance), `maxChunks` (160 against 1,600, a resident world an eighth the size) and the
  streamer's own budgets, which made celeron's remesh take **118 s where `high`'s took 13**. None
  of those is a tint. ⚠ **The pin has to be applied in the SAME `Runtime.evaluate` as
  `applyPreset`**, because `applyPreset` pushes `maxChunks` into the streamer before it returns
  and the next frame's `evict` acts on it; nothing yields inside one evaluation, so the streamer
  never sees the preset's budgets at all.

  **5. The allowance is now the measured sum of the look flags each preset differs from `high`
  in**, one at a time, on a settled world: `depthPrepass` 0.0%, `smoothLighting` 0.0%, `mipmaps`
  3.6%, `fancyLeaves` **6.5%**, `ao` 0.0% (a brightness multiplier cannot move `(max-min)/max`,
  and its luma delta is 0.4% at this camera — the existing note was right). So medium, which
  differs from `high` in `depthPrepass` and nothing else, is allowed the 6% drift margin and
  **measures 0.000/0.000/0.000 of mean colour: the two frames are identical**. That is a far
  tighter bound than the `leaf + 6%` every preset used to share. ⚠ And the classification is
  ASSERTED: every key in `Settings.PRESET_KEYS` must be either pinned as a cost or measured as a
  look, so a preset key added later cannot slip past the allowance unnoticed.
  §2, the section that actually catches D-159, went from **37 changed pixels to 12,174**.

  **6. `flashcheck` was starving its own phases, in three separate ways, and all three were the
  probe.** Its recovery beat handed a phase over at a flat `eligible >= 32` — a number its own
  scorer does not use. The scorer's floor is half the fullest world seen at that render distance,
  which measured **58 at rd 8**, so every phase was handed a world less than half of what it
  needed to judge: `teleport` scored 5 frames of 201 and `f7-f8-toggle` 7 of 78. `resize` had no
  beat at all. And the closing `settle` phase ran for three seconds, which is thirty frames at 60
  fps and **eight** at 2.7 — a phase of eight frames cannot clear a ten-frame bar however healthy
  the picture in them is.
  ⚠ **The beat now waits for the scorer's floor AND for the picture to stop growing, and the
  `&&` is the whole point.** Returning on the floor alone is self-defeating, because the floor IS
  `peak[rd]`: measured, that version left a full world at rd 8 reading **16** frustum sections
  where waiting for the plateau reached **229**, and every later judgement was made over a
  fourteenth of the world. Nothing lowered `FC.FLOOR` or `FC.FULL`; lowering the eligibility
  threshold is the one change that would have made the whole probe vacuous.

  **7. Where a phase is still short, the check now says WHY, in sections a second.** Every frame
  records `World.stats2.meshed`, which only goes up and only by sections the mesher handed back.
  Three verdicts, and only one of them is an excuse:
  **the world stopped arriving** (0 delivered while the picture sat under the floor) FAILS;
  **nothing delivered ever became eligible** (meshes built that never reach the frustum) FAILS;
  **the box could not keep up** (delivering the whole way and still short) is reported with the
  measured rate and does not fail — on two cores under a software rasteriser at render distance
  12 it is simply true, and the engine cannot fix it. A vacuity guard fails the run if fewer than
  half the phases scored, so the excuse cannot be handed to a whole run, and §5 runs `phaseVerdict`
  itself over synthetic rows in both directions.

  **Measured after, at the medium preset:** `flashcheck` 4,509 frames against 2,464, **6 of 7
  phases scored**, one excused with its numbers, 0 failures, and the settled camera drawing
  112,606 triangles against 39,484 — the probe is now watching a world roughly three times as
  full as the one it used to. ⚠ **It costs wall clock**: a run is about a quarter of an hour on
  the container box, because a full world at rd 8 there takes a minute and a half to arrive.
  On hardware with a real GPU the plateau comes in seconds and neither check waits.

- **D-225** ⚠ **THE SWAMP WAS DRY BECAUSE THE WORLD WAS THREE BLOCKS TOO HIGH, NOT BECAUSE THE
  RULE WAS WRONG.** `vanillacheck` §3 had one biome left disagreeing on its surface after D-219:
  **swamp, 65.6% agreement over 1,792 golden columns — vanilla tops 62% of them with water and
  MC-Lite topped 71% with grass_block** — while every other biome sat at 79–100%. The obvious
  suspect was the surface rule, because vanilla's swamp clause is the only one in the whole
  overworld tree that names a single block of y:

      biome_is [minecraft:swamp] -> y_above absolute 62 -> NOT y_above absolute 63
                                 -> noise_threshold minecraft:surface_swamp >= 0.0
                                 -> water[level=0]

  **THE RULE WAS ALREADY PERFECT.** Driven directly at 4,000 real swamp positions with the column
  top forced to y = 62, `Surface.stateAt` returns `water[level=0]` in exactly the columns where
  `surface_swamp(x, 0, z) >= 0` and in no others; `minecraft:surface_swamp` is packed with
  vanilla's own `firstOctave -2 / [1.0]`; the clause fires at y = 62 and at no other y, and in
  swamp and in no other biome. Nothing about `noise_threshold`, `y_above`, `pack-worldgen.mjs` or
  the order of the sequence was ever wrong. ⚠ The `yTop = hs - MINY` lead — vanilla's
  `SurfaceSystem.buildSurface` starts one cell higher — is a real difference and is **not this
  bug**: the cells above the terrain top are air and MC-Lite computes its stone depths
  arithmetically rather than by scanning, so starting higher changes nothing.

  **THE CAUSE IS `HEIGHT_CURVE`'s SEA-LEVEL ANCHOR, AND IT WAS ALWAYS WRITTEN DOWN AS A GUESS.**
  `04d_column.js` mapped `offset 0.0 -> y 66`, commented "coast, three blocks above sea level
  (63)". Vanilla's own arithmetic — `density_function/overworld/depth.json` is a
  `y_clamped_gradient(-64..320, 1.5..-1.5)` plus the offset spline, so the mean surface is
  `y = 128 + 128 * offset`, and `TerrainShaper.offset` subtracts **0.50375** in Java — puts that
  same point at `128 + 128 * (0 - 0.50375) = ` **63.52**. D-172 had already named that missing
  constant a TRUE OMISSION rather than part of deviation #1. It was worth **+2.5 blocks at sea
  level**, and measured against the golden world the median height residual in the y 61–63 band
  was **+3**. Nothing notices a plains three blocks too high. The swamp notices, because its
  clause needs the terrain top to BE y = 62, and MC-Lite's swamps topped out at 64–67.

  ⚠ **AND THE SEA FILLED ONE BLOCK TOO HIGH** (`04_worldgen.js` §2). Vanilla's global fluid
  picker is `FluidStatus(seaLevel, water)` and `FluidStatus.at(y)` returns water only for
  `y < fluidLevel`, so the real game's topmost water block is y = **62**. MC-Lite's loop said
  `y <= seaL` and put it at 63. Against the golden world **92% of `river` columns had MC-Lite's
  top block exactly one higher than vanilla's**. The same off-by-one corrupted the `waterY` handed
  to the surface rules: vanilla's `waterHeight` is the topmost fluid's y **plus one**, and
  `Integer.MIN_VALUE` when there is no fluid at all, so a column whose terrain top is exactly
  `sea - 1` has NO water on it — and saying `waterY = 63` there made the tree's `water offset=0`
  test (`y >= waterY`) false and answered **dirt** where vanilla answers `grass_block`.

  **THE FIX IS THREE VALUES.** `HEIGHT_CURVE`'s `[0.0, 66]` becomes `[0.0, 63.52]`; the sea fill
  becomes `y < seaL`; `waterY` becomes `hs < sea - 1 ? sea : NO_WATER`. The anchors at 0.2 and
  above are the DELIBERATE half of D-172's calibration — the stretch that stands in for the
  vertical variance dropping `base_3d_noise` removes — and they are untouched. `colcheck` §3c
  still pins the worst disagreement with vanilla's arithmetic at ~37 blocks, at the peaks, where
  Dan ruled it stays.

  **MEASURED, on the 240-chunk `vanillacheck` sample, before -> after:**

  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | swamp surface agreement | **65.6%** | **98.1%** |
  | swamp top block | grass_block 71% | water 60% (vanilla 62%) |
  | badlands | 78.4% | 85.6% |
  | wooded_badlands | 88.7% | 90.1% |
  | height residual, whole sample | median +1, \|d\|<=1 56.3% | median **0**, \|d\|<=1 **60.0%** |
  | height residual, below sea | median +1, \|d\|<=3 93.0% | median **0**, \|d\|<=3 **98.2%** |

  No biome joined the ledger and no named fence moved: frozen_ocean 91.4 (fence 84), snowy_plains
  96.5 (94), snowy_slopes 88.9 (86), grove 96.7 (95), jagged_peaks 97.2 (79), and the worst row in
  the table is old_growth_birch_forest at 77.5%, unchanged. ⚠ **Five biomes gave back a few points
  and the number is named rather than buried**: desert 97.1 -> 94.4, jungle 95.2 -> 91.2, plains
  93.9 -> 90.5, river 90.2 -> 88.4, forest 95.2 -> 94.7. Lowering the world 2.5 blocks at sea
  level moves where a beach ends and an ocean begins, and those five are the biomes that have a
  shoreline in this sample. All are far above §3's floor of 65 and none is near the 70 that makes
  a ledger entry. `gencheck` reports **14.99 ms a chunk**.

  ⚠ **`surfcheck` §3b IS THE CHECK THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, AND IT HAS TO BE TWO CHECKS.**
  §3 drives every biome at y = 70 and §8 asks only whether the top block is one vanilla is
  *allowed* to place in that biome — and `grass_block` is allowed in a swamp, so an entirely dry
  swamp passed both. §3b therefore asserts the clause's shape against the shipped JSON, drives it
  and requires water exactly where the noise is non-negative and at no other y and in no other
  biome, **and then generates 121 chunks of the golden world's own swamp and requires the water
  fraction to land inside 40..85 around the real game's 62%.** Its two anti-vacuity breaks split
  the same way: collapsing the clause's y window breaks the driven half, and putting the 66 back
  in `HEIGHT_CURVE` breaks the generated half. Only the second one reproduces the original bug —
  a compiled rule that is perfectly correct and never reached — which is the whole lesson.
  ⚠ The break that says `62 -> 61` does NOT work and the first draft used it: the clause is
  `y_above 62 AND NOT y_above 63`, so lowering the bound widens the window to {61, 62} and y = 62
  still fires. It has to be `62 -> 63`, which makes the window empty.

  ⚠ **`04d_column.js` IS OUTSIDE THIS WORK'S NAMED FILE LIST** and it is changed anyway, because
  the measurement put the cause there and a partial hand-off is a failure. It is one number and a
  comment; nothing else in that file moved.

- **D-226** ⚠⚠ **THE OCEAN MONUMENT WAS A DRY BUBBLE, AND NO CHECK THIS PROJECT HAS COULD SEE IT
  BECAUSE THE BUILDING IS WIDER THAN THE WINDOW.**

  `04w`'s monument hollowed itself out with `SU.Cells`'s `-1` marker, and `-1` means AIR. The
  comment on the line said *"hollow the interior out to water"* and the code wrote air; that one
  word was **41,362 cells of ocean turned into air per monument — 78.6% of every natural water
  cell in its window**, measured over two monuments on two seeds by generating each chunk twice
  and diffing. Every other structure family in the sample drained **zero**.

  D-212 fixed three writers that drained the sea (the beard's shave, `JG.writePiece`'s template
  air, the mineshaft's carve) and D-221 fixed two more. It could not reach this one: the monument
  is not a template and not a carve, it is a hand-built `blocksPiece`, and `-1` is the only clear
  marker `SU.writeBlocks` had.

  ⚠ **WHY `structaudit` §6 CALLED IT CLEAN FOR THREE SESSIONS, WHICH IS THE REAL LESSON.** §6's
  measured class is *"a structure-written AIR cell with water beside it or above it"*. A writer
  that drains the WHOLE NEIGHBOURHOOD scores zero on that class — there is no water left to be
  against. And the deep window is at most 3 chunks (48 blocks) square while a monument is 58
  blocks across, so the sampled window lay **entirely inside the building** and contained no sea
  at all. The check was measuring the inside of a bubble and reporting that the bubble was fine.

  **THE FIX.** `SU.SEA` (`-2`) is a second clear marker: water at or below `seaLevel`, air above
  it. The clamp is vanilla's own — `OceanMonumentBuilding.postProcess` floods its box up to
  `max(getSeaLevel(), 64)` — and it keeps a turret that pokes out of the water from carrying a
  column of sea in its roof. It is a pure function of `y`, so D-185 holds and there is no seam,
  and it reads no block, so it costs nothing over `-1`. Every hollow of the monument uses it: the
  interior, the core, the four turrets and the twelve entrance arches. Vanilla's monument has no
  air in it at all — every empty cell of an `OceanMonumentPiece` goes through `generateWaterBox`.

  ⚠ **AND THE REFEREE SETTLES IT, NOT AN OPINION.** Six real 1.18.2 ocean monuments on the golden
  pregen (seed 1337), found by clustering their prismarine and measuring inside the cluster's own
  bounding box: **water 53.3–72.9%, air 0.0–0.5%, natural terrain 6.6–34.7%**. MC-Lite's four
  monuments, measured by the identical procedure: water was **0%** before this fix and is
  **66.9–69.5%** after it — inside the real game's band. Air is 12.3–13.2% and that is the part of
  MC-Lite's monument ABOVE the waterline; see the open item at the end of this entry.

  **THE SECOND MONUMENT BUG, FOUND BY THE SAME PASS.** `c.box(27, 3, 27, 30, 3, 30, DP)` put the
  core's dark-prismarine dais inside a hollow of 25..32, so it touched nothing: an 18-cell island
  of dark prismarine and two sea lanterns hanging in the middle of the chamber. It is 25..32 now
  and rests on the core wall.

  **AND THE THIRD MECHANISM BEHIND `wrote-air-then-stood-on-it`, WHICH IS WHAT THIS WORK WAS SENT
  TO FIND.** The register carried 404 cells in the default sample and named two writers, neither
  of which was the biggest. Classified block by block, **180 of the 404 (44.6%) were in MONUMENT
  windows and not one of them was prismarine**: 164 were DEAD CORAL BLOCKS and 16 were the
  floating dais. The mechanism is **the feature pass building on ground the structure took** — the
  monument drained the sea, `04q`'s coral features then ran over the hole, found air where they
  expected water, wrote the DEAD variant of themselves and left it standing on the hole. A
  structure that drains the sea does not merely look wrong; it changes what the feature pass
  builds on top of it. Both go to zero with the flood.

  **WHAT REMAINS OF THAT CLASS IS VANILLA'S OWN RULE, AND IT IS COUNTED.** Of the 190 cells left
  in the default sample, **172 (90.5%) are `oak_planks` / `dark_oak_planks` at a mineshaft
  corridor's floor row** — 614 of 743 (82.6%) in `--deep`. `MineShaftCorridor.postProcess` places
  them there *because* the cell is air: `if (this.getBlock(level, x, -1, z, box).isAir())
  placeBlock(PLANKS)`. `04s` transcribes that test verbatim. A plank floor laid across a hole is
  what vanilla builds, the hole under it is another corridor of the same mineshaft, and this arm
  of the register will not go to zero. It stays registered so the 18 cells that are NOT it stay
  visible.

  **THE SHAVE'S WATERLINE BREAK WAS A BLOCK READ, AND A BLOCK READ CAN BE LIED TO.** D-221 gave
  `SU.writeBeard`'s shave a `break` on water, so it would not undermine the sea. Every FILL in a
  structure runs before every shave (that is what `phase` is for), so a plinth that had already
  reclaimed a shoreline left DIRT where the sea had been and the shave walked straight down
  through the waterline finding nothing to stop at. `structaudit` §6c caught the result: a
  two-cell **dry pocket at −1576, 56..57, −452 under five blocks of standing sea**. The shave now
  also stops on the pure form, `Column.height(x, z) < y <= seaLevel` — D-221's own test, which
  says where the sea WAS whatever has since been written over it. `air-against-water` went
  **113 → 92** with it: ruined_portal_mountain 10 → 0, ruined_portal_jungle 1 → 0, village_plains
  13 → 3.

  ── **THE REPORTING BUGS, WHICH WERE IN A TOOL WHOSE WHOLE JOB IS TO BE BELIEVED** ──

  **A FAMILY LABEL IN `structaudit` WAS THE NAME OF THE WINDOW, NOT OF THE STRUCTURE.** §3 has
  refused to blame a neighbour's technical block on the sampled family since it was written; §1's
  histogram used the start's BOUNDING BOX, which for a village is a hundred-block cube of mostly
  empty world, and §6 used no ownership test at all. So a `shipwreck 3` row was a mineshaft
  corridor crossing the shipwreck's window, and which family a defect landed on **changed with
  what else a run happened to sample**. Every count in §1, §2 and §6 is now split by
  `insidePiece` — §3's own test — and what the rest of the structure pass did in the same window
  is printed beside it under `window(not ours)` and charged to nobody. MEASURED on `--deep`:
  **pillager_outpost's ungrounded cells go 384 → 26**, and village_taiga's 175 window cells
  resolve to **9** that are the village's.

  **AND A STRUCTURE WIDER THAN THE WINDOW CANNOT BE MEASURED THIS WAY AT ALL.** A monument is 58
  blocks across and the deep window is 48, so every monument §1 reports is a CORE whose outer wall
  and whose footing are outside the frame — nothing in it can rest on natural ground, and §1
  duly reports 39–47% of it ungrounded. That is a fact about the frame. The row now carries
  `⚠ CLIPPED n/m` so a reader cannot take the worst floating figure in the file off the one
  structure the method cannot see whole.

  ── **§6c, THE NEW SECTION, AND WHY ITS SHAPE IS THE ONE IT IS** ──

  §6 asks whether there is water LEFT beside a structure's air. §6c asks the control world
  instead: **was this cell water, with water directly above it, and is it air now?** The `above`
  clause is what makes it an assertion rather than a complaint — without it the class also catches
  a jungle temple's `generateBox(AIR)` taking out a ONE-BLOCK puddle (73 cells on seed 1337) and a
  village house built into the edge of a pond, both of which are what vanilla's own box writers
  do. The **asserted** form is narrower still and is a statement about the finished world: the
  same cell with water standing SOMEWHERE ABOVE IT — a dry bubble a player digs down through the
  sea floor and falls into. Vanilla makes none; every family in the sample is now at zero.

  ⚠ Its anti-vacuity break (D-30) is **D-226 in miniature, and it asserts BOTH halves**: a walled
  and roofed 3×3×3 room hollowed out of the sea floor must be counted 27 times by §6c **and
  missed entirely by §6** (`leakAir === 0`), because a break that only proves the new measurement
  fires would not prove it measures something the old one could not. A one-block surface film
  cleared off the ground must count zero, which is what keeps the `above` clause honest.

  ── **§2 BURIAL, RULED WITH THE REFEREE RATHER THAN WITH AN OPINION** ──

  Nothing in §2 is a defect, and the two shapes that make its numbers large are now measured:

  · **The worst single piece in the whole sample, at 62.5%, is a mineshaft STAIRS piece, and
    62.5% is its ARITHMETIC.** An 8 × 8 × 3 box is 192 cells and a three-wide stepped channel
    through it is 72, so 120 stay rock. Vanilla's `MineShaftStairs` has the same box and carves
    the same channel. §2 prints the worst piece's KIND AND SHAPE now, so nobody re-derives it a
    fourth time.

  · **A submerged ruin genuinely is part buried, and the referee says by how much.** Six real
    1.18.2 ocean ruins on the golden pregen, found by clustering their `stone_bricks` family and
    measuring inside the cluster's own bounding box: **9.1%, 11.7%, 14.0%, 20.0%, 29.3% and
    29.8% natural terrain — and 0.0% AIR, every one.** MC-Lite's `ocean_ruin_cold` at 16.8% and
    `ocean_ruin_warm` at 21–27% are inside that band. What vanilla does NOT have is the air, and
    that invariant is §6's and §6c's.

  The bound therefore moves from **95% to 75%**, and it is derived rather than fitted: above every
  shape either of those two produces, below anything a piece whose carve did not run can look
  like. `--deep`'s three largest are 62.5% (the staircase), 42.1% (a mansion room) and 38.6% (an
  igloo).

  ── **THE ONE THING THIS WORK MEASURED AND DID NOT FIX** ──

  ⚠ **MC-LITE'S MONUMENTS BREAK THE SURFACE OF THE SEA AND VANILLA'S NEVER DO.** Every one of the
  six real monuments on the pregen tops out at **y = 60** — vanilla plants the building at a fixed
  y and its roof is three blocks under the waterline, which is why you cannot see a monument from
  a boat. MC-Lite anchors it to the sea floor (`floorY = s.lo - 1`) and its shape is 29 layers
  tall against vanilla's 22, so its four corner turrets stand at **y = 66**, three blocks out of
  the water, and 12.3–13.2% of its box is dry air above the waterline. This is a silhouette
  question with two coupled numbers — the anchor and the height — and changing the anchor alone
  would bury the building instead: at a top of y = 60 the floor goes to 32 and the sea floor (up
  to y = 51 by the monument's own siting rule) would put up to 65% of it inside rock, against the
  referee's worst real monument at 34.7%. It wants both numbers moved together and a look at the
  result, which is a session with a picture in it. **The measurement is written down here so the
  next one does not have to take it again.**
