- **D-227** ⚠⚠ **EVERY PARITY CLAIM IN THIS PROJECT RESTED ON ONE WORLD. IT NOW RESTS ON TWO, AND
  THE SECOND ONE DISAGREED FIVE TIMES.** `vanillacheck` compared MC-Lite against 13,307 chunks the
  real 1.18.2 server generated **at seed 1337**, and every bound in the file was fitted there. That
  is D-148's shape (*a test that runs at the origin tests the origin*) and D-179's (*one sample
  point out there proves nothing*) a third time: **a rule tuned to seed 1337 passes seed 1337 in
  silence.** A second pregen — seed 4242, 6,298 full chunks, ten areas, the same driver and the
  same jar SHA-1 — was already on disk and unwired.

  **THE FILE NOW TAKES A WORLD INSTEAD OF ASSUMING ONE.** `--golden <dir>`, `--seed <n>`,
  `--cross <dir>`, `--no-cross`, `--cross-chunks <n>`. Every `pregen*` directory beside a named
  candidate is discovered, so a second world needs no configuration once it is written next to the
  first. Default behaviour is unchanged: the named candidates are considered first and in order, so
  `WORLDS[0]` is still exactly the directory the one-world version picked. Both worlds are read
  through the same `provenance`/`openWorld`/`measure` — a difference between two worlds must never
  be a difference between two readers — and the engine is re-seeded with one `Gen.init`. Absent
  golden data still prints SKIP with the reason and exits 0, and now also prints the worlds it DID
  find, which is what a `--seed` that matches nothing needs to say.

  ── **§10: THE RATIO, NOT THE PASS** ──

  "Both worlds pass" is the weaker claim: both bands are wide enough to hold a compensating error.
  The strong one is that the **MC-Lite/vanilla RATIO agrees between worlds** — 0.96x oak leaves
  here should be about 0.96x there, because the number is a property of the PORT and not of the
  seed. §10 takes every family measurable in both worlds and bounds `q = rB / rA`.

  ⚠ **THE BOUND IS SYMMETRIC IN LOG SPACE, AND THE FIRST DRAFT WAS NOT.** `0.70x..1.30x` failed on
  rows that had just passed the moment the two worlds were run the other way round, because
  swapping them inverts every `q`. One factor `K` per kind, `q ∈ [1/K, K]`. ⚠ **AND THE FACTOR IS
  PER KIND, BECAUSE THE KINDS ARE NOT THE SAME CLAIM.** MEASURED at 240 chunks of each world:
  **every ore agrees between the two worlds to within 9%** (coal 1.09, the rest inside 1.05) — the
  strongest evidence in the file that the ore machinery is a property of the port. Ore and carved
  void get `K = 1.20`; a decoration family legitimately moves with the biome mix the sample drew,
  worst honest row `grass` at 1.34, so `K = 1.40`. Its anti-vacuity break triples and halves the
  **second** world's golden data and requires the cross-seed band to move (6 of 6 and 12 of 12).

  ── **WHAT THE SECOND WORLD FOUND** ──

  1. ⚠⚠ **THE DEEP CARVERS DO NOT TRACK THE REGION.** §5 holds the carved void in y −59..40 to
     ±20%. At seed 1337 it is 0.93–1.01x; **at seed 4242 it is 1.24x at 240 chunks and 1.31x at
     480, and §5 fails there.** A new y-band split says where: **−59..−21 is 1.18x at seed 1337 and
     1.45–1.52x at seed 4242**, while −20..9 and 10..40 sit at or under parity in BOTH. MC-Lite's
     deep volume is nearly CONSTANT between the worlds (2,715 and 2,569 cells a chunk) where
     vanilla's moves 24% (2,638 and 2,112). **The ±20% band is NOT relaxed** — §5 fails at seed
     4242 and should; §10 carries it as a NAMED open bug with a fence of 1.40x.
  2. ⚠ **BIRCH LEAVES ARE 1.34x IN ONE WORLD AND 0.92x IN THE OTHER** — a 1.47x swing inside §6's
     per-world 0.5x..1.9x leaf band, so **neither world's own band could ever have seen it.** Cause
     unproven; the suspect is the old-growth share (seed 1337: 1,008 `old_growth_birch_forest`
     columns against 832 `birch_forest`; seed 4242: 400 against 784, and the sign of the error
     follows it). Named with a 1.55x fence, to be ratcheted down, not widened.
  3. ⚠ **D-225's SWAMP FIX OVERSHOT, AND ONLY THE SECOND WORLD SAYS SO.** D-225 dropped the world
     2.5 blocks and took swamp from 65.6% to passing at seed 1337. At seed 4242 swamp is **62.6%
     over 768 columns and §3 fails: vanilla tops 55% of them with water, MC-Lite 86%.** The sign
     has flipped — MC-Lite's swamps are now too WET where they used to be too dry. A fix validated
     against one world is a fix validated against one world.
  4. **§7's "vanilla placed it and MC-Lite placed none" fired on noise, and two was never a
     sample.** MC-Lite places 0.7x vanilla's starts, so at n=2 the chance of drawing none is
     exp(−1.4) = 25% and at n=3 it is 12%. Seed 4242 duly produced `buried_treasure` 3-against-0
     and `igloo` 3-against-0 — **both of which MC-Lite does place at seed 1337.** The threshold is
     now **5**, the first n at which drawing none is under 5%, and the claim it was reaching for is
     made properly in §10 across BOTH worlds: a kind vanilla places in each and MC-Lite places in
     neither is a dead grammar, and no Poisson draw can manufacture that.
  5. **A NAMED DEVIATION CANNOT BE TESTED IN A WORLD THAT HAS NO JUNGLE.** §6's liveness assertion
     fired on `jungle_log` at seed 4242, whose ten areas contain no jungle and where the real
     server places not one. It is now asserted wherever vanilla places the block, reported as
     untestable where it places none — and a static test was added in its place, so a renamed or
     mistyped name still fails in every world: a named family must be a block `VEG` matches and
     some vanilla FEATURE places.

  ── **§6 STOPS MEASURING STRUCTURES IN A DECORATION LEDGER** ──

  `oak_planks` was 2.99x and carried a NAMED exception saying no feature places it. That was true
  and it was the wrong shape: if it is true, §6 is counting village and mineshaft material in a
  decoration ledger, and the honest fix is to say so **per family** rather than to carry an
  exception. The ledger is now split by asking **vanilla's own `configured_feature` registry**
  whether any feature places the block, following selector references through the `placed_feature`
  registry, with a hand table for the Java features whose block is compiled in rather than
  configured (`SeagrassFeature`, `VinesFeature`, `KelpFeature`, the coral shapes and twenty
  others). ⚠ **THE TABLE'S GAPS ARE LOUD:** a configured feature that names no block and is not in
  it fails the check — which is how eight tree selectors and `warm_ocean_vegetation` were found
  while writing it. `oak_planks` and `oak_fence` are printed as structure material and left to §7;
  the decoration side must keep at least twelve families, so the split cannot be used to quiet the
  section.

  ── **AND ONE NUMBER THE TWO WORLDS SETTLED: `cave_vines` 0.38x IS A BUG, AND IT IS NOT THE
  SCAN** ──

  D-223's new `environment_scan` filter took `cave_vines` from 0.93x to 0.38x and it was reported
  as *exposed, not caused*. It is neither. ⚠ **THE FILTER IS INNOCENT AND THE NUMBERS SAY SO
  TWICE.** `cave_vines_plant` — the vine BODY, placed by the same feature behind the same scan — is
  **1.15x**, and MC-Lite makes roughly the right number of vine COLUMNS: 4.88 a chunk against the
  golden world's 5.36. What is missing is the HEAD. Walking every vertical run of vine in 800
  golden chunks and in 144 MC-Lite ones: **vanilla has 4,286 runs and 4,285 of them end in a
  `cave_vines` head; MC-Lite has 703 runs and 533 of them have no head at all**, and every MC-Lite
  run that HAS a head is exactly one block long.

  **THE CAUSE IS `States.ceilingOk`, and it is a whole family of plants, not one block.**
  `src/02c_states.js` ends both placement tests with "…or the neighbour is the SAME BLOCK":

      SR.ceilingOk = function (st, above) {
        if (above === 0) return false;
        if (SR.opaqueBase[above] === 1) return true;
        return SR.block[above] === SR.block[st] && SR.stacksOnSelf(st);
      };

  Vanilla's `AbstractGrowingPlantBlock.canAttachTo` accepts the plant's **head block OR its body
  block** or a sturdy face. A `cave_vines` head hangs under a `cave_vines_plant` body — different
  blocks — so `04j_features.js`'s `setBlock` support test refuses the head and returns 0 without
  writing it. The head therefore survives only when the sampled body length is 0 and it hangs
  straight off the ceiling, which is 17–21% of columns and matches the measured 24%.
  `weeping_vines`/`weeping_vines_plant` (ceiling class) and `twisting_vines`/`twisting_vines_plant`
  (floor class, `floorOk`) have the identical defect; `kelp`/`kelp_plant` escape only because their
  support class is 0. **Fix at `src/02c_states.js`'s `floorOk`/`ceilingOk` — the head/body pair of
  a growing plant must attach to each other — not at the scan and not at §6's band.**

- **D-228** **A CHECK WHOSE SUBJECT IS THE RENDERER SHOULD NOT DEPEND ON WHERE SPAWN IS.**
  `cullcheck` §2b puts the camera inside a cave, because a camera buried in solid rock sees the
  clear colour and the section's whole comparison degenerates to two pictures of nothing. It found
  that cave by walking the PLAYER'S OWN COLUMN. When D-226 lowered the world two and a half blocks
  to vanilla's real sea-level anchor, the spawn column stopped having a cave under it and the check
  went red — **reporting the occlusion flood for a change in the terrain**.
  It now spirals outward over the loaded columns to a radius of 24 and takes the first air pocket
  with a roof over it, and it still FAILS when there is no cave anywhere near, which is the honest
  form of the assertion rather than a skip.
  ⚠ **This is D-148 (*a test that runs at the origin tests the origin*) inside a check whose
  subject has nothing to do with position** — the third variant of it this session, after D-196
  (a check that runs at one preset tests that preset) and D-227 (a bound fitted to one seed passes
  at that seed). The general form is worth writing down once: **if a check picks ONE example, it is
  testing that example.** Pick many, or pick by property.

- **D-229** ⚠⚠ **W2's REFEREE HAD NEVER SEEN A VANILLA NUMBER, AND THE FIRST ONE IT SAW BROKE TWO
  THINGS.** `tools/noisecheck.mjs` shipped 162 assertions and every one of them was
  self-consistency or a hand-copied constant: MD5 against RFC 1321, Xoroshiro against a second
  copy of Xoroshiro written in the same file, analytic bounds, moments, determinism. The file
  said so in its own header and `docs/NEXT.md` carried the gap for four sessions. **D-219 is what
  the gap cost** — `FROZEN_TEMPERATURE_NOISE` built with octaves `[-3,-2,-1]` instead of
  `[-2,-1,0]`, written from memory in session 3, wrong for five sessions, icing over every frozen
  ocean, with all 162 assertions passing beside it.

  **THE ROUTE: reflection over Mojang's own bytecode, driven by the OFFICIAL server mappings.**
  The alternative on the table was reading constants out of the class files, which is what D-219
  itself did; that settles constants and cannot produce a single VALUE, so it was the fallback and
  not the goal. Instead `_scratch/mclite/ng_dump.js` downloads
  `piston-data.mojang.com/.../server.txt` (SHA-1 `e562f588…`, verified), parses the ProGuard
  mapping — 4,753 classes — resolves the twenty classes and forty members this needs, writes them
  to a properties file, and `NoiseDump.java` reflects on them against the same 1.18.2 server jar
  the golden world came off (SHA-1 `c8f83c56…`, D-199). No decompiler, no remapper, no
  third-party mapping set, and nothing reimplemented: every number in the dump is what Mojang's
  code returned. Four things had to be learned the hard way and are written down so the next
  person does not re-learn them: 1.18.2's `XoroshiroRandomSource` does not hold the two 64-bit
  words but **delegates to `Xoroshiro128PlusPlus`**; the obfuscated classes are in the DEFAULT
  package and are **signed**, so a dumper class beside them makes the JVM refuse to load them
  ("signer information does not match") and it has to live in a package of its own; **the server
  jar ships no `data/minecraft/worldgen/noise/*.json`** — those files are an EXPORT of
  `BuiltinRegistries.NOISE`, so the sixty parameter sets come out of the registry after
  `Bootstrap.bootStrap()`; and `NoiseParameters` cannot be touched before that bootstrap because
  its Codec reaches the registries.

  **WHAT WAS SAMPLED, AND WHY THAT.** The value of this stack is in the composition, so a hundred
  values from one noise would have proved almost nothing. `tools/golden/noise-golden-1.18.2.json`
  is **132 cases, 1,060 values, 67 KB**, and `noisecheck` §6 turns them into **1,593 exact
  comparisons**: the raw Xoroshiro stream from six seeds (`nextLong`, `nextInt`, `nextInt(bound)`
  over eight bounds including the powers of two that take the other branch, `nextDouble`,
  `nextFloat`, and the two seed words after `upgradeSeedTo128bit`); the whole `forkPositional`
  derivation — sixteen `fromHashOf` cases covering the MD5 path and fourteen `at(x,y,z)` cases,
  each recording both seed words AND the first two draws; `Mth.getSeed` on its own; the
  `LegacyRandomSource` streams from six seeds plus its scrambled 48-bit seed; `ImprovedNoise` from
  three different sources, its three origins and 22 samples each, deliberately including
  coordinates either side of the `3.3554432e7` wrap and either side of a 256-block permutation
  period; twelve `PerlinNoise` octave stacks with **their per-octave origins, nulls included**,
  because a zero amplitude means the octave was never built; sixteen `NormalNoise` cases on the
  real registry parameters at two world seeds, carrying the parameters themselves so MC-Lite's
  packed copy is checked too; and seven `PerlinSimplexNoise` cases — the three fixed-seed statics
  read **off `Biome`'s own fields**, their reconstructions, and the pre-D-219 octave list as a
  **negative control that MC-Lite must fail to reproduce**.

  ⚠ **THE FIRST DISAGREEMENT: `Mth.getSeed` MULTIPLIES IN 32 BITS AND MC-LITE DID NOT.** The Java
  is `long l = (long)(x * 3129871) ^ (long)z * 116129781L ^ (long)y` — the first product is
  `int * int`, computed in 32 bits and **only then** widened, while the second is a 64-bit
  multiply. `src/03b_noise.js` did both in 64 bits. That agrees with the game for every |x| under
  686 and disagrees everywhere else, which is why nothing had ever noticed: the check suite's
  positions were `(0,0,0)`, `(1,2,3)` and `(16,255,16)`. Of the golden vector's seven positions
  the four near the origin agreed and **all three of the far ones were wrong** — at
  `(1000, 64, -1000)` MC-Lite answered `-93387159076605` where vanilla answers
  `-13171143507709`. **The break point is exactly x = ±687**, because 686 × 3129871 is the last
  product that fits in an int.

  ⚠ **AND IT WAS SHIPPING.** `positionSeed` has no direct caller, but `XoroFactory.at` does, and
  `04h_surface.js` has two: `vertical_gradient`'s per-block coin flip — the speckled deepslate
  line and the bedrock roof and floor — and `SurfaceSystem.getSurfaceDepth`'s quarter-block
  jitter, which half the surface tree's conditions read. **MEASURED at x ≈ 10,000 (D-229), against the old
  arithmetic: 33.5% of the blocks in a 16-block gradient band flipped, and 8.2% of columns got a
  different surface depth.** Neither is visible and no check could have seen either, because a
  wrong random is still a random with the right distribution — the speckle looked exactly as
  speckled as vanilla's, in the wrong places. It is the third time this project has been bitten by
  a test that ran at the origin (D-152, D-196), and it is the first time the thing at stake was
  invisible by construction rather than merely unnoticed. Track G's features and carvers are the
  next callers, and they would have been placed from the wrong seed everywhere but a
  1,373-block-wide strip down the middle of the world.

  ⚠ **THE SECOND: `maxValue()` WAS EXACTLY HALF VANILLA'S, FOR ALL TWELVE NOISES.** Mojang's
  `PerlinNoise.maxValue()` is `edgeValue(2.0)` — each octave allowed ±2, not ±1. MC-Lite's was
  `edgeValue(1)`. The fix is **not** to widen the bound `noisecheck` §3 measures against, because
  the tight bound is what notices a missing octave and the loose one does not: vanilla's
  `maxValue()` is now implemented exactly, `edgeValue(d)` beside it, and MC-Lite's tighter bound
  keeps its own name, `Normal.analyticBound()`, with §3 pointed at that. Two quantities, two
  names, neither able to be mistaken for the other. Nothing in the game reads either.

  **AND WHAT AGREED.** Everything else, to the last bit: 1,593 comparisons, **0 disagreements**,
  doubles bit-for-bit and 64-bit words as BigInt with no tolerance anywhere — the seed upgrade,
  the `++` scrambler, Lemire's bounded draw with its rejection loop, the MD5 big-endian long
  boundary, `java.util.Random`'s two `nextInt` branches, the improved-Perlin permutation shuffle
  and its `p[i + j]` swap partner, `wrap()`, the `1.0181268882175227` second stack, the 1.18.2
  `(1/6)/expectedDeviation` normalisation, the octave nulls, and all three `Biome` statics —
  **including `FROZEN_TEMPERATURE_NOISE`, which is now proved by value rather than by a constant
  read off `<clinit>`, and which does NOT match the pre-D-219 list.** The twelve sampled noises'
  packed `firstOctave` and `amplitudes` also match `BuiltinRegistries.NOISE` exactly, which is the
  first time MC-Lite's own worldgen data has been checked against the registry rather than against
  a file extracted from the same jar.

  **THE CHECK SKIPS CLEANLY AND CANNOT PASS VACUOUSLY.** No dump in the tree prints a reason, the
  path it looked at and how to regenerate it, and §§1–5 still run — they cover all sixty noises
  where the dump covers twelve, and they hold with no reference at all. With the dump present, §6
  asserts the schema, the jar and mapping SHA-1s, a floor of 120 cases and 1,000 values, that
  **every value in the file was compared** (`compared === goldenValues`), that all sixteen case
  kinds are present, that the negative control still exists, and that an unknown case kind is a
  failure rather than a silent skip. Eleven anti-vacuity breaks (D-30) perturb the dump one family
  at a time — a long off by one, a double moved one ulp, an octave vanilla built declared absent,
  an amplitude changed, a `valueFactor` doubled, the negative control replaced by the right
  answer, a case kind renamed — and every one is caught. `noisecheck` goes from **162 assertions
  to 1,793**.

  ⚠ **WHAT IS STILL NOT COMPARED, said plainly rather than left to be discovered.** The other
  forty-eight noise fields (only their parameters are checked, by §3's bounds); `nextGaussian` and
  `nextBoolean`, which MC-Lite does not implement; `Simplex.get2`, the 3D-seeded low-octave branch
  that throws by design because no octave list in the game reaches it; and `Normal.analyticBound`,
  which has no vanilla counterpart by construction. Everything the dump does contain is compared
  exactly — there is no tolerance anywhere in §6, and there should never be one, because every
  algorithm in this file is deterministic integer or IEEE-754 arithmetic with no reordering.

- **D-233** ⚠ **A GROWING PLANT MAY HANG FROM ITS OWN BODY, AND OURS REFUSED TO.**
  `States.floorOk` and `States.ceilingOk` both ended with *"…or the neighbour is the SAME BLOCK,
  and that block stacks"* (D-165). The head and the body of a growing plant are **different
  blocks**: `cave_vines` hangs under `cave_vines_plant`. Vanilla's `GrowingPlantBlock.canSurvive`
  is `canAttachTo(n) && (n.is(headBlock) || n.is(bodyBlock) || n.isFaceSturdy(growthDirection))`,
  so D-140's write-time test in `Features.supported` refused every vine TIP and `setBlock`
  returned 0 without writing it. **A head survived only where the sampled body length was 0.**

  **MEASURED** (D-227's diagnosis, seed 1337): the golden 1.18.2 world has **4,286 vertical vine
  runs and 4,285 of them end in a `cave_vines` head**; MC-Lite had 703 runs, 170 with a head —
  every one exactly one block long — and 533 with none. `vanillacheck` §6 read `cave_vines`
  **0.38x** while `cave_vines_plant` was **1.15x** and the COLUMN count was right: the bodies were
  all there and the tips were missing. `environment_scan` and `block_column`'s `prioritize_tip`
  were both checked and are innocent.

  **THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE, `States.attachOk`**, and it is the tail of BOTH `floorOk` and
  `ceilingOk`, so `Features.supported`, `World.canSurvive` and `floatcheck` keep one
  implementation (D-169). Two cases and no more: the same block where that block really stacks
  (D-165), and the other half of its own growing plant.

  ⚠ **THE PAIRS ARE DERIVED, NOT TYPED.** Vanilla names every `GrowingPlantBodyBlock` after its
  head with a `_plant` suffix, so *X and X\_plant, where both are blocks* gives exactly the four
  families — cave vines, kelp, twisting vines, weeping vines — and a version bump moves them with
  no list to edit. The same rule skips `chorus_plant` correctly: there is no block called
  `chorus`, its head is `chorus_flower`, and its real rule is a CONNECTIVITY rule that a
  one-neighbour support class cannot state anyway. `big_dripleaf`/`big_dripleaf_stem` is the one
  pair no naming rule gives, so it is a NAMED entry beside `STACKS` and `pack-runtime`'s
  `CEILING_BLOCKS` — and a DIRECTED one, which is why the table holds *what may I attach to*
  rather than a family id: `BigDripleafBlock.canSurvive` takes a stem below the leaf, and
  `BigDripleafStemBlock.canSurvive` takes a stem or `#big_dripleaf_placeable` and **never the
  leaf**. (The stem's second clause — the block ABOVE it must be a stem or a leaf — is not
  implemented: a one-neighbour support class cannot state it, and the generator builds stems
  upward under a leaf so it never produces the arrangement that clause would refuse.)

  **THE WHOLE CLASS, walked and stated.** `cave_vines` and `weeping_vines` are ceiling class and
  were broken through `ceilingOk`; `twisting_vines` and `big_dripleaf` are floor class and were
  broken through `floorOk` — the dripleaf silently, with **0 of 99 leaves standing on their own
  stem** in 49 lush chunks against 116 of 213 after. `kelp`/`kelp_plant` were already unaffected
  because their support class is 0 (`pack-runtime`'s `supportClass` gives them no rule at all), and
  they are fixed here anyway so the class is right if that ever changes. `bamboo` is class 0 too
  and `bamboo_sapling` is not a body block. `sugar_cane` and `cactus` stack on THEMSELVES and were
  always right through D-165's exception. `chorus_flower`/`chorus_plant` are deliberately left
  alone, above.

  **RESULT, one tree, seed 1337, 240 chunks:** `cave_vines` **0.77/chunk → 2.90 (0.38x → 1.45x)**,
  `cave_vines_plant` 4.01 → 3.98 (1.15x → 1.14x) — the bodies did not move, the tips arrived. In
  49 lush chunks: **717 vine runs, 717 of them headed, 0 headless** (was 163/554), mean run 1.95
  → 2.71 blocks against vanilla's 2.75. Seed 4242's ledger carries no vine row at all (vanilla
  places under two a chunk there) and moved only in the third digit of `grass`, `glow_lichen` and
  `oak_planks`. ⚠ **THE RESIDUAL IS A COLUMN COUNT, NOT A SUPPORT RULE**: at 1.45x MC-Lite makes
  more, slightly shorter vine columns than vanilla — head-to-body 0.73 against vanilla's 0.57 —
  which is `cave_vine`'s `count 188` and its scan, and is D-223's business rather than this one's.

  **FENCED** in `floatcheck` §2f: the predicate asserted by NAME in both directions (a head on its
  own body ACCEPTED, a head on another family's body, on a leaf, and a dripleaf stem on its own
  leaf REFUSED), the derivation asserted to stay derived (nine partnered blocks, `chorus_plant`
  not among them), the WRITE-TIME path asserted through `Features.supported` rather than through
  `ceilingOk` again, and the POPULATION asserted over generated chunks — every vine run ends in a
  head. ⚠ **The walk leaves the origin**: seed 1337 has no lush cave near (0,0) — 169 chunks there
  hold FOUR vine runs — so §2f walks a named lush area, which is D-148 one more time. Three
  anti-vacuity breaks (D-30): the pre-D-233 tail put back regenerates the same chunks and MUST
  produce headless runs, an "everything with a partner attaches" rule MUST break the refusals, and
  the walk itself MUST find no runs at the origin. §2c and §2d, which judge the world against the
  packer's sets BY NAME rather than against `floorOk` (D-164), get the head/body pairs as their
  own written-out table for the same reason.

- **D-230** ⚠⚠ **THE COAST IS NOT ONE BLOCK LOW. IT IS HALF AS ROUGH, AND THE DIFFERENCE DECIDES
  WHETHER THE FIX IS A CONSTANT OR A DEVIATION.**

  D-225 dropped the world 2.5 blocks at sea level and five biomes with a shoreline gave a few
  points back: desert 97.1 → 94.4, jungle 95.2 → 91.2, plains 93.9 → 90.5, river 90.2 → 88.4,
  forest 95.2 → 94.7. `old_growth_birch_forest` sat at 77.5%, the worst row in `vanillacheck` §3,
  and had been low before the height fix too. This session went after those last few points.

  ── **FIRST: WHICH COLUMNS DISAGREE, AND WHY — THE SPLIT** ──

  ⚠ **A DISAGREEMENT IS A SURFACE-RULE BUG ONLY IF THE TWO ENGINES' GROUND IS AT THE SAME y.**
  §3 compares the TOP block, and the top block counts the sea. So a column whose terrain is one
  block lower than vanilla's floods, `grass_block` becomes `water`, and §2's top-block residual
  still reads **zero** because both engines' topmost block is at y = 62. The height error hides
  inside a number that looks like a rule error. The fix is a second height, computed by the same
  predicate on both sides: **GROUND** — the topmost block that is neither air, nor vegetation,
  nor a fluid, nor the ice/snow cap the surface rules lay on one. Split every disagreement on
  whether the two grounds are at the identical y and the answer is not ambiguous:

  | biome | overlap | per-column | rule-only | height-out |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | badlands | 85.6% | 67.0% | **0.00%** | 33.0% |
  | frozen_ocean | 91.4% | 69.9% | 0.26% | 29.8% |
  | old_growth_birch_forest | 77.5% | 72.9% | **0.20%** | 26.9% |
  | wooded_badlands | 90.1% | 74.0% | 0.82% | 25.2% |
  | swamp | 98.1% | 74.9% | 1.84% | 23.2% |
  | deep_frozen_ocean | 86.0% | 81.3% | 3.63% | 15.0% |
  | jungle | 91.2% | 82.6% | **0.75%** | 16.7% |
  | desert | 94.4% | 85.8% | **0.16%** | 14.0% |
  | river | 88.4% | 87.7% | **0.50%** | 11.8% |
  | plains | 90.5% | 90.4% | **0.55%** | 9.1% |
  | forest | 94.7% | 90.7% | **0.80%** | 8.5% |

  Over 61,440 golden columns at seed 1337, **361 (0.60%) disagree with the ground at the
  identical y, and 190 of those are `packed_ice -> water`** — the iceberg, which is a feature §8
  already drops, and 186 of the 190 are `deep_frozen_ocean` rather than the `frozen_ocean` §8
  used to name. At seed 4242 the rule-only figure is 0.50%. What is left after the iceberg is
  `dirt -> grass_block` ×33 (vanilla's `setDirtAt` under a tree MC-Lite did not grow — D-222's
  ledger, not this one), `orange_terracotta -> red_sand` ×31, `grass_block -> gravel` ×20 and a
  tail of single-digit rows. **`04h_surface.js` is not where the missing points are, and nothing
  in it was changed.** Not one of the five biomes D-225 moved has a rule-only figure above 0.80%.

  ⚠ **AND §3's `agree` COLUMN IS A HISTOGRAM OVERLAP, NOT A PER-COLUMN AGREEMENT.** It is
  `sum over blocks of min(vanilla count, mc count)`, so an engine that gets a biome's PROPORTIONS
  right while getting every individual column wrong scores 100%. **Swamp reads 98.1% by overlap
  and 74.9% by column.** The overlap number is not deleted — every named fence in §3 is set on it
  and re-anchoring them would be loosening bounds — but the per-column number is now printed
  beside it and the new blanket floor is set on it.

  ── **SECOND: THE HEIGHT, MEASURED WITHOUT CONDITIONING ON A HEIGHT** ──

  ⚠ **SELECTING COLUMNS BY VANILLA'S OWN SURFACE y BIASES A COMPARISON OF SURFACE y.** The
  residual regresses toward the mean of the selection and the number that comes out is a property
  of the selection. The honest conditioning is on the **INPUT the two engines share**: the offset
  spline value. Biome parity is 99.994%, so the climate fields agree; restrict to `|offset| ≤
  0.04` with no jaggedness and no terracing and MC-Lite's height is exactly `offsetToY`, so what
  is compared is the two maps and nothing else. In BOTH golden worlds:

  | | n | vanilla mean | vanilla sd | MC-Lite mean | MC-Lite sd | gap | spread |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | seed 1337 | 21,451 | 65.56 | **4.62** | 64.16 | **2.22** | −1.39 | **48%** |
  | seed 4242 | 18,561 | 65.19 | **4.68** | 63.98 | **2.65** | −1.21 | **57%** |

  **MC-Lite's sea-level surface is not DISPLACED from vanilla's. It is UNDER-DISPERSED.** The two
  p05s and p25s agree (60/60 and 63/63 at seed 1337); what is missing is the upper half — vanilla
  puts 52.5% of these columns at or above y = 66 and MC-Lite 22.7%. The −1.2 to −1.4 block mean
  gap IS that missing half, not an offset.

  ⚠ **SO THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG, AND THE REFEREE SAYS SO RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT.** Raising
  the anchor to zero the gap was tried at 64.0, 64.3, 64.5, 64.6 and 65.0 against both worlds. It
  does what the arithmetic says it does — at 64.5 the offset-conditioned gap is 0.00 in both
  worlds and the ledger mean rises in both — and it lifts the low end that is **already correct**:
  at +1 block the golden world's own swamp area gives **36.7% water where the real game gives
  62%**, and `surfcheck` §3b(e)'s at-or-below-sea fraction falls from 86.9% to **68.2%, under its
  floor of 70**. Those two bounds are the real game's numbers and they are not for loosening, so
  the correction is refused by the referee and not by a preference. The cause is deviation #1 —
  `base_3d_noise` is the term that carries the vertical variance — and D-172's stretch restores it
  above offset 0.2, where the curve has anchors to stretch between; at sea level it has one anchor
  and nothing to stretch. **`HEIGHT_CURVE` is unchanged.** The deviation is NAMED in §8 instead.

  ⚠ **AND D-225 CALIBRATED A GLOBAL CONSTANT OFF THE MOST HEIGHT-SENSITIVE BIOME IN THE LEDGER.**
  The swamp's clause fires at exactly y = 62 and nowhere else, so a half-block move swings its
  agreement by twenty points — and the two worlds want opposite directions: at seed 1337 MC-Lite's
  swamp ground runs +0.84 above vanilla's and at seed 4242 −1.07 below, which is why D-227 found
  the fix had overshot in the second world. A biome that amplifies is an instrument, not a target.

  ── **WHAT LANDED IN THE CHECK** ──

  **§2b — the sea-level band's SHAPE, pinned in colcheck §3c's sense.** Prints both distributions
  and asserts three things: the level gap in −2.5..+0.5, the median column residual within one
  block, and the spread ratio in 0.40..1.30 as a RATCHET. ⚠ **THE CEILING ON THE GAP IS MEASURED,
  NOT EXTRAPOLATED.** Putting D-225's old `[0.0, 66]` back was estimated at +1.24 from the anchor
  move; the run says **+0.89**, and a fence set on the estimate would have let the bug straight
  back through. It is +0.5, it fails on the 66 world, and it leaves a block and a half of room for
  a correction someone can justify later. The spread ratio reads 0.483 on that same 66 world —
  a thousandth from today's 0.481 while the level moves 2.3 blocks — which is the evidence that
  the two halves are separate claims.

  **§3 — the split, printed per biome, and the fence that stops a TRADE.** Every bound in §3 was
  per biome, and a per-biome bound cannot see a change that buys one biome with another: D-225
  improved four and cost five and no assertion in the file moved. The new fences are the
  **column-weighted MEAN across the whole ledger** — overlap ≥ 90 (93.16% at seed 1337, 95.33% at
  4242) and per-column ≥ 82 (86.57% / 90.00%) — plus **rule-only ≤ 1.5%** (0.60% / 0.50%), which
  is immune to a height change by construction and is therefore the number W6's rules are actually
  held to. ⚠ **THE MEAN IS A FENCE, NOT AN OPTIMISATION TARGET**, and the file says so: the 66
  world scores 91.91% overlap and **86.86% per-column, BETTER than today's 86.57**, because the
  mean cannot see that one biome's rule had become unreachable. §3's per-biome floor is what
  catches that, and both are needed.

  **§8** gains the two named deviations — the sea-level spread, and which side of the waterline a
  coastal column falls on — and the iceberg row is widened from `frozen_ocean` to the family,
  because the measurement says 186 of its 190 columns are `deep_frozen_ocean`.

  **§9** gains a break per new claim (12 of 12 now, was 10). `topBlock: netherrack` must move all
  three of §3's means, not just the per-biome loop. `gsquash` — a new golden-side mutation that
  pulls the answer key's terrain toward the waterline **about its own middle** — moves the spread
  ratio past 1.30 while the level gap stays inside its band, so §2b's dispersion pin has a break
  that is not the `dy` break wearing a different name; and `dy: 6` now also has to move the level
  pin. ⚠ Every one of them is applied to the ANSWER KEY, in §9's standing style.
