- **D-415** **THE AUDIT SESSION: MOBS WERE DRAWN UPSIDE DOWN, THE SKY HAD A LINE IN IT, LAVA HAD
  NEVER MET WATER, AND "NEW WORLD" GAVE YOU THE OLD ONE.** 20 Sept 2026, session 51. Dan, awake
  for five minutes in the shipped build: *"using certain mob eggs doesnt work, the ones that do
  their sprites are mangled beyond belief… cows are upside down and have no coherent animations…
  hitting erase current world and create new one still slots you back with the old world… candles
  dont have the 4 in one block function… stuff like lava spawned with the world doesnt flow auto,
  water and lava have a genuinely incoherent interaction… when you turn left your held items
  transfer to the middle of the screen… random patches of air underwater… toggling smooth
  lighting does nothing… some lava pools in worldgen arent contained… make it possible to turn
  off that white line in the sky."* Every one of those was a real fault except the candles, and
  the candles are the reason the rest of this entry can be trusted: they were **checked and found
  already correct** (states stack 1→2→3→4 through `Player.placeBlock`, and the four models bake
  10/20/30/40 quads — screenshotted). A report is a lead, not a verdict.
  · **Mobs (the big one).** `ER.emitMobLayer`'s own header had named the gap and asked the first
  session with a real browser to settle it: `LivingEntityRenderer.render` applies
  `scale(-1, -1, 1)` and `translate(0, -1.501, 0)` before a single model part is posed, and this
  engine applied neither. Entity model boxes are authored **Y-DOWN from a point 1.501 blocks above
  the feet** — a humanoid's legs run y 12..24, and 1.501 − 24/16 = 0.001 is why its feet touch the
  floor — so without the flip every mob in the game was upside down and sunk into the ground. The
  yaw half was already paid for by a convention gap: vanilla rotates by `180 − yawMC`, this
  engine's yaw is Minecraft's minus 180 (`Cam.forward` is `(sin y, sin p, −cos y)`), so
  `180 − yawMC` **is** `−yaw` and the existing rotation differed from the right one only by
  negating X and Y. `ER.basePoseFor` / `ER.OWED_BASE_POSE` (the two projectile layers keep none,
  named not guessed).
  · **And the mob yaw was in the wrong units entirely.** `07k_goals.js` wrote `e.yaw` as
  MINECRAFT's yaw in DEGREES (`atan2(-dx, dz) * 180/PI`); `ER.build` reads it as `Math.cos(e.yaw)`
  — radians, this engine's convention. A mob walking north was drawn as if its heading were 180
  radians. `Combat.mobAttack`'s knockback read the same field through a second wrong conversion.
  · **And nothing ticked the walk cycle.** `ER.setupAnimDelta` has been correct since D-263 and
  had never been called with anything: `ER.build` passed `anim: null`. `LivingEntity.aiStep`'s own
  two lines now run in `EL.tickOne` (`animationSpeed` eased 0.4 toward `min(1, dist*4)`,
  `animationPosition` accumulating) and `ER.animOf` interpolates them the way vanilla does
  (the swing is wound BACK by the unplayed part of the tick, not lerped). `netHeadYaw`/`headPitch`
  stay 0 and are named: nothing turns a mob's head independently of its body yet.
  · **Four bugs in the MODEL EXTRACTOR, which is why the boxes were wrong under the pose.**
  `tools/extract-models.mjs` had no `fload` rule, so a float PARAMETER was invisible and `fadd`
  folded the two literals either side of the hole: `PartPose.offset(1.9F, 12.0F + yOffset, 0.0F)`
  became `(13.9, 0)` — one number short — and every humanoid in the game shipped with its arms
  beside it and its legs in its chest. Fixing that exposed three more: a shared factory's
  arguments must be indexed by LOCAL SLOT and not by the order the literals arrived (`slotArgs`);
  a layer paired straight to a hoisted factory takes its sheet size from the `LayerDefinition
  .create(mesh, 64, 64)` call site, and 65 layers had been shipping a **0×0 sheet**; the no-arg
  `CubeListBuilder.mirror()` was unrecognised, so every left arm and left leg lost its mirror
  flag; `CubeDeformation.extend(0.5F)` wiped the operand run, so 43 hats came out as zero-sized
  boxes; `addBox(String, FFFFFF)` was unrecognised, so the cow's two horns were LOST and its head
  shipped under the name `left_horn`; and the part name is the FIRST string of the chain, not the
  last (`getChild("head").addOrReplaceChild("hat", …)`). 1,102 boxes → 1,111, partial 223 → 21,
  no 0×0 sheets, and `animcheck`'s "zombie.hat unchanged" assertion — which had passed only
  because the hat box was zero-sized and could not move — is now vanilla's own
  `hat.copyFrom(head)`.
  · **The held item that walked off the screen.** `Input.applyLook` wraps yaw into (−180, 180];
  `Player.tick` eases `yBob` toward it THE SHORT WAY ROUND. Both are right; together they let
  `yBob` settle a full turn away from the yaw it chases, and `Hand3D.pose` — the one place that
  SUBTRACTS them — read −360, times 0.1, **per seam crossing, accumulating**. `H3.swayYaw` wraps
  the difference; `yBob` is deliberately left unwrapped (wrapping it would put a 360° step between
  `yBobO` and `yBob` on the tick it happened, and the renderer lerps between them).
  · **"New world" gave you the old world.** The title button cleared `localStorage` and the edit
  map by hand and re-entered `boot()`, whose second pass calls `Save.load()` again — which returns
  false at its FIRST line and therefore never touches `S.playerState` or the sky. The old player
  was still in the module and was restored, and the seed box was still showing the old world's
  seed. `Save.reset()` forgets the blocks, the player, the sky and the loaded flag; the button
  now returns to the title screen with a fresh random seed showing and the climate rows unlocked,
  which is also what vanilla does (erasing a world does not start one).
  · **Lava had never met water.** `LiquidBlock.shouldSpreadLiquid` (source → obsidian, flowing →
  cobblestone, looking at the OPPOSITE of each flow direction, so DOWN means "water above me")
  and `LavaFluid.spreadTo` (lava falling INTO water → stone) did not exist at all — there was no
  way to make cobblestone or obsidian in this world. ⚠ The test runs **synchronously on the
  neighbour change**, as `LiquidBlock.neighborChanged` does, not on the scheduled tick: lava ticks
  every 30 and water every 5, so a water source placed over lava gets six flow ticks first and the
  first one replaces the lava outright.
  · **And worldgen's fluids had never been woken.** A fluid only moves when something schedules a
  tick, and only a player's edit ever did — so a lava pool with a cave cut into one side sat there
  with a flat vertical face for ever and no lavafall in this game had ever run. Vanilla's
  `markPosForPostprocessing` is the same idea; `Behave.scanNewColumn` wakes only the cells that
  can actually go somewhere. **Measured over 169 chunks of seed 1337: 49,605 water cells and
  10,541 lava cells, of which 13 and 60 have an air neighbour.** Waking 0.43 cells a chunk is
  nothing; waking all sixty thousand would be a scheduler with 27,000 entries in it.
  · **Two worldgen features wrote holes.** `LakeFeature` walks its shell BEFORE it writes anything
  and returns false — places no lake at all — if any shell cell in the lower half is not solid or
  any in the upper half is liquid. That walk is the entire reason a vanilla lava lake has a stone
  wall on every side, and it was missing: the barrier pass only CONVERTS solid cells, so a lake
  rolled against a cave got no wall there and poured out of the hole. And `monster_room` gated on
  `heightmapY(0, …)` — WORLD_SURFACE, which under an ocean is `seaLevel + 1` however shallow the
  seabed is — so a dungeon dug into a seabed passed the gate, got no wall on its water side, and
  left a five-by-four pocket of air with the sea sitting on it. **Air cells directly under water
  over 169 chunks: 67 → 0.** It is now OCEAN_FLOOR, asked at the four corners as well as the
  centre, which is vanilla's floor-and-ceiling solidity test expressed as a pure function (D-141).
  · **The white line in the sky, and the option Dan asked for.** Vanilla runs
  `FogRenderer.setupFog(camera, FOG_SKY, viewDistance)` before `renderSky`; the sky disc sits 16
  blocks above the eye and runs out to a radius of 512, so its far rim arrives at the horizon as
  pure fog colour. Without it the disc is a flat slab of biome sky colour that STOPS at pitch 0
  where the clear colour takes over: a hard, dead-level line across the screen. ⚠ Fogging it
  needed the disc REBUILT. Projecting vanilla's nine-vertex fan through the frame's own
  `skyViewProj` at pitch 0 gives **w = 0 for the centre vertex** — it is the zenith, exactly in
  the plane through the eye — so every triangle has a vertex at infinity and nothing can be
  interpolated across it: the first attempt washed the whole sky to fog colour and the debug
  render showed a constant 512 at every pixel. `Sky.buildSkyDiscMesh` is the same surface in
  geometric rings (radii even in `log r`, because screen height goes as `1/r`), with the centre
  fan's degenerate triangles confined to `r < 8`, which projects off the top of the screen at
  exactly the angles where the degeneracy exists. The sun and moon are NOT fogged and that is a
  named deviation: at 76.8 blocks of fog on the Celeron preset, vanilla's rule would erase them.
  `Settings.horizonFade` (Video → Horizon Fade) is the switch Dan asked for; ON is the fix.
  · **Smooth Lighting really did do nothing worth seeing, and now does.** The option has been
  wired to `ao` alone since the menu existed, with a comment claiming "AO is the visible half of
  it". Measured: toggling it changed **3.9%** of a forest frame — AO only darkens the corners of
  concave geometry. What makes vanilla's Smooth Lighting unmistakable is the LIGHT, per vertex:
  each one takes the mean of the cells touching it, so a torch, a doorway or an overhang gets a
  gradient instead of a hard per-face step. `cornerLight` reuses the eight neighbour reads AO
  already makes; two cells merge only if their four corner lights agree as well. **Measured:
  +8.8% mesh time and +0.16% quads** (500 sections, seed 1337) — the merge barely moves because
  the key already carried the face's own light. Toggling now changes **11.4%** of the same frame.
  · **Checks:** `behavcheck` §6b (obsidian/cobblestone/stone, with water BELOW a capped source as
  the anti-vacuity — the case `d.getOpposite()` deliberately ignores); `savecheck` §8c
  (`Save.reset` forgets the player and the sky, and a reload after it does not resurrect them);
  `facecheck` §4c (the four corner lights, the exact mean of 15,0,0,0 = 3, and uniform light
  giving byte-identical output in both modes as anti-vacuity); `animcheck` §2 corrected to
  `hat.copyFrom(head)`; `extract-models` gained a short-row detector that DROPS a part whose
  box/pose/rot list came up short instead of printing an empty TSV cell a reader parses as 0.
  · **Found, NOT done:** the spider's eight legs have no `setupAnim` (vanilla's `SpiderModel`
  sets their `zRot`/`yRot`, so they stand out as straight bars) and its leg builder is read twice
  under one name with the texOffs lost; mob eggs are still a closed set of six types, because 96
  entity types have no bytecode-measured gravity/drag (`tools/_travel-caller-sweep.mjs` is the
  start of that job); the WebGPU backend has no sky pass at all, so the horizon fade is WebGL2's
  alone; `netHeadYaw`/`headPitch` are 0 until something turns a mob's head.

- **D-416** **THE SPIDER: ITS OWN `setupAnim`, AND THE EXTRACTOR BUG THAT MEANT IT HAD THE WRONG
  LEGS TO POSE.** 20 Sept 2026, session 51, straight after D-415 and named in it as found-not-done.
  · **The extraction first, because a pose on the wrong boxes proves nothing.** `SpiderModel`
  builds TWO leg shapes — `create().texOffs(18,0).addBox(-15,-1,-1,16,2,2)` for the right side
  and the same at `-1` for the left — `astore`s each, and `aload`s them four times apiece.
  `tools/extract-models.mjs` knew about hoisted builders (the creeper's and pig's legs), but it
  recorded only the raw six box numbers and read `tex`/`mirror` from variables the `addBox`
  handler had ALREADY consumed and reset — so every reuse came out at texOffs (0, 0) with no
  mirror flag — and it left the boxes on `boxAccum`, so the FIRST part to use a hoisted builder
  emitted every box built so far under its own name. The spider therefore shipped **twelve** parts
  with `right_hind_leg` in it TWICE (once at x −15 and once at x −1, the LEFT leg's box wearing
  the right leg's name) and seven legs at the wrong texture. A stored builder is a finished
  builder: it takes its whole `boxAccum` with it and leaves none behind, and an `aload` hands the
  list back. 11 parts, all eight legs at texOffs(18, 0), right at −15 and left at −1. ⚠ The left
  legs are NOT mirrored and that was checked in the bytecode rather than assumed — 1.18.2's spider
  has no `mirror()` call, unlike every humanoid.
  · **Then the pose.** `elg.a(T,FFFFF)` read instruction by instruction (field names from the
  constructor's own `getChild` strings): a base `zRot` of ±π/4 on the outer leg pairs and
  ±0.58119464 on the middle two, a base `yRot` of ±π/4 and ±π/8 with the FRONT pair's sign
  reversed, then `-(cos(limbSwing·0.6662·2 + phase)·0.4)·amount` added to `yRot` and
  `|sin(limbSwing·0.6662 + phase)·0.4|·amount` added to `zRot`, at phases 0, π, π/2, 3π/2 — the
  lift at HALF the swing's frequency and through `abs`, so a leg rises once per cycle rather than
  twice. Right legs take `+delta`, left legs `−delta`.
  · **`ER.modelKindOf`, and why it is not a type list.** `left_front_leg`, `right_front_leg`,
  `left_hind_leg` and `right_hind_leg` belong to the spider AND the quadruped, so the name-keyed
  `setupAnimDelta` was giving a spider a cow's trot on four of its eight legs and leaving the
  other four rigid. The family is now read off the parts a layer HAS — eight legs including
  `left_middle_front_leg` is a spider, arms and legs is a humanoid, front and hind legs is a
  quadruped — so a layer that matches none is left at REST (D-139) instead of being posed by
  whichever branch shared a name.
  · **Vanilla ASSIGNS where this file ADDS, and the two are the same number here** because every
  spider leg's rest rotation is zero. That is a fact about the extracted data, so `animcheck`
  asserts it before it asserts anything about the angles.
  · **Checks:** `animcheck` §3b — 11 parts, no duplicate name, every leg at texOffs(18, 0), a
  zero rest rotation, all eight legs splayed even when STANDING (the base angles, at amplitude 0)
  and all eight moving again when walking, the two body boxes never posed, the hind and
  middle-hind pairs on different phases, `modelKindOf` answering for all three families, and
  `left_front_leg` posed differently as a spider than as a quadruped. 60 assertions, 0 failures.
  · **Screenshotted:** a spawned spider is a body with eight legs under it, not a bar.

- **D-417** **A MOB MAY NOT MOVE ITSELF: `Ai.stepToward` WAS TELEPORTING EVERY MOB PAST THE
  COLLISION SWEEP, AND THE SWEEP WAS NEVER AT FAULT.** 20 Sept 2026, session 52. Dan, playing the
  shipped build: *"mobs even in their crude form phase thru blocks"*.
  ▶ **THE CAUSE, AND IT IS A CLASS AND NOT A MOB.** `Ai.stepToward` wrote `e.x`, `e.y` and `e.z`
  outright — a teleport of a fraction of a block per tick — so **nothing a mob did had ever been
  through `Ph.move`**. Anything that writes a POSITION instead of a VELOCITY is invisible to every
  collision test ever written, because the test is never called. `Ph.move` itself, its step-up, its
  fall-distance bookkeeping and `entlistcheck`'s own trajectory proof were all correct throughout.
  ▶ **THE LAW IS THE REFEREE'S, AND IT IS NOT GUESSABLE.** No javap exists on the Linux VM this
  session ran on (JRE 11 only), so the five classes were extracted from the jar with `jarlib` and
  disassembled in the cloud container, which is STATE §0's own sanctioned reason to use it.
  · `bcu` (`JumpControl`): `jump()` sets a flag, `tick()` does `mob.setJumping(flag)` and clears
  it. A jump is a BOOLEAN the travel step consumes, never a velocity write.
  · `bcw.a()` (`MoveControl.tick`), MOVE_TO branch, offsets 198–497: `operation = WAIT`; arrive
  under `2.500000277905201E-7`, `setZza(0)`, return; else `setYRot(rotlerp(yRot, atan2(d1,d0)·
  57.2957763671875 − 90, 90))`, `setSpeed(speedModifier · MOVEMENT_SPEED)`, and jump when
  `d2 > maxUpStep && d0²+d1² < max(1, bbWidth)` **or** the shape it stands in has its top above
  its feet and is neither a door nor a fence. The final else is `setZza(0)` — the WAIT branch.
  · **`aya.r(F)` (`Mob.setSpeed`) is `super.setSpeed(f); this.setZza(f);`** — the movement-speed
  attribute is ALSO the forward input, so a mob's acceleration goes as the **square** of it. A
  zombie's 0.23 gives 0.23 × 0.23 × (0.216/f³), not 0.23. Nothing but the bytecode says so, and
  the roster was passing invented blocks-per-tick numbers (0.05, 0.06) while `SpiderAttackGoal`
  already passed a real modifier (1.0): two units live in one file since D-416.
  · `axk.g(axk)` (`Entity.push`): `d2 = absMax(d0,d1)`; if `>= 0.01`, `d2 = sqrt(d2)` — the square
  root of the max, which is an oddity that is in the bytecode and is therefore the rule — then
  normalise, clamp `1/d2` to 1, scale by 0.05, and push both parties horizontally.
  · `axk.bm()` (`isInWall`): a box `width · 0.8` across and 1e-6 tall at the eye, against any
  suffocating cell. `axy.h(dpo)` (`travel`) is the method `landTick` already ports for the player.
  ▶ **WHAT CHANGED.** `Ph.travelMob` is `LivingEntity.travel` for an entity whose input comes from
  its move control; `Ai.stepToward` is now `MoveControl.tick`'s MOVE_TO branch and moves nothing;
  `EL.tickMob` runs age → combat timers → fluid state → **`e.zza = 0`** (the WAIT branch) → goals
  → travel → push → suffocate, and the ordering of all three of the middle steps matters. The
  roster's speeds are vanilla's modifiers. `FloatGoal` requests a jump instead of writing `vy`.
  ▶ **THE WAIT BRANCH IS NOT A DETAIL.** Without `e.zza = 0` before the goals, a mob keeps
  accelerating on the last order it was ever given: `goalcheck` found it as a baby cow told to
  stop three blocks from its mother walking into her, for ever.
  ▶ **`goalcheck` NEEDED 14 ASSERTIONS REWRITTEN**, and that is the finding, not the chore: they
  asserted that ticking a goal MOVES a mob, which is the bug written down as a test. A fixture
  that ticks a goal must travel too, or it is testing a mob vanilla would have left standing still.
  ▶ **Checks:** `tools/mobmovecheck.mjs`, new, in `suite.mjs`. The headline rule is stated as a
  CLASS — *after a tick, no living entity's box may overlap a full cube* — and its break restores
  the pre-D-417 teleport and watches it escape a sealed stone box. 37 assertions, 4 breaks.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `mobmovecheck`, `goalcheck` (137), `aicheck`, `entlistcheck`, `physcheck`,
  `movecheck`, `spawncheck`, `combatcheck`, `entitycheck`, `mobboxcheck`, `tickcheck`, `gatecheck`,
  `stagecheck`, `pistoncheck` all green. `node build.mjs` exit 0.

- **D-418** **AZALEA TREES ON WATER: `root_system` HAD NO GROUND TEST, AND WHAT SHIPPED WAS A
  CANOPY WITH NO TRUNK.** 20 Sept 2026, session 52. Dan: *"theres a bug where azalea trees spawn
  on water"*.
  ▶ **REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED.** Seed 1337, a badlands at (−42, 67, 68): a pond at y 62 and
  **51 azalea blocks in the air above it with no log anywhere in the column.** `heightmapY(0,…)`
  is `max(h, sea) + 1` — the cell ABOVE the water — the feature planted the tree there, the tree's
  own `isFree` test then refused every LOG (water is not free) and passed every LEAF.
  ▶ **THE RULE IS `cyr`'s, READ OUT OF THE JAR THIS SESSION.** `RootSystemFeature.place`
  (`cyr.a(cxi)`) refuses unless the origin is air. `placeDirtAndTree` (`cyr.a(cbn,cqr,dat,Random,
  gj$a,gj)`), offsets 53–88: `if (level.getFluidState(below).is(LAVA) || !level.getBlockState(
  below).getMaterial().isSolid()) return false;` — **a return false for the whole feature, not a
  continue to the next candidate height**. `spaceForTree` (`cyr.a(cbn,dat,gj)`) walks
  `required_vertical_space_for_tree` cells up and tests each against `isAllowedTreeSpace(state, i,
  allowed_vertical_water_for_tree)` (`cyr.a(cov,int,int)`): air always; otherwise `i + 1 <=
  allowedVerticalWater && isWater`. Both numbers are read from the configured feature (3 and 2 for
  the azalea), not typed.
  ▶ **THE ORIGIN'S OWN `isAir` TEST IS DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED.** The origin is in a CAVE, and a
  cave is a 240-block random walk no point query can answer (D-213). The placement's own
  `environment_scan` with `allowed_search_condition: air` guarantees it one layer up, where the
  question is pure. Named in the code rather than left as a difference.
  ▶ **RESULT: 51 → 0**, with the azalea count down 6.6% (2179 → 2035) — the feature still runs.
  ▶ **THE CHECK IS THE CLASS, STATED ON THE WORLD.** `tools/featgroundcheck.mjs`: *every connected
  component of blocks a feature ADDED INTO AIR must touch something that is not air.* No
  per-feature list, no predicate table, no update when a feature is added — a trunk touches dirt, a
  canopy its trunk, a lily pad water, an ore vein stone; a canopy with no trunk touches nothing.
  Which blocks are the feature's is decided by generating the same 121 chunks TWICE, with features
  on and off, and diffing: the generator is asked which blocks it owns.
  ▶ **"ADDED INTO AIR", NOT "CHANGED", AND THE FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG ABOUT IT.** Judging every
  changed cell flagged 319 components; every one was a carver artefact — a lone stone voxel left
  standing in a cave, recoloured to diorite by an ore blob, which was already floating as TERRAIN
  before any feature ran. A feature that REPLACES a block inherits whatever held that block up.
  ▶ **THE CLAIM IS SCOPED TO AT-OR-ABOVE SEA LEVEL, AND THE SCOPE IS D-213's.** Above the sea the
  terrain a placement sees is pure and the verdict is exact; below it the world is carved. The
  underground count (4) is printed on every run and carried by KW-25.
  ▶ **THE AUDIT FOUND A SECOND CAUSE AND IT IS BIGGER — KW-25.** `World.setBlock` asks
  `States.rule` first and falls back to the support CLASS; `Features.setBlock` only ever asks the
  class. **All 13,799 feature-placed blocks that carry a survival rule carry a JAR rule — zero are
  judged by the class alone — and 12 of them stand where the live rule will not have them.** That
  is D-346's own shape one door along. NOT fixed this session and the reason is stated: the fix is
  a level interface for `surviveRuleInner` (440 lines; 27 of its 40 rules need only
  `getBlock`/`loadedAt`, the other 13 need light, tags or the grow helpers), and it carries two
  rulings with it. §3 of the check measures it and asserts nothing, because a claim scoped
  narrowly enough to pass would have had zero blocks left in it (D-305).
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** the guard disabled reproduces the failure (`azalea_leaves at -38,66,70`) and
  restored clears it. `featgroundcheck`, `featcheck`, `floatcheck`, `wgcheck`, `surfcheck`,
  `supportcheck`, `behavcheck`, `worldcheck`, `coherecheck`, `gencheck`, `cavecheck` green.
  ⚠ `vanillacheck` SKIPPED here — the 13,307-chunk pregen is on Dan's PC; it runs at close-out.

- **D-419** **THE HOPPER — AND `guicheck` HAD NO REPORT BLOCK, SO IT COULD NOT FAIL.**
  20 Sept 2026, session 52, QUEUE row 1's next unit.

  `titleLabelX`; `HopperScreen` overrides nothing, so copying D-414's own centring line would have

  ▶ **THE MACHINE, WHICH IS THE HALF A SCREEN CANNOT SHOW.** `BlockEntities.tickHopper` is
  `HopperBlockEntity.tryMoveItems`: push then pull, both in the same tick (`|=`, not `else`),
  exactly ONE item, then an eight-tick cooldown. A hopper's throughput is 2.5 items a second and
  every sorter, feed and clock built on one depends on it. `ENABLED` is inverted — a hopper is
  enabled when it is NOT powered — and a powered hopper still OPENS.

  {0}, DOWN → {2, 1}, any side → {1}. So a hopper on top feeds the ingredient, one on the side
  feeds the fuel, one underneath takes the result and the spent bucket and never the ingredient.
  The insert goes through **`Menu.furnaceSetItem`** — the door D-414 named for exactly this caller
  — so a new ingredient restarts the cook and re-reads its length.
  ▶⚠⚠ **`guicheck` HAD NO REPORT BLOCK AT ALL, AND HAD NOT HAD ONE FOR SOME TIME.** Every `ok()`
  in it pushed its message into `fails` and nothing ever read the array: the file printed its
  sections, exited 0, and the suite counted it green whatever the pixels said. The suite's own
  "⚠ N check stages REPORTED NO ASSERTION COUNT and contribute nothing to the total" line had been
  naming it every run. **That is D-305 reached by OMISSION, which is the more dangerous route: a
  file with 259 correct assertions in it looks exactly like a working one.**
  ▶ **AND §4f WAS AN EMPTY SECTION.** D-414 cited `guicheck` §4f as the furnace screen's pixel
  proof; §4f was four lines of comment and no body. Written now — and the moment the report block
  existed it failed twice, both real: the furnace's **result slot has no 18×18 shadow corner**
  (vanilla draws it in a larger recess, measured 24 × 24 at (112, 31) with the slot centred four
  pixels inside), and the section's own anti-vacuity break was too weak (one pixel inside a
  16-pixel field of flat grey is still grey; a whole slot-pitch is a break). The recess is now
  asserted on its own terms rather than the rule being loosened.
  ▶ **Checks:** `tools/hoppercheck.mjs` (36 assertions, 5 breaks) — the one that matters measures
  the RATE over 100 ticks, because a hopper that drained a stack in a tick would pass any "did the
  item arrive" test; the break sets the cooldown to 0 and watches it move 64. `guicheck` §4f/§4g.

- **D-420** **THE DISPENSER AND THE DROPPER: ONE BLOCK WITH TWO ENDINGS, AND JAVA EDITION'S
  QUASI-CONNECTIVITY.** 20 Sept 2026, session 52, QUEUE row 1's second unit this session.
  ▶ **THEY SHARE EVERYTHING BUT THE ENDING.** State, screen, 3 × 3 container, trigger and
  four-tick delay are one; `dispenseFrom` differs. A DROPPER puts one item INTO the container it
  faces (and throws only when there is none); a DISPENSER never inserts — with no registry entry
  it is `DefaultDispenseItemBehavior`, which throws, into a chest's face if there is one. A check
  that only asserted "the item left the block" would pass either one behaving as the other, so
  `dispensercheck` §4 and §5 are the same scene with the two blocks swapped.
  ▶⚠⚠ **`hasNeighborSignal(pos) || hasNeighborSignal(pos.above())` — THE `pos.above()` TERM IS
  NOT A TYPO.** It is Java Edition's quasi-connectivity, and every BUD and every piston door in
  the game is built on it. A clone that dropped it would look identical on a lever and break every
  contraption. `TRIGGERED` is a LATCH, not a level: it is what makes the block fire ONCE on the
  rising edge instead of every tick the lever is down.
  ▶ **`getRandomSlot` IS RESERVOIR SAMPLING, NOT "the first non-empty".** A dispenser with two
  stacks fires from both, which is what makes one full of different items a randomiser. Measured
  uniform over 9,000 draws.
  ▶ **WIRED AT THE ONE DOOR.** `Rs.updateDispensers` settles inside `Redstone`'s own `settle`,
  for `Piston.update`'s stated reason: a second entry point would arm a dispenser twice on one
  change, and a dispenser armed twice fires twice off one lever. The four-tick fire lands in
  `Behave.scheduledTick`, the one place a scheduled tick lands.
  ▶ **AND THE HOPPER'S `enabled` PROPERTY IS WRITTEN NOW.** It was on `BE.HOPPER_OWED` as of
  D-419: the transfer asked the signal directly and the property was left lying, so a hopper
  behaved as powered while F3 said otherwise. One question, one answer, one place.
  ▶ **Checks:** `tools/dispensercheck.mjs` (37 assertions, 4 breaks), `guicheck` §4h — which also
  asserts from the other side that the shipped blob carries a `dispenser` sheet and NO `dropper`
  sheet, because vanilla ships none and a second copy would be a lie about the jar.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `dispensercheck`, `hoppercheck`, `guicheck` (275), `furnacecheck`, `chestcheck`,
  `usecheck`, `invcheck`, `behavcheck`, `pistoncheck`, `tickcheck`, `entlistcheck`, `combatcheck`,
  `mobmovecheck`, `gatecheck`, `stagecheck` green. `node build.mjs` exit 0.

- **D-421** — **THE BLOCK ENTITIES IN THE WORLD: A PLACED CHEST IS A THING YOU CAN SEE.**
  ▶ **THE HOLE, MEASURED RATHER THAN SUSPECTED.** `Mesher.modelQuadCount` on the default state
  gives **6 for `stone` and 0 for `chest`, `trapped_chest`, `ender_chest`, every bed, every
  banner, every sign and every shulker box.** Their block models are `builtin/entity` and bake
  nothing on purpose, because vanilla draws them from a BLOCK-ENTITY RENDERER — which this
  engine had never had. **Nine units of G19b (D-403..D-420) built container SCREENS over a block
  that was a hole in the world**, and every check stayed green because not one of them ever asked
  what the world looked like where a chest stood. That is D-303/D-304's shape again, and this
  time the invisible thing was the block the whole stage was about.
  ▶ **IT IS THE MOB PATH, NOT A NEW ONE.** `ER.emitMobLayer` already poses a hierarchy of boxes
  and stamps each face with its own atlas slice; a chest is three such boxes. So D-421 decides
  WHICH layer, at WHAT yaw, with WHAT lid angle, and hands all three to the emitter every mob
  already goes through: no shader, no vertex format, no backend method, no second buffer.
  `ER.BE_WORLD` is the drawn table, `ER.BE_WORLD_OWED` the named-not-silent remainder, and
  `beworldcheck` §1 fails if a block-entity block is in neither.
  ▶ **THE LAW IS THE JAR'S** (`esu` = ChestRenderer, `cmx` = ChestLidController, disassembled in
  the container — STATE §0's sanctioned reason, no javap on the PC):
  `translate(.5,.5,.5) · YP.rotationDegrees(-facing.toYRot()) · translate(-.5,-.5,-.5)`, then
  `o = getOpenness(partial); o = 1-o; o = 1-o³; lid.xRot = lock.xRot = -(o·π/2)`.
  ▶ **THE PIVOT IS CARRIED BY THE ORIGIN.** The emitter rotates about the model origin and has no
  pivot argument; rotating about the block centre is the same geometry translated by `C - R(C)`,
  and the origin is a translation. `ER.beWorldOrigin` is that arithmetic alone, so a check can ask
  it directly rather than infer it from a vertex.
  ▶ **TWO REAL BUGS, BOTH FOUND BY THE NEW CHECK BEFORE DAN COULD SEE THEM.**
  (a) **THE LID TOOK ELEVEN TICKS, NOT TEN.** `openness` is a Java `float` and `0.1f` is
  0.100000001490116 — a hair MORE than a tenth, so ten of them land on 1.0 and the clamp fires.
  JavaScript's double 0.1 is a hair LESS, ten land on 0.9999999999999999, and the chest is 10%
  slow in both directions for ever. `Math.fround` in `BE.tickLid` is the whole fix, and counting
  the ticks is how it was found rather than argued about.
  (b) **THE FACING ROTATION HAD THE WRONG SIGN**, and it was green on north and south, because a
  180-degree error is invisible on the axis it mirrors. An east-facing chest had its lock on its
  west face. `beworldcheck` §3 tests all FOUR facings by asking which side the LOCK — the chest's
  front fitting — sticks out on, which is a question a sign error cannot survive.
  ▶ **A REFEREE TRIP PAID FOR A SECOND DEBT.** D-413 named `ChestType.RIGHT -> FIRST` as its one
  transcribed-not-refereed fact ("no javap here"). There is javap here now: `ceo.g` is
  `SINGLE -> SINGLE, RIGHT -> FIRST, else SECOND`. The transcription was right; it is a fact now.
  ▶ **Checks:** `tools/beworldcheck.mjs` (53 assertions, 4 breaks) for the arithmetic, and
  `becheck` §6 for the PICTURE — a chest placed in a pit in front of the player, mined back out,
  and its lid opened, each measured against a control. That section cost two traps worth writing
  down: the camera must be tilted DOWN before the control (a chest is knee-high, and at pitch 0
  the whole experiment is below the viewport — it reported 5 px of change from placing a chest AND
  digging a pit), and a shot must be settled against wall-clock time, not a frame count.
  ▶ **OWED, NAMED:** a trapped chest and an ender chest draw the NORMAL chest's sheet.
  `mob-geometry.json` carries one sheet per layer and vanilla picks among nine chest materials at
  runtime; `extract-mob-textures.mjs` already has the `<layer>#<n>` family idiom for exactly this
  and the shipped payload uses none of it. That is a packer job, not a renderer job. Beds,
  banners, signs, shulker boxes and skulls are still holes, each named with the stage that closes
  it.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `beworldcheck`, `becheck` (70), `g17ccheck`, `mobboxcheck`, `behavcheck`,
  `chestcheck`, `chestpaircheck`, `bemodelcheck`, `animcheck`, `entitycheck`, `tickcheck` green.
  `node build.mjs` exit 0.

- **D-422** — **THE HEAD TURNS, AND THE BODY FOLLOWS.**
  ▶ **EVERY MOB IN THE GAME STARED DEAD AHEAD, AND THE GOAL MEANT TO FIX IT MADE IT WORSE.**
  `ER.animOf` fed `netHeadYaw = 0, headPitch = 0` to every model there is and said so in its own
  header. Meanwhile `Ai.LookAtPlayerGoal.tick` wrote **`e.yaw` — the BODY yaw — directly**, with
  no rate limit and no clamp, so a cow snapped its entire body round in ONE TICK the instant a
  player came in range. **`goalcheck` has fourteen sections and does not mention a look goal**,
  which is how it survived. This is D-417's class of bug one field over: a GOAL writing the state
  a CONTROL owns. Goals ask; controls move.
  ▶ **THE LAW IS THE JAR'S** (`bcv` LookControl, `bcr` BodyRotationControl, `aya` Mob):
  `setLookAt` stores a wanted POINT and a two-tick cooldown; `tick()` throws the pitch away and
  rebuilds it every tick (`resetXRotOnTick`), steps the head yaw toward the target by at most
  `getHeadRotSpeed()` = **10 degrees**, and falls back to easing the head onto the body when the
  cooldown runs out.
  ▶ **`rotateTowards` AND `rotateIfNecessary` ARE NOT THE SAME FUNCTION**, and the difference is
  the whole character of the motion. The first MOVES a little way toward the target every tick;
  the second does nothing at all until the limit is exceeded and then pulls back to exactly it.
  Swap them and you get either a head that teleports or a head that can point backwards.
  `headcheck` §1 asserts they give different answers for the same arguments.
  ▶ **THE BODY CATCHES UP ON ITS OWN CLOCK** (`bcr`): moving → the head is clamped to the body;
  standing with the head moved more than 15 degrees since it was last stable → the BODY is pulled
  to within `getMaxHeadYRot()` of the head; standing with the head stable for more than 10 ticks
  → the body swings round with an allowance that **ramps from 75 degrees to 0 over ten ticks**,
  which is the slow turn-and-face an animal does when you stand still next to it. Measured:
  60 degrees of offset closes to 0, gradually.
  ▶ **THE EIGHT PER-SPECIES OVERRIDES ARE THE JAR'S, AND THE LIST IS COMPLETE.** Every class in
  `Mob`'s subtree was walked and every override of `getMaxHeadXRot`/`getMaxHeadYRot`/
  `getHeadRotSpeed` read off its bytecode — these are all of them, and `getHeadRotSpeed` is
  overridden by nothing: slime 0 pitch (and `magma_cube`, which extends it), guardian 180 (and
  `elder_guardian`), shulker 180/180, ravager 45 yaw, goat 15 yaw, axolotl 1/1, dolphin 1/1, and
  **wolf, the one that is a BRANCH rather than a constant** — `isInSittingPose() ? 20 : super`.
  The obfuscated classes were matched to registry names through `EntityType`'s own `<clinit>`
  (each `ldc "<name>"` sits beside the `invokedynamic` whose bootstrap method handle names the
  constructor's class), so which mob is which is not a guess either.
  ▶ **DEGREES IN, RADIANS OUT.** `setupAnim`'s two rotation arguments are degrees in vanilla and
  every formula in `ER.setupAnimDelta` multiplies by `DEG2RAD` on the way in. Handing it radians
  would turn a head a fifty-seventh of the angle it asked for — a bug that looks like "the head
  barely moves" rather than like a unit error, so `headcheck` §5 asserts the factor explicitly.
  ▶ **Checks:** `tools/headcheck.mjs` (64 assertions, 6 breaks), including the one that matters:
  ticking `LookAtPlayerGoal` must leave `e.yaw` untouched, and the shipped bug — writing it — is
  asserted to be a 90-degree snap.
  ▶ **OWED, NAMED on `Ai.OWED`:** this engine keeps one body yaw where vanilla has two, so
  `BodyRotationControl`'s moving branch is a no-op rather than a missing line; the
  clamp-while-pathing condition asks `e.zza` where vanilla asks the navigator; and
  `Mob.tickHeadTurn`'s own smoothing is not modelled.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `headcheck`, `goalcheck`, `aicheck`, `mobmovecheck`, `animcheck`, `entitycheck`,
  `entlistcheck`, `combatcheck`, `spawncheck`, `physcheck`, `movecheck` green, and `g18ccheck`
  (the live-mob browser stage) green at `MCLITE_PRESET=medium`. `node build.mjs` exit 0.

- **D-423** — **LOVE MODE, AND THE TWO GOALS THAT WERE WIRED TO NOTHING.**
  ▶ **`Ai.BreedGoal` AND `Ai.TemptGoal` HAVE BEEN DEAD SINCE D-383 AND `07i_entitylist.js`'s OWN

  ▶ **THE REFEREE IS `tools/extract-breeding.mjs`**, the twenty-somethingth application of D-263.
  `AgeableMob` is the ONE class in the jar whose constant pool carries the `ForcedAge` NBT key and

  ▶ **AND WHAT EACH ANIMAL EATS, PER SPECIES, WITH FOUR KINDS THAT ARE FOUR DIFFERENT FACTS.**

  ▶ **`e.growAge` IS NOT `e.age`.** `EL.spawn` has always given every entity an `age` — ticks

  ▶ **REFUSALS, NOT GUESSES.** `Breed.SPECIAL` names the thirteen species whose `getBreedOffspring`

  ▶ **A BONUS OFF THE SAME READ.** Cow's `registerGoals` (`bij.u()`) puts the stroll, the look and

  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `breedcheck` (79 assertions, 4 deliberate breaks) — including the live
