- **D-424** — **A BABY IS NOT THE ADULT DRAWN SMALLER.**
  ▶ `docs/QUEUE.md` row 2 asks for "the child model with the model class's own head-scale ratio".
  Vanilla's `AgeableListModel` splits every model into HEAD parts and BODY parts and gives the two
  groups **different** transforms — and for **four of the ten** models this engine could read, the
  head is not scaled at all. A baby cow is a full-sized head on a halved body, and a uniform
  shrink would be wrong for every one of them in the one way that is visible.
  ▶ **`tools/extract-babymodel.mjs` READS WHAT THE SIX ARGUMENTS MEAN, NOT JUST THEIR VALUES.**
  `AgeableListModel` is the only class with both a `(boolean, float x5)` constructor and two
  abstract no-arg `Iterable` methods. Its roles are then derived twice over: which FIELD each
  constructor parameter lands in (from the storing constructor — **not** the six-argument one,
  which only delegates), and what the render method divides each field by (1.5 into the head
  scale, 16 into the two offsets, 1 into the body scale). The layer is read off the entity
  RENDERER's own generic supertype — `euy extends ewp<bij, ejd>` is Cow's renderer naming Cow and
  CowModel — and resolved to a registry name through the existing entity table.
  ▶ **A `PoseStack` SCALE FOLLOWED BY A TRANSLATE SCALES THE TRANSLATE TOO**: the matrix is S·T,
  so a point lands at `s * (p + t)`. The other reading puts a calf most of a block under the floor.
  ▶ **15 OF 25 MODELS ARE UNREAD AND NAMED** (`:six`, `:headGroup`, `:partNames`) rather than
  defaulted, and `Entities.babyModel` returns null for them, so an unread mob draws as its adult
  self and somebody has to answer for it.
  ▶ **THE BOX IS EVERY LIVING ENTITY'S RULE, NOT AN ANIMAL'S**: `LivingEntity.getDimensions` scales
  the type's own box by `getScale()`, and the crossing — not a later refresh — is the event, so
  `Br.setAge` is the only place that needs to know.
  ▶ **AND IT FOUND KW-26.** The screen test written for this unit could not be made to mean
  anything: a guardian four blocks ahead changes ~3,100 pixels and a COW at the identical spot
  changes **111**, with `ER.build` reporting `drawn: 1` and 58 quads. That is a separate and
  severe fault — every mob but the guardian is effectively invisible, and `g18ccheck` has only
  ever photographed the guardian. It is measured and filed, not fixed (Dan's gate rule: finish the
  unit you are on), and `g18ccheck` §4 proves this unit's live join by reading what the live
  renderer EMITS for the same cow adult and baby instead of by counting pixels on a bug.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `babycheck` (32 assertions, 3 breaks) and `g18ccheck` §4 green at
  `MCLITE_PRESET=medium`; `animcheck`, `mobboxcheck`, `breedcheck`, `gatecheck` green.

- **D-425** — **KW-26 WAS A WRONG FORWARD VECTOR, AND THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE EXISTED.**
  ▶ **WHAT WAS CLAIMED, ONE SESSION EARLIER IN THE SAME SESSION:** that every mob but the
  guardian was effectively invisible — guardian 3,098 pixels against cow 111, spider 68, turtle
  54, with `ER.build` reporting `drawn: 1` and the right quad count for all of them. It was
  written up as KW-26 severe, with the base-pose flip (D-415) named as the suspect, and Dan was
  told the whole game was broken.
  ▶ **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG:** the harness spawned each mob along `[-sin(yaw), 0, cos(yaw)]`
  instead of the engine's own `Player.lookVec()`. Every mob went off to the SIDE, into tree
  trunks and behind foliage. `ER.build` lights a mob from the block its feet are in
  (`W.getLight(it.wx, it.wy, it.wz)`), a log's light is zero, and a mob lit at zero is a BLACK
  SILHOUETTE — which is what vanilla draws too. The mobs were there, in the wrong place, unlit.
  The pixel counts were true and they were the truth about a bad test.
  ▶ **WHAT WAS RULED OUT ALONG THE WAY, AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING:** the atlas shard boundary
  (D-380) is not involved — 58 of the guardian's 60 quads are above it and it draws fine; the
  mob tiles are real and opaque in `Atlas.mips[0]` (cow tile 2012 is 256 opaque texels, mean RGB
  125); disabling `CULL_FACE` on the opaque pass changes nothing, so the flip's winding is not
  inverted; and `Gfx.stats().entityTris` is 84-132 per mob, so the triangles reach the GPU.
  ▶ **AND THREE HARNESS LESSONS, each of which cost a wrong hypothesis:**
  (1) **Ask the engine where forward is.** `lookVec()` exists and `g18ccheck` uses it.
  (2) **A screenshot is not a frame.** With the pointer unlocked the page presents on its own
  schedule: a spawn eight game-frames old was still not on the screenshot and its pixels turned
  up in the NEXT measurement — which is how one pass read "cow 79,260, guardian 23" and the next
  read the reverse. Settling AFTER the change is worse than useless, because two stale
  screenshots agree perfectly. A change is WATCHED, not waited for.
  (3) **A silhouette passes a naive drawing test.** Counting changed pixels alone cannot tell a
  drawn mob from a black cut-out, so the pixels a mob changes are measured for BRIGHTNESS and
  COLOUR as well.
  ▶ **THE REAL GAP WAS A CHECK GAP, AND IT IS CLOSED.** `g18ccheck` has photographed a live mob
  since session 30 and it photographs the **guardian** — a cube with no `LivingEntityRenderer`
  preamble, the one type unlike the rest. Nothing had ever photographed the other six.
  `tools/mobdrawcheck.mjs` puts every spawnable mob on a lit, open, floored spot it CHOOSES
  itself and asserts the frame builds it, that it reaches the screen (pixels per square metre of
  its own box, against a floor derived from the best mob in the run rather than typed in), and
  that it is drawn LIT and in colour. Its anti-vacuity breaks are an entity with no model layer
  (nothing like a mob appears) and a mob standing INSIDE a block (it goes dark) — the second one
  is KW-26's own mistake, kept as a test.
  ▶ **MEASURED, all seven drawn, lit and textured:** cow 24,636 px · guardian 29,096 · dolphin
  22,443 · turtle 17,973 · zombie 17,679 · spider 17,530 · skeleton 13,580.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `mobdrawcheck` 38 assertions, 0 failures, 2 breaks, at `MCLITE_PRESET=medium`;
  `knowncheck`, `gatecheck`, `stagecheck` green. KW-26 struck, kept in place with the whole
  account, because the mistake is more useful than the entry was.

- **D-426** — **A DEAD BUTTON THAT LOOKS ALIVE IS THE BUG, NOT THE DEAD BUTTON.** Dan, session
  55: *"you cant click earth on world load screen."* The climate rows on the title screen have
  been locked once a saved world exists since D-111, deliberately and correctly — changing the
  climate of a world that has been built in would move every biome out from under everything in
  it. But the lock lived **entirely inside the click handler** (`if (!locked) { ... }`): the
  button drew in the same colours as a live one, lit up on hover like a live one, and then
  swallowed the click in silence. There is no reading of that other than "the button is broken",
  and the tiny grey footer line that did explain it was fifteen rows away and not where anyone
  looks after pressing something.
  ▶ **THE RULE, which this crude menu is the one screen in the project that never had:** a
  disabled control must (a) be drawn differently, (b) not react to hover, and (c) **say why when
  it is pressed**. All three, or a person learns to distrust the whole screen. `15f_options.js`'s
  vanilla buttons have had a `disabled` sprite since G13; `15_hud.js`'s `button()` now takes the
  REASON as its last argument instead of the caller checking a flag, so the three halves cannot
  be implemented separately and one of them forgotten. The hit region is still pushed — a button
  that is not clickable at all cannot explain itself, and the click would fall through to
  whatever is behind it.
  ▶ The reason names the way out (*"Climate is fixed once a world exists — press 'New world' to
  change it"*), which the old footer line did not: it said the rule and not the remedy.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `titlecheck` §D-426 presses the Vanilla button both locked and unlocked, on the
  real screen at its real pixels, and asserts all three halves in both directions — unlocked it
  must change the climate, locked it must not, must be drawn a DIFFERENT COLOUR (sampled off the
  live canvas), and must leave a reason behind that matches `/New world/`. Its live anti-vacuity
  break puts the pre-D-426 silent no-op back and requires the "it said why" assertion to fail.
  95 assertions, 0 failures.
  ⚠ A third page is opened for it: `page2` has already pressed Enter by then and is inside the
  world, so the title screen it would be asked about no longer exists. The first run of that
  section failed with "no Vanilla button", which is a fact about the harness and not about the
  game — `cdp.mjs`'s own rule, and the second time this project has had to learn it.

- **D-427** — **ITEMS SLID NINETEEN TIMES TOO FAR, AND THE NUMBER THAT WOULD HAVE STOPPED THEM
  HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED.** Dan, session 55: *"items slide too much when dropped."*
  `EntityList.tickOne` damped all three axes by the single uniform `drag` from
  `entity-motion-1.18.2.tsv` — 0.98 for an item — so a dropped stack kept 98% of its speed every
  tick **for ever, on the ground exactly as in the air**. Vanilla multiplies an item's horizontal
  speed by the friction of the block UNDER it times 0.98: on grass that is 0.588, twenty-four
  times more damping per tick. Measured through the engine: a stack pushed at 0.5 blocks/tick
  used to travel **13.86 blocks** and now travels **0.71**, and 9.72 on ice.
  ▶ **THE REASON IT WAS MISSING IS THE INTERESTING PART.** `extract-entity-motion.mjs`'s own
  header named it as owed, in as many words: *"Vertical drag appears in TWO shapes — `scale(0.98)`
  … and `multiply(f, 0.98, f)` for the ones whose horizontal damping is a VARIABLE … Every case
  seen so far is 0.98, which is exactly why it must not be assumed."* That was the right call and
  it left a hole nothing filled for twenty sessions. `tools/extract-entity-ground.mjs` fills it:
  the ON-GROUND half of an entity's tick, in the two shapes the jar actually uses.
  ▶ **THE TWO SHAPES, both refereed:**
  `block` (item `bli`, experience_orb `axq`) — `f = 0.98`, and `f = friction(below) * 0.98` when
  on the ground, then `multiply(f, 0.98, f)`, then a bounce; `flat` (tnt `blj`, falling_block
  `blh`) — the uniform drag, then on the ground `multiply(0.7, -0.5, 0.7)`.
  ▶ **AND THE BOUNCE IS NOT ONE NUMBER AND NOT ONE GUARD, which is why rule 4 exists.** An item
  bounces **−0.5** and **only while it is already falling**; an experience orb bounces **−0.9**,
  unconditionally. Memory says "−0.5, both". The extractor's anchor set deliberately includes the
  orb's −0.9 and the item's `falling` guard, so a jar that moved them cannot pass.
  ▶ **`ItemEntity` ALSO DOES NOT MOVE EVERY TICK.** `if (!onGround || lengthSqr(delta) > 1.0E-5
  || (tickCount + getId()) % 4 == 0)` guards the whole move-and-damp block, so a stack lying
  still runs the collision sweep on one tick in four. Read out of the jar (`restSkip`), ported,
  and only `item` has one.
  ⚠ **AND THE FRICTION LOOKUP IS NOT `Ph.frictionOf`.** The player asks
  `getBlockPosBelowThatAffectsMyMovement()`, which is y − 0.5000001 so a slab still counts;
  `ItemEntity` and `ExperienceOrb` build `new BlockPos(getX(), getY() - 1, getZ())` — a flat minus
  one. Two different lookups in the same jar, and using the player's for an item would be the kind
  of "close enough" that is wrong on exactly the interesting blocks. `entlistcheck` asserts the
  position the lookup asks for, not just its answer.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `entlistcheck` §8 recomputes the slide by hand from the TABLE's own numbers and
  compares, on TWO surfaces — the same push must die inside a block on grass (0.6) and carry
  nine blocks on ice (0.98), so a hard-coded 0.588 could not pass. Two live anti-vacuity breaks:
  the pre-D-427 uniform drag back (the distance test fires), and a friction table with one value
  for every block (the grass-vs-ice comparison fires). 76 assertions, 0 failures, 11 breaks.

- **D-428** — **THE RECOMMENDATION WAS BEING USED AS THE CEILING.** Dan, session 55: *"add a
  proper option in settings to toggle amount of web workers; its set to 4 now with no
  tinkering."* Two separate faults behind that one sentence. `ENV.workers` is the RECOMMENDED
  pool size — one fewer than the machine's threads, never more than 4 (D-36) — and it was also
  the CLAMP, in three places, so on a 12-thread desktop the setting could not be raised past 4
  however it was set. And there was no control to raise it with. `ENV.workersMax` is the
  machine's own thread count and is the clamp now; the recommendation is unchanged and is still
  what an untouched install gets.
  ▶ **THE POOL IS NO LONGER FIXED AT START-UP, and the comment that said it was gave the real
  reason:** *"respawning workers mid-game would drop every job in flight."* It would have.
  `J.inflight` maps a job id to the promise waiting for it, and terminating its worker leaves
  that promise pending **for ever** — a chunk that never generates and never says why. So
  `Jobs.resize` does not terminate a busy worker: it **retires** it. `_pick` stops handing it
  work and `_onMessage` terminates it the moment its last result comes back. Nothing in flight is
  lost, nothing has to be re-requested, and there is no "restart to apply".
  ▶ The slider is on the Video screen, 1 to `ENV.workersMax`, and its label shows the LIVE pool
  when it disagrees with the setting — a worker finishing a chunk is still alive, and a slider
  that claimed otherwise would be lying for a second or two every time it is dragged down.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `optionscheck` §W — the row exists exactly once, both ends of the range are
  reachable on a 12-thread machine, every position round-trips, a 2-thread machine gets a
  working two-position slider, and §W3 drives the real `09_jobs.js` against a fake `Worker`:
  grow 4 → 8, then shrink to 1 with one worker holding a job, and assert it is **not**
  terminated, is on the retiring list, and IS terminated when its result lands. Anti-vacuity:
  `ENV.workers` put back as the ceiling and the range test fires. 284 assertions, 0 failures.
  ⚠ The check's own first draft arranged the pool wrong twice — `resize` drops the LEAST loaded
  first, by design, so a shrink has to be pushed past the busy worker for the retire path to be
  exercised at all. A break that cannot fire is not a break (D-305), and neither is a setup that
  cannot reach the code.

- **D-429** — **THE ZOMBIE'S ARMS-OUT POSE IS A SECOND LAYER, NOT A DIFFERENT MODEL.** Dan,
  session 55: *"the zombie doesnt have its arms out pose."* `ER.modelKindOf` calls a zombie a
  HUMANOID and is right to — its part names ARE a humanoid's — so `HumanoidModel.setupAnim` hung
  its arms at its sides and swung them with the walk. The pose is not in that method at all. It
  is one line in `AbstractZombieModel.setupAnim`, after the super call:
  `AnimationUtils.animateZombieArms(leftArm, rightArm, isAggressive(e), attackTime, ageInTicks)`,
  and that helper **overwrites** all three angles of both arms rather than adding to them — so it
  cannot be expressed as a delta on the humanoid swing, and the humanoid swing must not survive
  under it. `ER.setupAnimDelta` returns the difference from REST for those two parts instead.
  ▶ **THE ANGLE IS NOT −π/2.** Every description of this animation says the arms are set to
  −π/2. The bytecode says **−π over 1.5 when the mob is aggressive and 2.25 when it is not** —
  −120° and −80°, neither of them −90° — and the difference between the two IS the "it raises its
  arms when it comes for you" read. `tools/extract-zombiearms.mjs` is the referee: AnimationUtils
  found by float fingerprint (0.09f, 0.067f and 1.2f together — one class in 6,399), the pose read
  by POSITION in its literal sequence, and `bobArms` walked through the `(Part, Part, float)` →
  `(Part, float, float)` chain to its own two constants.
  ▶ **AND IT IS NOT ONLY ZOMBIES.** The callers come off the jar's own call graph, not the word
  "zombie": **drowned, illusioner, vindicator, zombie, zombie_villager** — the illager model
  calls the same helper, which is why a vindicator charges with its arms out. A hand-written list
  would have had four of the five wrong. `husk` is NAMED as unmatched in the table rather than
  dropped: its renderer does not spell out both an entity and a model in its generic supertype,
  which is the same shortfall `extract-babymodel.mjs` already names for its own rows.
  ▶ `MeleeAttackGoal.start/stop` now sets `e.aggressive`, transcribed (the standard this goal's
  own reach formula already uses, D-394); the POSE it drives is refereed. `attackTime` is 0 and
  `ER.ZARM_OWED` says why — nothing in this engine ticks a mob swing animation, which is exactly
  right for every tick a mob is not mid-swing and wrong for the six it would be.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `animcheck` §3c, with every number read from the SHIPPED table and only the
  SHAPES asserted here — the two arms mirror, angry is higher than calm by more than half a
  radian, the bob depends on age and stays inside ±2·bobAmp, the pose is absolute under a part
  with non-zero rest angles, and, the bug itself, **the arm delta no longer moves with
  `limbSwing`**. Two live breaks. 94 assertions, 0 failures.
  ⚠ `animcheck` had never loaded `DATA.entities` at all — `loadsrc.mjs` builds the registry and
  the models but not the entity table, so `M.Entities.init()` there has always returned
  not-ready. Invisible while `setupAnim` needed nothing from it; the zombie-arm layer is IN that
  table, so a check that skipped it would have gone on asserting the pre-D-429 pose and passing.
  It is loaded now, and asserted loaded.

- **D-430** — **THE POSITION WAS INTERPOLATED AND THE ROTATION WAS NOT.** Dan, session 55: *"all
  turns of mobs look stuttery and not smooth."* The class of the bug rather than the instance:
  `ER.posAt` has lerped a mob's POSITION between ticks since G17b, so it glides; its three
  rotations were read raw, so its heading snapped twenty times a second underneath a body that
  was moving smoothly. Everything else the renderer reads per-tick was already interpolated — the
  item bob and spin off `age + partial`, the limb swing off `animSpeedO`, a chest lid off
  `lidOpenness(e, partial)`. Rotation was the one that was not, and it is the one you look at.
  ▶ `yawO`, `yHeadRotO` and `xHeadRotO` are captured at the TOP of `tickOne`, beside `px/py/pz`,
  because everything that turns a mob — the look control, the body-rotation control, `travelMob`
  — runs below that line. `ER.rotLerp` is `Mth.rotLerp` in radians and `ER.yawAt` is the one
  place the renderer reads a heading.
  ▶ **THE WRAP IS THE WHOLE FUNCTION.** A plain `a + (b - a) * t` between 179° and −179° sweeps
  the mob 358 degrees the long way round in one tick — a spin, not a turn — and it happens at
  exactly the heading a mob walking north keeps crossing.
  ▶ **BOTH ENDS, for the head.** `netHeadYaw` is the head's offset FROM THE BODY, so lerping the
  head against a body yaw that is still snapping would make the head jerk by exactly the amount
  the body did, in the opposite direction.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `animcheck` §3d — the wrap takes the short way, `yawAt` reaches both ends and
  is linear inside the tick, an entity that has never been ticked is not lerped from zero, a head
  turning WITH its body reads as straight ahead while one turned off it still reads as turned,
  and a source scan of `ER.build`'s mob branch requires `ER.yawAt(it.e, partial)` and refuses the
  pre-D-430 expression — a correct `yawAt` that nothing calls fixes nothing. Two live breaks.

- **D-431** — **F4 IS MINEHTML'S DIAGNOSTICS OVERLAY NOW; THE WIREFRAME IS F7 AND THE FROZEN
  FRUSTUM IS F10.** Dan, session 55: *"move what is currently linked to f4 to f7, and add in f4
  what we have in f4 in claudeisthegoat."* F7 was already taken by the frozen cull frustum, so
  that moved to F10 rather than being dropped — Dan chose that; nothing was lost to make room.
  `src/15i_diag.js` is the port: three columns, the frame-time graph, the frame-budget bar, the
  phase breakdown, GPU/world/streaming/worker rows, spikes, stutter-since-opened, the memory bar,
  the bottleneck verdict, the jitter-source line, the Observable entity profiler with its
  Aggregate/Individual/Chunks tabs, and the live console tail — with MineHTML's own CSS, its keys
  (F4 toggle, PgUp/PgDn scroll, Tab cycles the tab, Del clears the log) and its colour ramp.
  ▶ **WHAT IS PORTED IS THE PANEL, NOT THE ROWS.** MineHTML's rows name MineHTML's internals — a
  `Weather / Hunger / Combat CD / Shield / Farming / Fluids / Scheduled / Furnaces` bundle, a
  per-status worldgen ladder, a decoration breakdown. Transcribing those names would give a panel
  of `--`s that looks like a diagnostic and diagnoses nothing. The rows are the phases MC-Lite
  has and now measures: `Main.prof` gains one ring per phase (world tick, stream+light, render,
  HUD) plus **loop lag** — the gap between frames minus the work in them, which is the number
  that tells a stutter caused by this game from one caused by the machine.
  ▶ **IT IS DOM, AND EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS PROJECT'S UI IS CANVAS.** On purpose, and it is why
  it is its own file rather than part of `15_hud.js`: the HUD is drawn INTO the frame and costs
  frame time, and a panel whose whole job is to measure frame time must not be in it. A DOM
  overlay is composited outside `Gfx.render` and its own cost lands in `loop lag` where it can be
  seen. No external anything — the stylesheet is a `<style>` the module writes and every element
  is `document.createElement`, so it can be deleted in one piece.
  ▶ **THE COUNTERS RUN EVERY FRAME AND THE DOM DOES NOT.** MineHTML rolls its history while
  closed so the graph is full on open, and that half must be every frame; writing sixty DOM nodes
  sixty times a second is a measurable cost inside the thing being measured, so the panel
  repaints at 6 Hz. **A diagnostic that changes what it is diagnosing is the one bug this file
  cannot have**, and `diagcheck` §6 measures exactly that — frame time with the panel open
  against frame time with it closed, as a SHARE of the frame rather than a number of
  milliseconds, because the same 6 Hz repaint is a tenth of a frame at 60 fps and most of one in
  a headless Chromium at 9.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `tools/diagcheck.mjs`, a new browser stage next to `inputcheck` for the same
  reason `inputcheck` exists — every assertion is about a key handler on `window` and a DOM tree
  built at runtime, and there is no Node-level version of either. It asserts the panel fills with
  the GAME's numbers (a panel that draws but never updates shows the `--` it was built with and
  is completely convincing in a screenshot), that the graph is drawn from the ring, that the keys
  work, and — **the half a remap always forgets** — that **F4 no longer toggles the wireframe**.
  Adding F7 and leaving F4 wired passes every other test. 44 assertions, 0 failures, 5 breaks.
  ⚠ Its first run caught two mistakes in itself: a graph floor of 200 lit pixels that an EMPTY
  graph clears (the two reference lines are 800 px on their own), and a chunk count compared
  against a world that had streamed on for the 170 ms since the panel last repainted. Both are
  the shape of KW-26 — a fact about the harness reported as a fact about the game.
  ▶ OWED, NAMED: MineHTML's "3D overlay (green→red)" entity tint has no per-entity tint channel
  to hang on in this renderer and is not drawn rather than drawn dead (D-426's rule, one file
  over); its RECORD/EXPORT perf trace is a `file://` download problem and is not in this port.

- **D-432** — **QUEUE row 1 unit: the trapped chest and the lectern, the last two owed sources
  G19b is responsible for.** `redcheck` FAILS if a source stays owed against a completed stage,
  and both are refereed off the jar rather than remembered:
  `clg.a` = `clamp(ChestBlockEntity.getOpenCount(level, pos), 0, 15)`, `clg.b` =
  `dir == UP ? getSignal(...) : 0`; `chp.a` = `POWERED ? 15 : 0`, `chp.b` =
  `(dir == UP && POWERED) ? 15 : 0`.
  ▶ **A TRAPPED CHEST'S POWER IS AN OPENER COUNT, NOT A BOOLEAN.** Vanilla returns the NUMBER of
  players with it open, clamped to 15, so two players emit 2. This engine has one player, so the
  value is 0 or 1 today — and writing it as `open ? 15 : 0` would have been a different rule that
  happens to agree in every single-player case and would be wrong the moment anything else opens
  a chest. It reads the same `e.open` the LID animation already keeps, which is how vanilla keeps
  a trapped chest's lid and its power from ever disagreeing (D-403/D-413).
  ▶ **THE LECTERN'S ROW IS NARROWED, NOT DELETED.** Its signal is a block-state property, so that
  branch is live and complete. Nothing SETS `powered` yet: vanilla pulses it for two ticks when a
  page is turned, and turning a page needs the lectern screen (G19e). Leaving the whole row owed
  would have hidden the fact that the only missing piece is a screen — the difference between
  "not built" and "waiting on a named stage".
  ▶ **THE TRAPPED CHEST JOINS THE COMPARATOR AS AN EXEMPTION IN `redcheck`'s CLOSED-SET TEST**,
  for the same reason: its strength is not in its block state at all, so a state driven to
  `powered` answers 0 there and is right to. §17 asserts it where it lives.
  ▶ **VERIFIED:** `redcheck` §17 — a real block entity at a real position (stubbing `BE.get`
  would test the arithmetic and not the join, and the join is where D-276 says the bugs are);
  0 openers → 0, 1 → 1, 4 → 4, 99 → 15; STRONG power only downward and WEAK power in every
  direction; a trapped chest with no block entity reads 0 rather than throwing; the lectern
  asserted in both directions on both questions. Anti-vacuity: at 4 openers the count rule and
  the boolean rule give different answers (the count assertion is not a tautology) and with the
  chest CLOSED they agree (which is why a check that only tested open-vs-closed could never have
  told them apart). 379 assertions, 0 failures, 22 breaks.

- **D-433** — **THE TWO HEADLESS CHECKS THAT WERE ALREADY RED WHEN THIS SESSION STARTED.** The
  ledger's last full run failed five stages and two of them were nothing to do with the browser.
  ▶ **`tickcheck`: `Breed.tick` was a per-tick function the loop never called.** It was written
  as *"both halves in vanilla's own order"* and it only ever called `tickAge`. It could not have
  been anything else: `EL.tickMob` runs `tickAge` BEFORE the goals and `tickLove` AFTER them,
  because that is where the jar puts them (`AgeableMob.tick` vs `Animal.aiStep`), so a single
  wrapper cannot express the order at all. Nothing called it. DELETED, not kept beside its
  replacement (D-139). `tickcheck`'s whole job is "is every per-tick function something the loop
  CALLS" (D-301) and it was right to name it.
  ▶ **`modecheck`: the `creative` boolean was still in `Br.interact`'s options.** G6 spent a
  whole stage replacing that boolean with `Abilities.instabuild`, and `modecheck` §6 keeps `src/`
  clean of it — but the option `Use.entityUse` passes was still CALLED `creative` while carrying
  `P.instabuild`. Renamed to `instabuild` all the way through, which is what
  `Animal.usePlayerItem` asks for in the jar. ⚠ A name that survives the thing it named is how
  the thing comes back, and the scanner was right to read it as creeping.
  ⚠ `modecheck` §6 scans `src/` and not `tools/`, and `palettecheck` sets `MCL.Player.creative`
  — named here, not fixed blind, because whether that line does anything is a question about
  `palettecheck` and belongs to whoever next opens it.

- **D-434** — **THE F4 PANEL'S FIRST REAL RUN FOUND A PIPELINE STALL IN THE DEBUG OVERLAY THAT
  HAS BEEN THERE SINCE F3 WAS WRITTEN.** `diagcheck` §6 asks one question — *what does this panel
  cost the frame it is measuring* — and on Dan's GPU it answered **35.6% of a frame**. Chasing
  that took four wrong answers and the last one was worth the whole exercise.
  ▶ **IT WAS `Gfx.backend.info()`, AND IT IS 119.5 ms A CALL.** `L.info` calls `gl.getParameter`
  six times; each is a synchronous query the driver must drain its queue to answer. Measured in
  one probe at render distance 12: `info()` **119.5 ms**, `World.stats()` 0.3 ms, `World.biomeAt`
  0 ms, `Jobs.stats()` 0 ms. `Hud.drawDebug` calls `info()` **once a frame** whenever F3 is open,
  so **F3 has been stalling the pipeline every frame since it was written**, and the F4 panel
  inherited it. Nothing had ever measured the debug overlay, which is exactly the hole a panel
  that measures itself closes. ▶ Fixed by the split the data already had: `vendor`, `renderer`,
  `glsl`, `maxTexSize` and `maxLayers` are properties of a CONTEXT and cannot change while it
  lives, so they are read once and dropped on `webglcontextlost`. Everything else on that object
  is a field this module already holds. Result: **0 ms cached against 251.5 ms uncached**, and
  the panel's median repaint went from 295 ms to **0.4 ms**.
  ▶ **THE THREE WRONG ANSWERS, KEPT BECAUSE EACH ONE IS A TRAP THIS PROJECT WILL MEET AGAIN:**
  (1) *"it is the DOM writes"* — plausible, and the fixes are kept because they are right
  (write only what changed; build the budget bar once; rebuild the entity list and the log only
  when they change), but they were not the cause.
  (2) *"it is `World.stats()`"* — a guess that names the wrong line is worse than no guess,
  because the next reader believes it. The comment that claimed a measured 300 ms for it has
  been corrected in place rather than quietly deleted.
  (3) *"time the repaint and average it"* — the panel is built once and kept at `display:none`,
  so the first repaint after the first F4 pays for the first LAYOUT of ninety rows in three flex
  columns. Measured, with the layout forced between each: **170.7, 0.9, 1.1, 0.9, 0.7, 0.8, 0.7,
  0.8, 0.9 ms**. An exponential average seeded on that first sample read 89 ms for a panel
  costing one, and the self-throttle below then slowed the panel to **one repaint every nine
  seconds** — a self-inflicted freeze out of a measurement that was true exactly once. It is a
  MEDIAN over the last sixteen now, which ignores the one-off the moment the ring fills and still
  rises if the panel genuinely gets slow.
  ▶ **THE PANEL PAYS FOR ITSELF OUT OF ITS OWN REFRESH RATE.** A fixed 6 Hz is a fixed number of
  repaints a second and therefore a VARIABLE share of the frame — the same repaint is a tenth of
  a frame at 60 fps and most of one at 9 — and the repaint costs MORE on a machine that is doing
  well, because a machine doing well has a bigger resident world to summarise. So the interval is
  derived from the measured cost, clamped at both ends: never more often than `HZ`, never more
  than 3% of wall time, and never slower than once a second, because a panel that answers every
  nine seconds is not a diagnostic however honest its arithmetic. It reports its own cost in its
  header, since that is the one number in there nobody would think to doubt.
  ▶ **AND §6 NOW MEASURES THE PANEL'S WORK AGAINST THE PANEL'S PRESENCE.** Comparing "open" with
  "closed" cannot answer the question: a full-screen translucent overlay costs the browser
  something to COMPOSITE whether or not anything in it changes, and in a software-rasterised
  headless browser that plus ordinary frame noise swamps everything — measured on one run at
  closed 146 ms, open 135 ms, open-with-the-repaint-stubbed 152 ms. The panel appeared to make
  the game faster, and then slower than that, having done nothing. The control is now the panel
  OPEN AND INERT: same overlay, same compositing, same noise, `paint` replaced by a no-op. The
  difference is the panel's WORK and nothing else (**0.07 ms a frame**); the compositing cost is
  reported, not asserted, because it is the browser's. `diagcheck` §7 keeps `info()` cheap, with
  the uncached call as its own break.
  ▶ **`cullcheck`: NO LIVE MOBS (the sixth failing stage, and this one was mine).** Every
  assertion in that file is "two screenshots of the same scene are the same picture", and a mob
  is not the same scene twice — it walks, and since D-430 its heading is INTERPOLATED between
  ticks rather than snapping once a tick. §3's "turn 180° and back" started failing on 85 changed
  pixels against a 26-pixel noise floor the day D-430 landed; those pixels were the edge of a
  cow, and the flood-fill culler the file is about had nothing to do with them. Natural spawning
  is held off (D-397's rule, which `cullcheck` never took) and the list emptied, so the picture
  is the WORLD. Not a loss of coverage: `mobdrawcheck` and `g18ccheck` are the checks that
  photograph mobs, and neither asks whether two frames are identical.

- **D-435** — pack-sounds keeps the last complete pack on a machine with no sound source (session 56)
A cloud session reaches Dan's files one staged file at a time: the 1,214 cached Opus encodes are ~25
staging calls, the finished `assets/sounds.bin` is one. `pack-sounds` now keeps an existing pack ONLY
when nothing on the machine could rebuild it (zero raw sources, zero cached encodes) AND its own meta
says it was complete (`filesMissing` 0, `filesWanted` equal to today's want-list, byte count equal to
`rawBytes`). A partial pack is never carried forward; with any source present the branch is skipped.

- **D-436** — POLLING IS BANNED, PHYSICALLY, FOR THE LIFE OF THE PROJECT (session 56)
Dan, 20 Sept 2026: "fully stop polling for the rest of this project's lifespan." The session that
wrote that rule then broke it twice — it started the suite in the background and kept coming back to
it with ten-minute `timeout … tail --pid` waits, calling each one "blocking" as if that were different.
Dan: "I want it physically banned … there should be no workaround."
  ▶ **The harness refuses the call.** `.claude/settings.json` runs `tools/nopoll.mjs` as a
  **PreToolUse hook on every tool** (exit 2 blocks the call and tells the session why), and its
  `permissions.deny` names the wait tools (ScheduleWakeup, Monitor, CronCreate, TaskOutput,
  BashOutput, send_later) and the shell shapes (`sleep`, `timeout`, `watch`, `nohup`, Start-Sleep,
  Wait-*, `lane.mjs wait|answer`) as a second layer. The hook blocks: wait/check-back tools; sleeping;
  `timeout`/`wait`/`tail -f|--pid`/`watch`; shell `while`/`until` loops; ANY background launch
  (`run_in_background`, `&`, nohup, setsid, Start-Job) — the only reason to background a job is to come
  back to it; timers in inline scripts. `--selftest` proves 20 banned shapes blocked and 9 normal
  commands passed, and `toolscheck` §2c runs it and checks the wiring.
  ▶ **The tools cannot wait either.** `lane.mjs` has no wait loop and no sleep: `run`, `push` and
  `suite` queue and return; `wait` is removed and refuses. `session.mjs close` QUEUES the push;
  `session.mjs start` reads every answer the last close queued ONCE (`lane.mjs answers <since>`,
  stamped by `.ledger/last-close.json`). `toolscheck` §2b fails if a wait loop returns to `lane.mjs` or
  `session.mjs`, or a wake-up instruction returns to a doc; both breaks are its anti-vacuity.
  ⚠ Scope, stated honestly: a hook binds Claude Code and anything that loads this project's
  `.claude/settings.json`. A Cowork `device_bash` session that does not load project hooks is bound
  by the deny list only where Cowork honours it — and by Dan's saved preference, which now says the
  same thing as a permanent ban.

- **D-437** — why the suite is slow: measured, not yet fixed (session 56)
One full run in the cloud container (2 cores, SwiftShader), `MCLITE_PRESET=medium`: the 152 headless
stages took **547 s**; the browser half never finished — `cullcheck` was still rendering after more
than ten minutes, GPU process pinned at ~180% CPU. Where the headless time goes:
structcheck 110 s · redcheck 57 · parcheck 52 · titlecheck 44 · structaudit 34 · floatcheck 29 ·
coherecheck 25 · featcheck 23 · pistoncheck 20 · surfcheck 18 · streamcheck 17 · climcheck 12 — the
top eleven are 78% of it. Two causes, in order of size:
  1. **Worldgen is regenerated from scratch by 16 separate checks** (structcheck, structaudit,
     floatcheck, coherecheck, featcheck, surfcheck, parcheck, featgroundcheck, streamcheck, …), each in
     its own process, often the SAME chunks at the same seed. A shared on-disk chunk cache keyed by
     (seed, cx, cz, worldgen-source hash) generated once per suite run removes most of it.
  2. **Every stage is `spawnSync`, one at a time** — on a 12-thread PC the headless half uses one core.
     Independent stages (no stage reads another's output after `gen-data`/`build`) can run N-wide.
  3. **Browser stages render full frames on a software rasteriser here**; `cullcheck` compares many
     full-resolution screenshots and has no wall-clock budget. It needs a frame/time cap and a smaller
     viewport for the pixel comparisons (the property it tests does not depend on 960x540).
Also seen, environment rather than code: doccheck, briefcheck, inboxcheck, backupcheck fail in a
container that has no `.git` history, `for-dan/` or backup folder. QUEUE row 0 carries the fixes.
- **D-438** — a permanent, device_bash-independent shell, and the polling ban hardened to bind Cowork (session 57).
  Context: a Cowork session reaches this PC two ways — `device_bash` (a Linux shell over the folder) and
  file staging. On/around 8 Sept 2026 a Windows update broke `device_bash` outright ("Workspace
  unavailable … prevents Claude's workspace from reaching your files"); file staging and computer-use
  kept working. `session.mjs`/`lane.mjs` all shell out to `node`, so with the bridge down the whole
  two-command session was unrunnable. Two things were built, both without `device_bash`:
  1. **The file runner** — `tools/shell-runner.mjs` + `.shell/` + `START-SHELL.cmd` (a supervisor that
     relaunches it and logs to `.shell/runner.log`) + `INSTALL-SHELL.cmd` (self-test, register a
     `MCLiteShell` Task Scheduler job at logon, start now). A session DROPS `.shell/inbox/<id>.job` and
     READS `.shell/done/<id>.json` (exists ⇒ finished) + `.out`. No 180 s cap; needs only file access,
     so it is the resilient path even after `device_bash` returns, and long jobs still go to `lane.mjs`.
     The daemon runs one job at a time, kills a job's whole process tree on timeout, keeps head+tail of
     large output, is heartbeat-locked (a hung daemon is taken over, never a deadlock), and cannot be
     killed by an unhandled rejection (Node 24 would otherwise terminate on one). Bootstrapped this
     session by committing the files and double-clicking `INSTALL-SHELL.cmd` via computer-use, because
     `device_bash` was down; verified alive (pid, heartbeat) and end-to-end (`session.mjs start` and the
     verify jobs ran through it).
  2. **The polling ban hardened.** `nopoll.mjs` was NOT import-safe — its `--selftest`/`--install`
     branches fired on `process.argv` at import time, so the runner importing it hijacked those flags;
     fixed with an `isMain` guard (so `shell-runner` can import `verdict` and enforce the SAME ban on the
     file-queue path — the one layer that binds Cowork, where `.claude/settings.json` hooks never run).
     Added Windows wait shapes to the rule set (`ping -n/-t`, `timeout /t`, `choice`/`waitfor`). Added
     `tools/nopollcheck.mjs`, a watchdog that fails the close (and warns at `start`) if any layer is
     stripped: `verdict` blocks/passes an anti-vacuity battery, the Claude Code hook + full deny list are
     present, `shell-runner` still imports and calls `verdict`, and the loud `NOPOLL:D436` banner is
     present in CLAUDE.md, STATE.md and the `session.mjs start` output. Wired `nopollcheck` into
     `session.mjs close`'s doc-check list. Defence in depth: the Claude Code hook, the runner's refusal
     (binds Cowork), and `nopollcheck` at commit.
  Docs: STATE §0 corrected (it claimed `device_bash` always reaches the project — the disagreeing doc was
  the bug) and §3 gained the file-runner lane; CLAUDE.md and STATE.md carry the no-poll banner.
- **D-439** — the suite runs independent stages N-wide, auto-scaled to the machine (D-437 fix 2). The
  sequential `spawnSync` loop in `tools/suite.mjs` is now a barrier-aware pool: consecutive `check`
  stages run concurrently (async `spawn`), while `build`/`gen`/`browser` stages run alone, in order, so
  nothing races its own input (no check reads another check's output after `gen-data`/`build`, D-437).
  Width AUTO-SCALES: `MCLITE_JOBS` if set, else `cpus().length - 1` (one core left free so the box stays
  usable) — 11 on Dan's 12-thread PC, and 1 on a two-core box, i.e. the old sequential behaviour for
  free (Dan, session 57: "make sure the parallel loop auto adjusts by machine ... more or less
  threads"). Results are recorded by id and printed in STAGES order regardless of finish order; the
  live per-stage print (D-211), the assertion/break counting, `--only/--from/--to/--fast`, the partial-
  run warning (D-218) and the exit code are all preserved. Verified on `dads`: `--only
  regcheck,tagcheck,knowncheck` ran 3-wide, 0 failures, 14 breaks caught, header "(11 jobs on 12
  cores)". Still open in QUEUE row 0 item 2: the shared worldgen chunk cache (fix 1, the biggest), the
  `cullcheck` frame/viewport cap (fix 3), and the six red checks blocking one fully green run. This is
  LOCAL cpu parallelism inside one suite process — not the session-level parallelism D-24/AGENTS.md
  governs.
- **D-440** — the section-visibility flood tested material opacity, not the occlusion graph (session 58,
  QUEUE row 0 item 4: block under a cactus vanished at distance). `M.visibility()` (05_mesher.js) — the
  coarse BFS flood used for section-level occlusion culling — read `SR.opaque` (does this block's texture
  read as opaque) to decide whether a cell blocks the flood. That is a MATERIAL question; the flood needs
  a GEOMETRIC one (does this cell fill its whole cube), and vanilla already has that test built for the
  mushroom-growth rule: `SR.solidRender` = `canOcclude() && the outline shape is a full cube` (D-350). Any
  opaque-textured, non-full-cube block — cactus first reported, but the same class covers fences, walls,
  slabs, stairs, carpets, torches, flower pots, glass panes, iron bars — wrongly blocked the flood exactly
  like a solid wall, hiding whole sections behind it at distance. Fix: precompute `SR.visOpaque` from
  `SR.solidRender` (02c_states.js, right before `SR.ready = true`, since registry geometry is decoded by
  then) and switch `M.visibility()`'s local `opaque` binding to it; the mesher's separate per-face quad
  culling (which already correctly combines `SR.cull` + `SR.opaque`) is untouched. New check
  `tools/visfloodcheck.mjs`: a full plane of cactus does not disconnect −Y from +Y (mask stays `VIS_ALL`,
  was 0); a full plane of stone still does (mask 0); an inset-block audit (cactus, fence, wall, slab, pane,
  torch, stairs, flower pot, bars all read `visOpaque=0`, stone/dirt/planks/obsidian/sandstone all read 1);
  anti-vacuity flips `visOpaque` back to 1 for cactus and shows the flood breaking again, then restores it.
  20 assertions, 0 failed. Wired into `suite.mjs` beside `facecheck` (same mesher domain, coarse
  section-occlusion vs. `facecheck`'s per-face culling).
- **D-441** — a fluid predicate's offset trusted a pre-feature guess across a chunk it had not decorated
  yet (session 58, QUEUE row 0 item 3: sugar cane generated on dry land — AUDITED session 57, fixed here).
  `compilePredicate` (04j_features.js) reads an offset predicate's target cell through `ctxBlock`, which
  for a read outside the chunk currently being decorated falls back to `terrainAt` — the pure, pre-carver,
  pre-surface terrain function D-213 uses so that neighbouring chunks agree on a feature whose effect could
  span a border (a tree, say). Reproduced live (`CANE_TRACE=1 node tools/_cane-guard.mjs`, seed 1337,
  chunk cz=13 decorating, cane base at (-309,64,208)): its −Z water offset reads (-309,63,207), in
  chunk cz=12, one over. `terrainAt` there says water (a coastal cell at sea level); the neighbour chunk's
  OWN decoration (a sand/gravel `disk`, D-217) had since dried that exact cell to air — the two chunks
  disagreed, and the guess, not the built world, is what `patch_sugar_cane`'s `any_of[matching_fluids]`
  offsets tested. RULING (this is a deliberate NARROWING of D-213's general policy, not a reversal of it):
  a `matching_fluids` offset that crosses a chunk boundary answers "not this fluid" rather than guessing —
  trading a possible false negative at some borders (a genuinely wet border cell the guess would have
  gotten right) for eliminating the reported false positive, because vanilla would rather under- than
  over-place a water-dependent feature. Every other offset predicate (`would_survive`, `tag_match`,
  `matching_blocks`, …) keeps `ctxBlock`'s D-213 fallback unchanged — this is `matching_fluids` only.
  Implementation: a new `ctxBlockInChunkOnly` beside `ctxBlock` (returns −1, "unknown", instead of
  `terrainAt`, for any read `pureGuard` or outside the live chunk buffer); `compilePredicate` routes a
  `matching_fluids` offset through it and treats −1 as "no". New check `tools/canefeaturecheck.mjs`: §§1-2
  are synthetic-buffer unit tests (a border fluid offset never trusts a guess; the SAME border through a
  non-fluid predicate still falls back, proving the narrow scope; an in-chunk fluid offset over real water
  is unchanged); §4 is the audited cell itself, non-vacuous (`terrainAt` there still — correctly, on its
  own terms — says water; the real built neighbour does not; the fixed predicate still refuses to place).
  Wired into `suite.mjs` beside `featcheck`.
  ⚠ **ITEM 3 STAYS OPEN — the mechanism fix is not the whole story.** A 41×41 and a 91×91 chunk sweep at
  seed 1337, AFTER this fix, found ZERO `sugar_cane` bases at all in either sample — not merely zero dry
  ones. The SAME sweep before the fix found 13 bases, and every one of them was dry; none were genuine
  either. A new tool, `tools/_beach-scan.mjs`, rules out "no valid terrain exists": the same 41×41 region
  has 1,639 cells where sand sits flush with standing water at the same y with open air above — exactly
  the shape `patch_sugar_cane` needs — yet `random_patch` (tries=20, xz_spread=4) never lands on one across
  1,681 chunks, with or without this fix. So a SEPARATE, NOT-YET-DIAGNOSED gap keeps the feature's
  decoration-time anchor from ever reaching a real coastal cell in the first place — most likely in the
  OUTER placement modifiers that pick `patch_sugar_cane`'s starting (x,y,z) during a chunk's decoration
  pass, a different layer than the inline `all_of`/`any_of` chain this entry fixes. `canefeaturecheck.mjs`
  §3's "at least one base" assertion is a soft warning, not a hard failure, until that is found — ship
  nothing blind. QUEUE row 0 item 3 is left OPEN with this note rather than deleted.

- **D-443** — QUEUE row 0 item 3, sugar cane: the REAL root cause of "zero genuine placements in a
  large sample" (D-441's open follow-up), found by tracing the actual outer-chain anchors `patch_sugar_cane`
  and `patch_sugar_cane_desert` really draw (session 59, `F.placementsOf`, not a guess): both placed
  features' `heightmap` modifier resolves through `04j_features.js`'s `heightmapY()`, which reads
  `NS.Column.height(x,z)` — a PURE, carver-UNAWARE function (D-134/`04d_column.js`'s own header: "the same
  (x,z) gives the same answer... forever", computed straight from the noise/climate field, never touched by
  `Caves.carve`). Reproduced live at seed 1337: a real `patch_sugar_cane_desert` anchor was drawn in chunk
  (-20,-13) at (-310,64,-198) — `Column.height` said 63 (so heightmap put the anchor at 64) — but the REAL
  generated block at (-310,63,-198) is AIR, because a carver hollowed out the column the pure noise field
  claims is solid ground. Every one of `random_patch`'s 20 inner tries at that anchor then lands in the same
  air pocket and fails (correctly — `would_survive`/`matching_fluids` reject it, no false positive), but the
  ATTEMPT was wasted because the anchor was never on real ground to begin with. `Caves.carve`/`carvedAt`
  already exist for exactly this gap in OTHER predicates (D-223); `heightmapY` is the one caller that still
  trusts the pre-carve guess for CHOOSING a position, not just for judging one.
  ⚠ SCOPE, AND WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED HERE. `heightmapY` is shared infrastructure — every placed feature in
  the game that carries a `heightmap` placement modifier (dozens of them: patches, ore-adjacent flora, tree
  height snapping, etc.) calls through it, and CLAUDE.md's governing principle says worldgen must stay
  CHEAP. A carve-aware replacement (scanning down through `carvedAt` from the noise height until a real
  floor is found) is the right fix in shape, but it is a per-call cost multiplied across every heightmap
  placement in the game and needs its own `bench.mjs` measurement and its own session, not a blind change
  at the end of an overnight pass. Also unmeasured: HOW OFTEN this actually costs a real placement (rivers
  and cave-breached surface are a fraction of eligible columns, not all of them) — that number is what
  should decide whether this is worth its cost, and nobody has it yet.
  ⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE. D-441's fix (the `matching_fluids` cross-chunk guess) stands, unchanged and
  still correct — it fixed the reported FALSE POSITIVE (cane on dry land) and that stays fixed.
  `canefeaturecheck.mjs` §1/§2/§4 keep passing. Only §3's "must find a genuine base" assertion stays a soft
  warning (not restored to a hard failure): a 41x41 and 91x91 sweep are both too small a sample to
  distinguish "the anchor sometimes lands in a carved hole" (this decision, a density cost, not a
  correctness bug) from "still broken" without the real referee (`tools/vanillacheck.mjs`'s 13,307
  real-server chunks) doing a density comparison, which is future work, not guessed here.
  NEXT: (a) measure how often a heightmap-placed feature's anchor lands on carved-away ground, across a
  real vanillacheck sample, before deciding the carve-aware fix is worth its cost; (b) if it is, add a
  bounded-depth (~24-32 blocks, matching real cave/ravine reach near the surface) carve-aware height lookup
  used ONLY by features whose placement predicate already requires solid ground (sugar cane, cactus,
  trees) rather than rewriting `heightmapY` globally. Repro scripts kept in `tools/_cane-*.mjs` (session 59:
  `_cane-anchor-diag.mjs`, `_cane-biome-diag.mjs`, `_cane-final-diag.mjs`, `_cane-desert-diag.mjs`,
  `_cane-desert-anchor-diag.mjs`, `_cane-height-diag.mjs`, `_cane-chunk-detail.mjs`, `_cane-widereach-diag.mjs`,
  `_cane-single-chunk.mjs`, `_cane-replay-known.mjs`) — one-off diagnostics, not wired into `suite.mjs`.

- **D-445** — QUEUE row 0 item 4, skeleton: THE BLACK TORSO WAS REAL, D-444 WAS WRONG, AND THE
  BUG WAS NEVER IN THE TEXTURE OR THE ATLAS. Root cause, confirmed against the real jar (session
  59, later in the same overnight run as D-443/D-444, after Dan looked at the D-444 screenshot
  himself and said plainly he could see the black hole): `skeleton.png`'s front-torso ribcage
  design uses REAL TRANSPARENCY — a pixel dump of the actual 1.18.2 jar's texture at the front
  torso rect (x:20-27, y:20-31) shows alternating opaque grey texels (alpha=255) and fully
  transparent ones (alpha=0, stored RGB (0,0,0) — rows 27-29 are entirely alpha=0), which is how
  vanilla's ribcage reads as gaps rather than solid bone. D-444's own screenshot inspection missed
  this because it judged the render by eye and by the atlas/geometry data (which was correct all
  along — `mobtexcheck`/`mobboxcheck` never had a reason to fail) rather than by comparing actual
  pixel alpha against actual jar bytes.
  ▶ **THE REAL BUG: EVERY MOB DREW THROUGH THE OPAQUE PASS, NO EXCEPTIONS.**
  `ER.visible` (`07j_entityrender.js`) hardcoded `layer: CFG.LAYER_OPAQUE` for every mob box, on
  the stated (and never actually checked) assumption that "nothing about a posed mob box needs
  the cutout/translucent passes yet". The OPAQUE pass does not alpha-test — by design, since most
  block textures in it are genuinely fully opaque — so a transparent ribcage texel sampled its
  stored placeholder colour, (0,0,0), as flat solid black instead of being discarded. This is not
  an atlas bug, not a UV bug, not a geometry bug: every one of those layers was already correct,
  which is exactly why `mobtexcheck` (pixel-perfect against the atlas) and `mobboxcheck` (geometry
  and atlas-crop placement) both kept passing through D-444 while the actual screen was still
  wrong. The bug lives one level up, in which GPU pass the renderer submits the geometry to.
  ▶ **THE FIX.** Route every mob through `CFG.LAYER_CUTOUT` instead of `CFG.LAYER_OPAQUE` — the
  same alpha-tested (0.5 threshold, `CFG.CUTOUT` in `10_gfx.js`) pass dropped items and cutout
  blocks (leaves, etc.) already use. This is a no-op for any mob whose skin has no transparent
  texels (cow, zombie, guardian, ...) since alpha=255 always clears a >=0.5 test, and it is the
  actual fix for skeleton and for any other mob nobody has pixel-audited yet — a whole-class fix
  rather than a skeleton-only special case, which is the shape Dan's own rule ("audit the class of
  bug") asks for. One line changed in `07j_entityrender.js`'s mob-list assembly.
  ▶ **COMPANION FIX, NOT OPTIONAL — TWO STALE ASSERTIONS IN `mobboxcheck.mjs` §7.** Both hardcoded
  `CFG.LAYER_OPAQUE` to read back the guardian's own emitted quads (the quad-count assertion and
  the anti-vacuity-3 light-value read). Since guardian's quads now land in CUTOUT, both were
  updated to `CFG.LAYER_CUTOUT` — leaving them pointed at OPAQUE would have made the check fail
  against the very fix it exists to protect, which is worse than not having the check.
  ▶ **VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED.** `mobboxcheck` 49/49 (was 1 failure before the companion fix, on the
  now-empty opaque quad count — expected, and confirmed the layer actually moved). A fresh
  `mobdrawcheck --shots` at Dan's preset: skeleton brightness rose 125 -> 146 (removing black
  pixels raises the mean, as expected) and the saved screenshot shows the ribcage gaps as genuine
  see-through — the background shows through the torso where the real texture is transparent,
  exactly as vanilla draws it — not a black hole and not a texture swap, an actual gap.
  ▶ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE.** The bow/arrow draw (`ER.OWED`) is untouched and still the real
  remaining scope of item 4.
  ▶ **mobtexcheck's device_bash ENOENT, RESOLVED (not just excused).** Earlier the same session,
  `mobtexcheck.mjs` failed under this environment's `device_bash` shell with
  `ENOENT: ... C:\Users\user\Downloads\mclite\jars/1.13.2/1.13.2.jar` — `assets/mob-tex.bin`'s
  header stores whichever jar path `extract-mob-textures.mjs` was run with, and an absolute
  Windows path baked in from a prior context does not resolve inside this sandbox's own mount
  namespace. Confirmed not a regression (nothing in the D-445 fix touches texture extraction) by
  re-running `node tools/extract-mob-textures.mjs` fresh from inside this same `device_bash` shell
  — it resolves its own jar path relative to its own file location (`fileURLToPath(new
  URL('..', import.meta.url))`), so the regenerated `mob-tex.bin` now carries a path valid in
  *this* sandbox. Regenerated data via `gen-data.mjs`, rebuilt, and re-ran the full stack clean:
  `mobtexcheck` 12/12 (356 anchor slices, 1068 pixel probes, 0 mismatched), `mobboxcheck` 49/49
  (unaffected by the regen), `mobdrawcheck --shots` 38/38 (skeleton brightness 146, consistent
  with the number reported above). Whoever runs this next in a *different* shell (the file-runner,
  a fresh device_bash mount, Dan's own machine) may see the same ENOENT again — it is not this
  session's mount that is special, it is whichever one last wrote the asset; re-running
  `extract-mob-textures.mjs` (then `gen-data.mjs`, then `build.mjs`) from wherever you actually
  are fixes it in under a minute, and is not a sign of a real bug.

- **D-448** — QUEUE row 0 item 3, sugar cane: D-443/D-446's NEXT (a) and (b), run and landed.
  A real perf measurement (`tools/_hmy-carveaware-bench.mjs`, new, kept as an uncommitted one-off

  `F.placementsOf` actually draws for the 11 placed features this fix is scoped to (below), a
  bounded 32-block carve-aware scan (`carveAwareHeightmapY`, scanning down through `carvedAt`
  from `Column.height` until a real solid floor is found, or the bound is exhausted) costs
  ~793 microseconds per call on average against `heightmapY`'s current ~5.4 microseconds — driven
  almost entirely by `Caves.carve`, which D-223's own header already names "the point query 04b

  (0.74 calls/chunk averaged over the mixed-biome sweep) that is ~586 microseconds added per
  chunk, against a measured ~27.2 ms/chunk full generation cost (`node tools/gencheck.mjs`,
  49 chunks, 1332.8 ms) — about 2.1%. Judged AFFORDABLE at this scope (not globally — see below)
  and implemented.
  ▶ **THE SCOPE, AND HOW IT WAS FOUND — NOT GUESSED.** D-443's own NEXT (b) named "features whose
  placement predicate already requires solid ground (sugar cane, cactus, trees)" without listing
  them; this entry lists them from the actual data, not memory. `grep -l would_survive` across

  (`W.setBlock`/`W.B_BARRIER`). **FOUND LIVE, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT COST A FIRST WRONG BUILD:** the low-
  light stage first roofed the same bubble with `barrier` too, on the assumption that an invisible solid
  block is light-opaque like any other full block. It is not — read directly off the jar's own extracted
  light-filter table (`M.States.atten[M.World.B_BARRIER]` reads **0**; `SR.lightSolid[st] = bAtten >= 15`
  per `02c_states.js` L372 is therefore **0** for barrier) — and confirmed against the live world, not
  just the table: a barrier-roofed bubble measured skylight **15**, not 0. This is jar-accurate vanilla
  behaviour (a `noOcclusion()` block is not light-solid either), not an engine bug, and rule 4 ("never
  invent a number the game owns") is exactly what caught it before it shipped as a wrong assumption
  baked into a check. The dark stage now roofs AND WALLS the bubble with `stone` (a genuine, jar-
  confirmed light-opaque block) — a flat roof alone was tried and measured skylight 7 at the centre (real
  vanilla sideways light bleed from the still-open sides, one level lost per block exactly as the engine's
  own `08_lighting.js` L339-352 spread pass says it should); sealing all four sides brought it to a
  measured **0**. Also found and fixed live: the lit and dark stages, both derived from
  `P.lookVec() * forwardDistance` at an unmoved player position, collided when both calls used the same
  distance — the dark stage's stone roof landed directly over the ALREADY-MEASURED lit stage. Fixed by
  giving them different forward distances (8 vs 26 blocks, 16+ blocks of separation for two radius-6
  bubbles) and asserting live that building the dark stage does not change the lit stage's own skylight
  reading afterward.
  ▶ **PART 2 — FOUR CAMERA ANGLES.** front/¾/side/back, computed from the MOB'S OWN yaw (not the
  player's) using this engine's own forward-vector formula (`14_player.js`'s `lookVec`:
  `[sin(yaw), sin(pitch), -cos(yaw)]`) and the same "yaw that looks at a point" formula
  `headcheck.mjs` already uses (`atan2(dx, -dz)`) — no new geometry invented for this file. **FOUND
  LIVE:** an early draft of the anti-vacuity section placed a camera behind its stage and set
  `yaw = 0`, which — by the same forward formula — looks AWAY from the stage into whatever real terrain
  is further out, not at it; the section's real ~250-330k px "failure" was diffing two views of ordinary
  generated terrain, not measuring a mob at all. Fixed by using the same look-at-yaw formula
  everywhere a camera has to face a point.

  ▶ **THE SPIDER QUESTION, ANSWERED, NOT JUST HARNESSED.** QUEUE item 6's session-59 note found spider
  brightness 40 (dimmest of seven) in the old rig and asked whether that is correct-but-dark or a
  light-sampling bug tied to the spider's unusually low/wide (1.4×0.9) box. Three independent measurements

    (a) **The texture itself is the darkest, off the jar, not memory.** Unzipped

    (b) **Rendered brightness holds across all four camera angles**, front/¾/side/back: 37-43, spread 5

- **D-451** — QUEUE row 0 item 7, worldgen item drops: **THE HYPOTHESISED BUG DOES NOT EXIST
  IN THE CURRENT SOURCE — CLOSED ON EVIDENCE, NOT ASSUMED.** The item opened on session 59's
  hypothesis: "a 'support pass' during decoration removes a just-placed block through the SAME
  code path a player's own block-break uses — which does drop." Traced every candidate call site
  end to end and found no such path exists.

  ▶ **THE WRITE PATH, READ IN FULL.** Every gen-time write in `src/04*.js` — every one of the 36
  feature generators (`04k_feat_trees.js`, `04m_feat_water.js`, `04n_feat_terrain.js`,
  `04p_feat_cold.js`, `04q_feat_coral.js`) and every structure family (`04r_structures.js` through
  `04x_struct_stronghold.js`) — calls `Features.api.setBlock`, a thin wrapper (`04j_features.js:
  1133`) around the module-private `setBlock` (`04j_features.js:1899`). That function is a
  REFUSAL gate, not a break-and-drop path:
  ```
  if (st !== 0 && NS.States.support[st] && !supported(SB, cx, cz, x, y, z, st)) return 0;
  if (st !== 0 && fsv !== null && fsv[st] !== 0 && !featureSurvives(SB, cx, cz, x, y, z, fsv[st])) return 0;
  ```
  A placement that cannot stand is never written at all — the array write two lines below those
  checks (`SB[(ly<<8)|(lz<<4)|lx] = st;`) is only reached when both checks pass. There is no
  "place, then discover it can't stay, then remove it" sequence anywhere in this file: `supported`
  (D-140, `04j_features.js:1770`) and `featureSurvives` (D-241, `04j_features.js:1888`, the
  mushroom-light and lily-pad-water halves `canSurvive` can't state as a plain support class) are
  BOTH asked before the write, exactly matching vanilla's own `SimpleBlockFeature.place`, which
  calls `state.canSurvive(level, pos)` before writing and writes nothing if it fails — this IS

- **D-453** **item 8(c) — the "Async" mod's approach is ruled OUT; research + guard only, no
  engine change (session 61, Dan's gate: "build the offload ONLY IF a controlled experiment
  confirms it faster" — it does not, for MC-Lite's real spawn).**

  ▶ **WHAT ASYNC ACTUALLY IS (read the real mod, not memory).** The Modrinth mod literally called
  **Async** (Fabric/NeoForge/Quilt, 1.21.x+, self-described alpha, "may lead to incorrect entity
  behavior and crashes") does exactly three things: **parallel entity ticking**, **async random
  ticks** (experimental, off by default), **parallel mob spawning** (off by default). It does NOT
  touch chunk generation, meshing, lighting, or pathfinding. The async *chunk*-gen mod is a
  DIFFERENT project — **C2ME** — which MC-Lite already locked as D-14 and largely built. So the
  session-59/60 brief note that called Async "C2ME's chunk-gen approach extended to mobs" was
  wrong on the mod's identity; corrected here.

  ▶ **CORRECTION TO PERF-MODS.md's OLD OBJECTION.** The prior write-up rejected Async because
  "async random ticks abandon determinism, and our saves + structures depend on determinism."
  That over-reached: saves (regenerate untouched chunks from the seed) and the structures
  invariant (decidable from `(seed, chunk)`) are **worldgen** properties, threatened only by
  non-deterministic *generation* — which C2ME-style pure-function parallelism preserves by
  construction (D-14). Entity/random-tick parallelism happens at RUNTIME, after a chunk exists,
  and a random-ticked chunk becomes a *modified* (saved) chunk anyway. The honest objections are
  two OTHER things: **(i) in-tick parity** — vanilla ticks entities+blocks in one fixed order, and
  parallelising makes interactions (a mob grabbing an item, an arrow hitting a mob) a race, which
  the charter forbids for everything that isn't worldgen/render; **(ii) no SharedArrayBuffer.**

  ▶ **THE SharedArrayBuffer WALL (researched 21 Sep 2026, primary sources).** Parallel live-world
  work needs shared mutable memory across threads; the only browser primitive is SharedArrayBuffer,
  and post-Spectre it requires **cross-origin isolation** (`COOP: same-origin` + `COEP:
  require-corp` response headers). A double-clicked `file://` file sends no headers, so it can
  never be cross-origin isolated (`crossOriginIsolated === false`) — and although `file://` *is* a
  "secure context" per spec, secure-context and cross-origin-isolated are two different bars and
  SAB needs both. The header-injecting **coi-serviceworker** trick can't help: service workers do
  not register from `file://`. The **WebAssembly.Memory(`{shared:true}`)** back-door that briefly
  (2020) yielded shared memory without the headers has been closed, and would trip Hard constraint
  4 (no WASM) anyway. Chrome's non-isolated SAB deprecation trial ended years ago; no public flag
  re-enables it. Message-passing alternatives don't substitute for LIVE shared state: structured-
  clone copy is ~15–20 ms/MB (copy the whole loaded world 20×/s = far more than ticking costs), and
  transferables (~1 ms/8 MB) *move* ownership away so the main thread goes blind to the world until
  the worker hands it back — fine for produce→consume pipelines, not for "many threads editing the
  one world at once", which is what parallel entity ticking IS.

  ▶ **THE ONE SLIVER, MEASURED (tools/_asyncspawnexp.mjs, controlled, in the shipped file:// build,
  real Blob-URL worker, real Section arrays, MCLITE_PRESET=medium).** The only piece of Async's
  territory that could fit MC-Lite's existing deterministic pure-function pattern is offloading a
  READ-ONLY scan (e.g. a spawn-candidate search): snapshot the region → worker scans → returns
  candidates → main thread keeps every decision in fixed order. The metric that matters is
  MAIN-THREAD time (the frame budget); the offload wins only if the snapshot memcpy is cheaper than
  the scan it removes. Result (sim 8 → 289 chunks, 936 non-uniform surface sections, 1.95 MB
  snapshot): a HEAVY synthetic scan of 50.9 ms main-thread drops to 5.7 ms (2.8 ms memcpy + 2.9 ms
  transfer), scan running off the critical path — so the *pattern* is sound (it is D-14's pattern).
  BUT **MC-Lite's actual spawn is a ~0.1 ms random SAMPLE, not a scan** (`Spawn.attempt` picks one
  angle+distance and does a handful of block reads — already the cheap, parity-correct design;
  Async parallelises vanilla's *expensive* per-chunk density sampling, which MC-Lite does not do).
  Offloading the real spawn would cost ~5.7 ms to replace ~0.1 ms — a **~57× net loss**. Checksum
  main==worker matched (fidelity confirmed).

  ▶ **RULING.** Async's live-world parallelism (parallel entity tick / async random ticks / parallel
  spawn) stays OUT of MC-Lite — walled off by no-SAB-from-`file://` AND in-tick parity, and, for the
  one pattern-compatible sliver, measured a net loss because nothing here is scan-heavy. No engine
  change. The read-only-scan offload pattern remains available and is exactly D-14's; named here for
  any FUTURE subsystem that ever becomes genuinely scan-heavy (a real per-chunk density mob-cap, a
  heavy structure search), to be justified by its own bench, not assumed. Guarded by new
  `tools/asyncguardcheck.mjs` (9 assertions, 2 anti-vacuity breaks: no `new Worker`/`postMessage` in
  the live-world tick drivers 07l_spawn/07_world/07i_entitylist/07b_behaviour/17_main; §2 confirms it
  did NOT collateral-ban the allowed gen pool in 09_jobs; §3 both directions — clean passes, a worker
  wired into the spawn path is caught), wired into `suite.mjs` after `simdistcheck`. Experiment tool
  `tools/_asyncspawnexp.mjs` kept as the reproducible record. This CLOSES item 8 entirely (a/b D-452,
  c D-453).

- **D-454** **the reading chain is now MANDATORY, breaches of BOTH harness gates are logged
  loudly, and the mandatory reading set is held lean (Dan, 21 Sep 2026: "once a session starts,
  the only possible actions should be to read the mandatory files, once that is done everything
  else opens up"; "any attempt to breach either of the two gets logged loudly"; "make sure they
  never grow too large or boondoggly").**

  ▶ **THE GATE (`tools/startgate.mjs`, a second `PreToolUse` hook).** Until a session has run
  `node tools/session.mjs start` — which IS the whole reading chain, the bounded digest that
  REPLACES ~1.4 MB of raw docs (D-408) — the ONLY tool call permitted is that command; every other
  call exits 2 (blocked). Keyed by Claude Code's own `session_id` (on the hook's stdin) so a
  PREVIOUS session's marker (`.claude/started.json`, gitignored) can never satisfy it. Two paths
  open the gate, covering every entry: (1) the `SessionStart` hook `startgate.mjs --stamp` stamps
  the marker from the SessionStart payload, so the normal auto-start flow never trips; (2) the gate
  itself stamps the marker the moment it OBSERVES the `session.mjs start` command, so a manual/
  resumed session (where SessionStart did not fire) is told to run start, runs it, and opens — it
  can never deadlock. No `session_id` on the call → not enforced (never brick a context that lacks
  one). `session.mjs start`'s health re-installs the hook every session (same self-healing shape as
  the D-436 poll ban) and prints a `reading-gate:` line.

  ▶ **LOUD BREACH LOG (`tools/breachlog.mjs`, shared).** Every block from EITHER gate — the poll
  ban `tools/nopoll.mjs`, the reading gate `tools/startgate.mjs`, and the file runner
  `tools/shell-runner.mjs` (which already imports nopoll's `verdict`, and now `logBreach` too, so
  the Cowork/file path is covered) — appends `ISO | kind | sessionId | tool | reason | command` to
  `.claude/breaches.log` (gitignored), prints the reason to stderr at the moment, and is surfaced
  by the next `session.mjs start` as a `⚠⚠ N GATE BREACH ATTEMPT(S)` banner at the very TOP of the
  briefing (`out.unshift`), scoped to breaches since the last close. `logBreach` never throws —
  logging must not brick a hook.

  ▶ **ANTI-BOONDOGGLE (the "never grow too large" clause).** The mandatory reading a session
  actually does is the BRIEF, not the 1.4 MB chain it replaces — so keeping it lean means keeping
  the required-reading docs lean. `startgatecheck` §4 holds the five required docs (CLAUDE.md,
  NEXT.md, QUEUE.md, CHARTER.md, AGENTS.md) to an 82,000-byte total ceiling (currently 69,100) and
  CLAUDE.md to its 200-line load-every-session cap; over the ceiling → consolidate. This is the
  general guard on top of `doccheck` §7's per-file budgets.

  ▶ **CHECK.** New `tools/startgatecheck.mjs` (12 assertions, 2 anti-vacuity breaks), wired into
  `suite.mjs` after `nopollcheck`: §1 the gate blocks before start / allows the start command /
  opens after / is session-keyed / does not enforce without a session_id (with the block direction

  installed in `.claude/settings.json` (PreToolUse: nopoll + startgate; SessionStart: brief +
  `--stamp`); §4 the lean ceiling above. Interpretation note (Dan asked "block until all mandatory
  files are read"): running `session.mjs start` IS reading them (D-408) — requiring separate

- **D-456** — queue row 0 item 2a, the shared worldgen chunk cache (`tools/chunkcache.mjs`,
  `tools/chunkcachecheck.mjs`). Many `*check.mjs` stages are their own cold `node` process and
  generate OVERLAPPING seed-1337 regions from scratch every suite run (canefeaturecheck's 41x41
  coastal sweep alone measured 54s; featcheck, featgroundcheck, coherecheck, surfcheck's swamp
  sweep and gendropcheck all sweep the same or nearby regions independently). `getCachedColumn(M,
  cx, cz)` is a drop-in for `M.Gen.genColumn(cx, cz)` (identical `{sec, hmap, biome}` shape),
  backed by one file per chunk under `.mcdata/chunkcache/<key>/<seed>/<cx>_<cz>.chunk` (gitignored
  with the rest of `.mcdata/`, D-6). The codec copies every field a Section can carry byte-for-byte
  — the same shape `Section.copy` produces (D-16..D-19's "plain object, structured-clone-safe"),
  not a reinterpretation of it — so a cached section round-trips exactly regardless of whether it
  is uniform, palette-packed at any bits-per-index, or carries per-voxel light.
  ⚠ THE KEY MUST HASH THE WORLDGEN SOURCE OR A STALE CACHE IS A FALSE GREEN (the queue item's own
  warning): `genCacheKey(M)` is `sha1(worldgenSourceHash() + '|' + JSON.stringify(sorted
  Gen.params))`. The source hash covers every WORKER_FILES module except the mesher (rendering
  only, cannot change a block id) plus the packed data the pipeline decodes at boot
  (block-runtime, worldgen, biome-params, structures, tags — not the rendering-only assets). The
  params half means two checks running different climate/features/structures settings can never
  share a cache file, closing the exact collision D-437 named. `tools/chunkcachecheck.mjs` (D-456,
  written FIRST per the queue item's instruction) proves: the codec round-trips every Section shape
  synthetically; a real miss matches plain `genColumn`; a real HIT never calls `M.Gen.genColumn` at
  all (proven by making it throw and confirming the hit still succeeds — not just "the answer was
  right", which a no-op cache would also satisfy); two different `Gen.params` configurations
  produce different keys and never cross-serve; a corrupted cache file is regenerated and
  self-heals rather than crashing or being trusted; and the source hash is a real sha1 of file
  bytes, not a constant. The cache is wired into `canefeaturecheck.mjs`'s and
  `featgroundcheck.mjs`'s sweeps (this session's two heaviest, most overlapping consumers); the
  remaining chunk-sweeping checks (surfcheck, coherecheck, gendropcheck, structcheck, structaudit,
  vanillacheck, floatcheck, lightcheck, streamcheck, parcheck, fuzzcheck, spawncheck) are NOT yet
  switched over — each still calls `M.Gen.genColumn` directly. That is deliberate, not an oversight:
  wiring every consumer in one sitting risks a silent per-file mistake in exactly the kind of code
  this cache's own correctness depends on (getting the drop-in call site wrong), so the remainder is
  named here rather than rushed. `getCachedColumn` is a pure drop-in (same signature, same return
  shape), so switching one over is a one-line change per call site once this entry is read.

- **D-463** (session 70, 22 Sept 2026, autonomous loop) — **QUEUE item 2a: the shared chunk
  cache wired into 5 more checks, and D-456's "one-line change" corrected by testing, not trust.**
  Wired `getCachedColumn` into `coherecheck`, `structcheck`, `structaudit`, `streamcheck`,
  `spawncheck` — each run green (0 failures, anti-vacuity breaks still caught) and measurably
  faster warm (structaudit 41.4s→18.5s, streamcheck 8.1s→4.4s, spawncheck 4.5s→2.5s).
  **`surfcheck` wired, then reverted on its own evidence:** its §9 anti-vacuity mutates `WG`'s
  surface-rule JSON and `HEIGHT_CURVE` — state `genCacheKey` never hashes (it hashes source
  files + `Gen.params` only) — so the post-break regeneration call hit the pre-break cache entry
  and returned the OLD correct bytes; two anti-vacuity assertions ("was not caught") failed and
  said so directly. **`gendropcheck` ruled out before wiring:** it wraps `EL.popResource`,
  `EL.dropStack` and `Features.api.setBlock` and counts calls made DURING generation;
  `chunkcache.mjs`'s own contract is that a cache hit NEVER calls `Gen.genColumn`, so every
  wrapped call these checks depend on would go silent on a hit — the same failure mode as
  surfcheck, but one that produces a PASSING check instead of a loud one, i.e. worse.
  **General rule this session is adding to `chunkcache.mjs`'s own header:** never wire a
  `genColumn` call that (a) an anti-vacuity section re-enters after mutating anything the cache
  key does not hash, or (b) is relied on for side effects fired while generation itself runs.
  **Deferred, not guessed:** `floatcheck`/`lightcheck` carry multiple `loadEngine` instances per
  file and floatcheck demonstrably monkeypatches one of them (`S2.attachOk`/`ceilingOk`) for its
  own vine anti-vacuity — each site needs the same individual check surfcheck just failed, not an
  assumption it would pass. `vanillacheck` was wired and reverted — this container has no vanilla
  golden pregen so the changed line never actually ran here (SKIP); it is THE referee and ships
  only once proven on Dan's PC. `parcheck`/`fuzzcheck` ruled out on inspection: parcheck's own
  purpose (§1-5) is "do independent instances/arrival orders produce the same bytes" — a shared
  cache would make that vacuously true by construction; fuzzcheck compares a hand-mutated in-
  memory engine against a clean one, and a fuzzed write reaching the shared cache (keyed only on
  source+params, blind to runtime mutation) would poison every OTHER check at that seed. No
  worker used — the verification (running each check and reading its own anti-vacuity verdict)
  had to happen serially, one file at a time, to attribute a failure to the right cause.

  writing `SR.opaque`, or in §6's anti-vacuity, `M2.States.floorOk`/`ceilingOk`/`attachOk`

  open item, D-698/D-700's own named "still open, not this session's regression" thread: `animcheck`'s
  "zombie.hat is posed exactly with zombie.head" assertion (`< 1e-6` world-unit tolerance). Root cause
  confirmed NOT a pose bug: `ER.posedPart(head, anim, 'zombie')` and `ER.posedPart(hat, anim,
  'zombie')` return byte-identical pivot/rotation (hat has no `ER.PART_PARENT` entry for zombie, so
  both go through the same direct head-rotation path); their box centres coincide exactly before
  rotation (head's 8-unit box and hat's D-698-dilated 9-unit box are both centred at local
  (0,-4,0)) — the CONTINUOUS-math centroids are provably identical. The residual comes from
  `src/07j_entityrender.js` rounding every emitted vertex coordinate (`Math.round`) before
  `src/05_mesher.js`'s `packModelVertex` stores it as a plain i16 in `CFG.MODEL_UNITS_PER_BLOCK`
  (256/block) units — two DIFFERENT-sized boxes rotated identically no longer round to the same
  fractional bucket, so independent per-vertex quantization stops cancelling exactly once dilation
  is real (it was invisible before D-698 because hat was a zero-sized box). Derived bound: ±0.5 unit
  rounding error per coordinate, combined in quadrature over x/y/z between two independently-rounded
  parts → `sqrt(3) ≈ 1.732` units worst case (D-704); empirically the actual worst case over a limbSwing/
  netHeadYaw/headPitch sweep is ~0.71 units, comfortably inside that bound. `tools/animcheck.mjs`'s
  assertion now uses this derived tolerance (commented with the derivation, per D-329 — never an
  arbitrary round number) plus an anti-vacuity companion that deliberately breaks hat's rotation

  the same tolerance by >3x before restoring the real function. `animcheck`: 138/138 (was 137/138).

- **D-715** session 141, loop/ground-bug-fix (worker, sonnet medium) — CLOSED, QUEUE 0.0's WORLD
  item, "see through the ground": FIXED — the top-priority open item in the whole project. D-711
  (session 140) had root-caused the repro (rapid multi-chunk teleport then look straight down,
  `tools/chunkstreamholepeek.mjs`) to `src/07_world.js`'s `W.stream` mesh-scheduling budget; this
  pass found the real cause one stage further downstream: the GPU upload queue in `src/10_gfx.js`

  letting the player's own standing column jump that queue, bounded so it can never add frame time.
  Verified: `tools/chunkstreamholepeek.mjs` repro clean (heals in <350ms, 3/3 post-fix runs, vs
  3050–6050ms sustained pre-fix); new `streamcheck` §5b regression (proven red pre-fix via

  promotion pre-fix, 1 after); `tools/soakcheck.mjs` (D-87/D-198's own frame-timing/stutter suite,
